units.translation: Even if an injunction is admitted, this is not a novel injunction. He says:

units.label: Verse 1.88
units.deva: नियमः परिसंख्या वा विध्यर्थोऽपि भवेद्यतः । अनात्मादर्शनेनैव परात्मानमुपास्महे ॥ ८८॥
units.iast: niyamaḥ parisaṃkhyā vā vidhyartho'pi bhavedyataḥ | anātmādarśanenaiva parātmānamupāsmahe || 88||
units.translation: If an injunction is accepted, its force may be restriction or exclusion; we contemplate the Supreme Self precisely by not attending to the not-Self.

units.label: Text 283
units.deva: यच्चोक्तं "विश्वासो नान्यतोऽस्ति नः" इति -- तदपि निद्रातुरचेतसा त्वया स्वप्नायमानेन प्रलपितम् । किं कारणम् । न हि वयं प्रमाणबलेनैकात्म्यं प्रतिपद्यामह ऐकात्म्यस्य स्वत एवानुभवमात्रात्मकत्वात् । अत एव सर्वप्रमाणावतारासंभवं वक्ष्यति ।
units.iast: yaccoktaṃ "viśvāso nānyato'sti naḥ" iti -- tadapi nidrāturacetasā tvayā svapnāyamānena pralapitam | kiṃ kāraṇam | na hi vayaṃ pramāṇabalenaikātmyaṃ pratipadyāmaha aikātmyasya svata evānubhavamātrātmakatvāt | ata eva sarvapramāṇāvatārāsaṃbhavaṃ vakṣyati |
units.translation: What you said—“we trust no other source”—was also a dreamlike utterance from a mind drowsy with ignorance. Why? We do not arrive at non-duality through the force of a means of knowledge; oneness is itself nothing but direct experience. For this very reason he will show that no means of knowledge can operate [on what is already self-evident].

units.label: Text 284
units.translation: For the ordering of the means of knowledge itself rests on direct experience.

units.label: Text 285
units.translation: Therefore he says:

units.label: Verse 1.89
units.deva: वाक्यैकगम्यं यद्वस्तु नान्यस्मात्तत्र विश्वसेत् । नाप्रमेये स्वतस्सिद्धेऽविश्वासः कथमात्मनि ॥ ८९॥
units.iast: vākyaikagamyaṃ yadvastu nānyasmāttatra viśvaset | nāprameye svatassiddhe'viśvāsaḥ kathamātmani || 89||
units.translation: When a thing is knowable only through a sentence, one should rely on no other source about it. But how could one distrust the Self, which is self-established and not an object of knowledge?

gloss.en: in what cannot be an object of knowledge

units.label: Text 288
units.translation: As for what you said—“without an injunction”—

units.label: Text 289
units.translation: that too seems to us to have been said without due thought.

units.label: Text 290
units.translation: Such reasoning applies to actions whose fruits come at a later time.

units.label: Text 291
units.translation: It is not fitting for knowledge of the Self, whose fruit is given at the very moment the Self is attained. He says:

units.label: Verse 1.90
units.deva: ज्ञानात्फले ह्यवाप्तेऽस्मिन्प्रत्यक्षे भवघातिनि । उपकाराय तन्नेति न न्याय्यं भाति नो वचः ॥ ९०॥
units.iast: jñānātphale hyavāpte'sminpratyakṣe bhavaghātini | upakārāya tanneti na nyāyyaṃ bhāti no vacaḥ || 90||
units.translation: When knowledge has attained its immediate fruit, destroying worldly becoming, our statement that it is of no benefit is unreasonable.

units.label: Text 294
units.deva: यदपि जैमिनीयं वचनमुद्घाटयसि -- तदपि तद्विवक्षापरिज्ञानादेवोद्भाव्यते । किं कारणम् । यतो न जैमिनेरयमभिप्राय आम्नायः । सर्व एव क्रियार्थ इति ।
units.iast: yadapi jaiminīyaṃ vacanamudghāṭayasi -- tadapi tadvivakṣāparijñānādevodbhāvyate | kiṃ kāraṇam | yato na jaiminerayamabhiprāya āmnāyaḥ | sarva eva kriyārtha iti |
units.translation: You cite the words of Jaimini, but their intended meaning must first be understood. Jaimini did not mean that the Veda is concerned only with action; for if he had, he would not have composed the profound inquiry into the meaning of all Vedānta, the Śārīraka Sūtras, which reveal the true nature of Brahman alone.

units.label: Text 295
units.translation: “Then, therefore, the inquiry into Brahman”;

units.label: Text 296
units.deva: जन्माद्यस्य यतः " इत्येवमादिब्रह्मवस्तुस्वरूपमात्रयाथात्म्यप्रकाशनपरं गम्भीरन्यायसंदृब्धं सर्ववेदान्तार्थमीमांसनं श्रीमच्छारीरकं नासूत्रयिष्यत् । असूत्रयच्च ।
units.iast: janmādyasya yataḥ " ityevamādibrahmavastusvarūpamātrayāthātmyaprakāśanaparaṃ gambhīranyāyasaṃdṛbdhaṃ sarvavedāntārthamīmāṃsanaṃ śrīmacchārīrakaṃ nāsūtrayiṣyat | asūtrayacca |
units.translation: “that from which the origin and the rest [of the universe proceed]”—and the other sūtras: he did compose them.

units.label: Text 297
units.deva: तस्माज्जैमिनेरेवायमभिप्रायो यथैव विधिवाक्यानां स्वार्थमात्रे प्रामाण्यमेवमैकात्म्यवाक्यानामप्यनधिगत वस्तुपरिच्छेदसाम्यादिति । अत इदमभिधीयते ।
units.iast: tasmājjaiminerevāyamabhiprāyo yathaiva vidhivākyānāṃ svārthamātre prāmāṇyamevamaikātmyavākyānāmapyanadhigata vastuparicchedasāmyāditi | ata idamabhidhīyate |
units.translation: Jaimini’s own view is that, just as injunctions are authoritative regarding their own subject, so too are sentences about non-duality, since they disclose a thing not previously known. Hence it is said:

units.label: Verse 1.91
units.deva: अधिचोदनं य आम्नायस्तस्यैव स्यात्क्रियार्थता । तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यानां ब्रूत कर्मार्थता कथम् ॥ ९१॥
units.iast: adhicodanaṃ ya āmnāyastasyaiva syātkriyārthatā | tattvamasyādivākyānāṃ brūta karmārthatā katham || 91||
units.translation: The Veda that deals with injunctions may be directed toward action. Explain how sentences beginning with “That thou art” could be directed toward action.

units.label: Text 300
units.deva: अपि च । ऐकात्म्यपक्ष इवादृष्टार्थकर्मसु भवत्पक्षेऽपि प्रवृत्तिर्दुर्लक्ष्या । यतः ।
units.iast: api ca | aikātmyapakṣa ivādṛṣṭārthakarmasu bhavatpakṣe'pi pravṛttirdurlakṣyā | yataḥ |
units.translation: Moreover, even on your view, action toward unseen results is difficult to explain, just as it is on the view of non-duality. For:

units.label: Verse 1.92
units.deva: स्वर्गं यियासुर्जुहुयादग्निहोत्रं यथाविधि । देहाद्व्युत्थापितस्यैवं कर्तृत्वं जैमिनेः कथम् ॥ ९२॥
units.iast: svargaṃ yiyāsurjuhuyādagnihotraṃ yathāvidhi | dehādvyutthāpitasyaivaṃ kartṛtvaṃ jaimineḥ katham || 92||
units.translation: One who wishes to reach heaven should duly perform the Agnihotra. But if, as Jaimini holds, the Self is set apart from the body, how can it be an agent?

units.label: Text 303
units.translation: The Self alone, whose nature excludes the body and every instrument of action, is not eligible for ritual action. Why?

units.label: Verse 1.93
units.translation: Jaimini’s Self cannot be reached through the usual means of knowledge and is known only through the sense of “I.” Since it does not take up the object “you,” how could it be prompted to act?

gloss.en: not reached by any means of knowledge

units.label: Text 306
units.translation: There is no cause that could prompt it to act. For:

units.label: Verse 1.94
units.deva: सुखदुःखादिभिर्योग आत्मनो नाहमेक्ष्यते । पराक्त्वात्प्रत्यगात्मत्वाज्जैमिनिः प्रेर्यते कथम् ॥ ९४॥
units.iast: sukhaduḥkhādibhiryoga ātmano nāhamekṣyate | parāktvātpratyagātmatvājjaiminiḥ preryate katham || 94||
units.translation: The Self is not seen as joined with pleasure, pain, and the like; these are outward, while the Self is inward. How could Jaimini’s Self be prompted to act?

gloss.en: with pleasure, pain, and the like
because it is the inward Self

units.label: Text 309
units.translation: Further:

units.label: Verse 1.95
units.deva: न तावद्योग एवास्ति शरीरेणात्मनः सदा । विषयैर्दूरतो नास्ति स्वर्गादौ स्यात्कथं सुखम् ॥ ९५॥
units.iast: na tāvadyoga evāsti śarīreṇātmanaḥ sadā | viṣayairdūrato nāsti svargādau syātkathaṃ sukham || 95||
units.translation: The Self is never connected with the body, far less with sense-objects. How could there be pleasure in heaven and the like?

units.label: Text 312
units.translation: Since that would make no sense otherwise,

units.label: Verse 1.96
units.deva: नराभिमानिनं तस्मात्कारकाद्यात्मदर्शिनम् । मन्त्र आहोररीकृत्य “कुर्वन्” इति न निर्द्वयम् ॥ ९६॥
units.iast: narābhimāninaṃ tasmātkārakādyātmadarśinam | mantra āhorarīkṛtya "kurvan" iti na nirdvayam || 96||
units.translation: By saying “performing,” the mantra addresses one who identifies as a person and sees the factors of action as the Self; it does not speak of the non-dual Self.

gloss.en: one who identifies as a person
one who sees the factors of action and the rest as the Self

units.label: Text 315
units.deva: यच्चोक्तं "विरहय्य " इति तदपि न सम्यगेव । तथापि तु न या काचित्क्रिया यत्र क्व चाध्याहरणीया किं तु या यत्राभिप्रेतसंबन्धं घटयितुं शक्नोत्याकाङ्क्षां च वाक्यस्य पूरयति सैवाध्याहरणीया । एवंविशिष्टा च क्रियास्माभिरभ्युपगतैव । सा तूपादित्सितवाक्यार्था विरोधिन्येव नाभूतार्थप्रादुर्भावफलेति ।
units.iast: yaccoktaṃ "virahayya " iti tadapi na samyageva | tathāpi tu na yā kācitkriyā yatra kva cādhyāharaṇīyā kiṃ tu yā yatrābhipretasaṃbandhaṃ ghaṭayituṃ śaknotyākāṅkṣāṃ ca vākyasya pūrayati saivādhyāharaṇīyā | evaṃviśiṣṭā ca kriyāsmābhirabhyupagataiva | sā tūpāditsitavākyārthā virodhinyeva nābhūtārthaprādurbhāvaphaleti |
units.translation: What you said—“sentences do not combine without an action-word”—is not quite correct. Not just any action-word may be supplied wherever one pleases. Only the verb that can establish the intended relation and complete the sentence’s expectation may be supplied, and we accept that. But in sentences whose intended meaning is knowledge, such a verb would conflict with their purpose, which is not to produce something that did not exist.

units.label: Text 316
units.translation: Since the Self is free from the six modifications, free from every ill born of duality, self-luminous, and independent, the verb “am” in a sentence such as “I am” must be understood as conveying the reality already established in its own glory, not as conveying a contrary meaning.

units.label: Verse 1.97
units.deva: धावेदिति न दानार्थे पदं यद्वत्प्रयुज्यते । एधीत्यादि तथा नेच्छेत्स्वतः सिद्धार्थवाचिनि ॥ ९७॥
units.iast: dhāvediti na dānārthe padaṃ yadvatprayujyate | edhītyādi tathā necchetsvataḥ siddhārthavācini || 97||
units.translation: Just as the word “may run” is not used to mean “may give,” one should not import a command to become into words that describe what is already established in itself.

gloss.en: in a word expressing what is self-established

units.label: Text 319
units.deva: न च यथोक्तवस्तुवृत्तप्रतिपादनव्यतिरेकेण तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यं वाक्यार्थान्तरं वक्तीति शक्यमध्यवसातुमित्याह ।
units.iast: na ca yathoktavastuvṛttapratipādanavyatirekeṇa tattvamasyādivākyaṃ vākyārthāntaraṃ vaktīti śakyamadhyavasātumityāha |
units.translation: Nor can it be concluded that sentences such as “That thou art” express a meaning other than the reality of things as stated. He says:

units.label: Verse 1.98
units.deva: तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यानां स्वतस्सिद्धार्थबोधनात् । अर्थान्तरं न संद्रष्टुं शक्यते त्रिदशैरपि ॥ ९८॥
units.iast: tattvamasyādivākyānāṃ svatassiddhārthabodhanāt | arthāntaraṃ na saṃdraṣṭuṃ śakyate tridaśairapi || 98||
units.translation: Since sentences beginning with “That thou art” reveal a meaning that is already self-established, not even the gods can discover another meaning in them.

gloss.en: because they reveal a self-established meaning

units.label: Text 322
units.translation: Since this is so,

units.label: Verse 1.99
units.deva: अतः सर्वाश्रमाणां तु वाङ्मनःकायकर्मभिः । स्वनुष्ठितैर्न मुक्तिः स्याज्ज्ञानादेव हि सा यतः ॥ ९९॥
units.iast: ataḥ sarvāśramāṇāṃ tu vāṅmanaḥkāyakarmabhiḥ | svanuṣṭhitairna muktiḥ syājjñānādeva hi sā yataḥ || 99||
units.translation: Therefore, even actions of speech, mind, and body, when well performed by people in every stage of life, do not bring liberation; for liberation comes through knowledge alone.

gloss.en: for people in every stage of life
through actions of speech, mind, and body

units.label: Text 325
units.translation: For this reason, the following too is well said:

units.label: Verse 1.100
units.translation: Therefore, for those whose minds are puffed up with ideas of their own making, these words suit ritual scholars, but not those who know the Self.

gloss.en: for those whose minds are puffed up by ideas of their own making
among those who know the Self

units.label: Chapter colophon
units.translation: Thus ends the first chapter.

units.label: Chapter heading
units.translation: Now begins the second chapter.

units.label: Text 2
units.translation: Perception and the other ordinary means of knowledge do not take the Self as their object; they operate only on the objects that give rise to them. The Self is unlike every knowable object. Therefore only words such as “That thou art,” which clearly reveal things as they are, bring about the rising of the sun of knowledge that removes ignorance, the cause of every ill. This has been shown through many arguments.

units.label: Text 3
units.translation: The second chapter now begins to remove the obstacle that prevents understanding the meaning of that sentence.

units.label: Verse 2.1
units.translation: If someone who has heard “That thou art” does not understand the sentence’s meaning, it is because the meaning of “thou” is not understood; that meaning is therefore explained.

units.label: Text 6
units.deva: योऽयमहंब्रह्मेति वाक्यार्थस्तत्प्रतिपत्तिर्वाक्यादेवेति प्रत्यक्षादीनामनेवंविषयत्वादित्यवादिषं तस्य विशुद्ध्यर्थमनैकात्त्रिकत्वं पूर्वपक्षत्वेनोपस्थाप्यते ।
units.iast: yo'yamahaṃbrahmeti vākyārthastatpratipattirvākyādeveti pratyakṣādīnāmanevaṃviṣayatvādityavādiṣaṃ tasya viśuddhyarthamanaikāttrikatvaṃ pūrvapakṣatvenopasthāpyate |
units.translation: I said that the meaning of the sentence “I am Brahman” is known from the sentence alone, since perception and the other means of knowledge cannot know it. To clarify that point, the opponent’s claim that the reasoning is inconclusive is introduced:

units.label: Verse 2.2
units.deva: कृत्स्नानात्मनिवृत्तौ च कश्चिदाप्नोति निर्वृतिम् । श्रुतवाक्यस्मृतेश्चान्यः स्मार्यते च वचोऽपरः ॥ २॥
units.iast: kṛtsnānātmanivṛttau ca kaścidāpnoti nirvṛtim | śrutavākyasmṛteścānyaḥ smāryate ca vaco'paraḥ || 2||
units.translation: One person reaches peace when the whole not-Self falls away; another recalls a sentence previously heard, and a third is reminded by someone else’s words.

gloss.en: when the whole not-Self has fallen away
from memory of a sentence heard

units.label: Text 9
units.translation: To show that another listener is possible in either case, he says:

units.label: Verse 2.3
units.deva: वाक्यश्रवणमात्राच्च पिशाचकवदाप्नुयात् । त्रिषु यादृच्छिकी सिद्धिः स्मार्यमाणे तु निश्चिता ॥ ३॥
units.iast: vākyaśravaṇamātrācca piśācakavadāpnuyāt | triṣu yādṛcchikī siddhiḥ smāryamāṇe tu niścitā || 3||
units.translation: Someone may reach the meaning merely by hearing the sentence, like a goblin; among these three, success is accidental, while it is certain for the person who is reminded.

units.label: Text 12
units.translation: This reason is not inconclusive, because:

units.label: Verse 2.4
units.deva: सर्वोऽयं महिमा ज्ञेयो वाक्यस्यैव यथोदितः । वाक्यार्थं न ह्यृते वाक्यात्कश्चिज्जानाति तत्त्वतः ॥ ४॥
units.iast: sarvo'yaṃ mahimā jñeyo vākyasyaiva yathoditaḥ | vākyārthaṃ na hyṛte vākyātkaścijjānāti tattvataḥ || 4||
units.translation: All this power belongs to the sentence alone, as stated: no one truly knows the sentence’s meaning apart from the sentence.

units.label: Text 15
units.deva: वाक्यं च प्रतिपादनाय प्रवृत्तं सत्प्रतिपादयत्येव सर्वप्रमाणानामप्येवंवृत्तत्वात् ।
units.iast: vākyaṃ ca pratipādanāya pravṛttaṃ satpratipādayatyeva sarvapramāṇānāmapyevaṃvṛttatvāt |
units.translation: A sentence, when used to explain, does indeed explain an existing thing; all means of knowledge function in this way.

units.label: Verse 2.5
units.deva: नाहंग्राह्ये न तद्धीने न प्रत्यङ्नापि दुःखिनि । विरोधः सदसीत्यस्माद्वाक्याभिज्ञस्य जायते ॥ ५॥
units.iast: nāhaṃgrāhye na taddhīne na pratyaṅ nāpi duḥkhini | virodhaḥ sadasītyasmādvākyābhijñasya jāyate || 5||
units.translation: For someone who understands “That thou art,” the text does not conflict with what is grasped as “I,” what depends on that “I,” the inward Self, or the sufferer.

gloss.en: for one who understands the sentence

units.label: Verse 2.6
units.deva: नाविरक्तस्य संसारान्निविवृत्सा ततो भवेत् । न चानिवृत्ततृष्णस्य पुरुषस्य मुमुक्षुता ॥ ६॥
units.iast: nāviraktasya saṃsārānnivivṛtsā tato bhavet | na cānivṛttatṛṣṇasya puruṣasya mumukṣutā || 6||
units.translation: A person who is not dispassionate toward saṃsāra cannot wish to withdraw from it; nor can someone whose thirst for objects remains become a seeker of liberation.

gloss.en: for one who is not dispassionate
for one whose thirst has not ceased

units.label: Verse 2.7
units.deva: न चामुमुक्षोरस्तीह गुरुपादोपसर्पणम् । न विना गुरुसंबन्धं वाक्यस्य श्रवणं भवेत् ॥ ७॥
units.iast: na cāmumukṣorastīha gurupādopasarpaṇam | na vinā gurusaṃbandhaṃ vākyasya śravaṇaṃ bhavet || 7||
units.translation: One who does not seek liberation does not approach a teacher; and without a relationship with a teacher, there can be no hearing of the sentence.

gloss.en: for one who does not seek liberation

units.label: Verse 2.8
units.deva: तथा पदपदाथौ च न स्तो वाक्यमृते क्वचित् । अन्वयव्यतिरेकौ च तावृते स्तां कैमाश्रयौ ॥ ८॥
units.iast: tathā padapadāthau ca na sto vākyamṛte kvacit | anvayavyatirekau ca tāvṛte stāṃ kaimāśrayau || 8||
units.translation: Words and their meanings do not stand apart from a sentence; without them, what could provide a basis for agreement and exclusion?

units.label: Verse 2.9
units.deva: अन्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यां विना वाक्यार्थबोधनम् । न स्यात्तेन विनाज्ञानप्रहाणं नोपपद्यते ॥ ९॥
units.iast: anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ vinā vākyārthabodhanam | na syāttena vinājñānaprahāṇaṃ nopapadyate || 9||
units.translation: Without agreement and exclusion, the meaning of a sentence would not be understood; without that understanding, the removal of ignorance is impossible.

gloss.en: understanding the meaning of a sentence

units.label: Verse 2.10
units.deva: विनाज्ञानप्रहाणेन पुरुषार्थः सुदुर्लभः । तस्माद्यथोक्तसिद्ध्यर्थं परो ग्रन्थोऽवतार्यते ॥ १०॥
units.iast: vinājñānaprahāṇena puruṣārthaḥ sudurlabhaḥ | tasmādyathoktasiddhyarthaṃ paro grantho'vatāryate || 10||
units.translation: Without removing ignorance, the human goal is exceedingly difficult to attain; therefore, the next section is introduced to establish the realization just described.

gloss.en: to establish the realization just described

units.label: Verse 2.11
units.deva: वर्चस्कं त्वन्नकार्यत्वाद्यथा नात्मेति गम्यते । तद्भागः सेन्द्रियो देहस्तद्वत्किमिति नेक्ष्यते ॥ ११॥
units.iast: varcaskaṃ tvannakāryatvādyathā nātmeti gamyate | tadbhāgaḥ sendriyo dehastadvatkimiti nekṣyate || 11||
units.translation: Excrement is understood as not-Self because it is produced from food. The body, with its sense-organs, is likewise part of that food; why is it not seen the same way?

gloss.en: because it is produced from food

units.label: Text 30
units.translation: When the beginning and end are known to be not-Self, what prevents the middle from being seen as not-Self too?

units.label: Verse 2.12
units.translation: Food is manifestly not-Self before it is eaten, yet through ignorance it seems to become the Self. Therefore the discerning person should see the body as distinct, like a garland or ointment.

units.label: Text 33
units.deva: अथैवमपि मद्वचनं नाद्रियसे स्वयमेवैतस्माच्छरीराद् अशुचिराशेर्निराशो भविष्यसि ।
units.iast: athaivamapi madvacanaṃ nādriyase svayamevaitasmāccharīrād aśucirāśernirāśo bhaviṣyasi |
units.translation: Even if you do not heed my words, you will become disenchanted with this body yourself, since it is a heap of impurities.

units.label: Verse 2.13
units.deva: मन्यसे तावदस्मीति यावदस्मान्न नीयसे । श्वभिः क्रोडीकृते देहे नैवं त्वमभिमंस्यसे ॥ १३॥
units.iast: manyase tāvadasmīti yāvadasmānna nīyase | śvabhiḥ kroḍīkṛte dehe naivaṃ tvamabhimaṃsyase || 13||
units.translation: You think “I am this” only as long as you have not been separated from the body; when dogs have seized it, you will no longer think “I am this.”

units.label: Verse 2.14
units.deva: शिर आक्रम्य पादेन भर्त्सयत्यपरान् शुनः । दृष्ट्वा साधारणं देहं कस्मात्सक्तोऽसि तत्र भोः ॥ १४॥
units.iast: śira ākramya pādena bhartsayatyaparān śunaḥ | dṛṣṭvā sādhāraṇaṃ dehaṃ kasmātsakto'si tatra bhoḥ || 14||
units.translation: One dog steps on the body’s head and snarls at the other dogs. Seeing that the body is common to all, why are you attached to it, friend?

units.label: Text 38
units.translation: The point delivered by scripture—that from the intellect down to the body all is not-Self—is stated:

units.label: Verse 2.15
units.translation: Just as one seed separates into husk, grain, and straw, so food is present in the forms of intellect, flesh, and excrement.

gloss.en: in the parts called husk, grain, and straw
in the parts called intellect, flesh, and excrement

units.label: Text 41
units.deva: यथोक्तार्थप्रतिपत्तौ सत्यां न रागद्वेषाभ्यां विक्रियते विपश्चिदित्यस्यार्थस्य प्रतिपत्तये दृष्टान्तः ।
units.iast: yathoktārthapratipattau satyāṃ na rāgadveṣābhyāṃ vikriyate vipaścidityasyārthasya pratipattaye dṛṣṭāntaḥ |
units.translation: An example is given to show that once this point is understood, the discerning person is not altered by attachment or aversion:

units.label: Verse 2.16
units.deva: वर्चस्के संपरित्यक्ते दोषतश्चावधारिते । यदि दोषं वदेत्तस्मै किं तत्रोच्चरितुर्भवेत् ॥ १६॥
units.iast: varcaske saṃparityakte doṣataścāvadhārite | yadi doṣaṃ vadettasmai kiṃ tatroccariturbhavet || 16||
units.translation: When excrement has been discarded and recognized as impure, what fault is there in someone who says it is impure?

gloss.en: for the one who utters it

units.label: Verse 2.17
units.deva: तद्वत्सूक्ष्मे तथा स्थूले देहे त्यक्ते विवेकतः । यदि दोषं वदेत्ताभ्यां किं तत्र विदुषो भवेत् ॥ १७॥
units.iast: tadvatsūkṣme tathā sthūle dehe tyakte vivekataḥ | yadi doṣaṃ vadettābhyāṃ kiṃ tatra viduṣo bhavet || 17||
units.translation: Likewise, when the subtle and gross bodies have been discarded through discernment, what fault in them could affect the knower?

units.label: Text 46
units.deva: एतावदेव ह्यहं ब्रह्मास्मीति वाक्यार्थाप्रतिपत्तौ कारणं यदुत बुद्ध्यादौ देहान्ते ह्यहंममेति निस्सन्धिबन्धनो ग्रहः ।
units.iast: etāvadeva hyahaṃ brahmāsmīti vākyārthāpratipattau kāraṇaṃ yaduta buddhyādau dehānte hyahaṃmameti nissandhibandhano grahaḥ |
units.translation: The only obstacle to understanding the sentence “I am Brahman” is the unbroken grasp “I” and “mine” in the intellect and the rest, extending to the body.

units.label: Text 47
units.deva: तद्व्यतिरेके हि न कुतश्चिद्विभज्यत एकल एव प्रत्यगात्मन्यवतिष्ठत इत्याह ।
units.iast: tadvyatireke hi na kutaścidvibhajyata ekala eva pratyagātmanyavatiṣṭhata ityāha |
units.translation: When one is separated from all that, one remains alone in the inward Self, indivisible from anything else. This is stated:

units.label: Verse 2.18
units.deva: रिपौ बन्धौ स्वदेहे च समैकात्म्यं प्रपश्यतः । विवेकिनः कुतः कोपः स्वदेहावयवेश्विव ॥ १८॥
units.iast: ripau bandhau svadehe ca samaikātmyaṃ prapaśyataḥ | vivekinaḥ kutaḥ kopaḥ svadehāvayaveśviva || 18||
units.translation: For the discerning person who sees the same Self in an enemy, a relative, and one’s own body, how could anger arise, any more than toward one’s own limbs?

gloss.en: toward the parts of one’s own body

units.label: Text 50
units.translation: The body and the rest are not-Self for another reason too:

units.label: Verse 2.19
units.deva: घटादिवच्च दृश्यत्वात्तैरेव करणैर्दृशेः । स्वप्ने चानन्वयाज्ज्ञयो देहोऽनात्मेति सूरिभिः ॥ १९॥
units.iast: ghaṭādivacca dṛśyatvāttaireva karaṇairdṛśeḥ | svapne cānanvayājjñayo deho'nātmeti sūribhiḥ || 19||
units.translation: The wise know the body is not-Self because it is an object, like a pot, to those same senses, and because body-consciousness is not continuous in dreams.

gloss.en: like a pot and the like
because it is seen; an object

units.label: Text 53
units.translation: Those who examine whether the body, its effects, and its instruments are connected or disconnected directly observe effects that contradict one another.

units.label: Verse 2.20
units.translation: The body that four bearers lift with all their strength becomes light as cotton to a fool who identifies it as “I.”

units.label: Text 56
units.translation: To conclude the subject, which is already well known, he says:

units.label: Verse 2.21
units.deva: स्थूलं युक्त्या निरस्यैवं नभसो नीलतामिव । देहं सूक्ष्मं निराकुर्यादतो युक्तिभिरात्मनः ॥ २१॥
units.iast: sthūlaṃ yuktyā nirasyaivaṃ nabhaso nīlatāmiva | dehaṃ sūkṣmaṃ nirākuryādato yuktibhirātmanaḥ || 21||
units.translation: Having reasoned that the gross body is no more the Self than blueness belongs to the sky, one should likewise reject the subtle body as the Self through reasoning.

units.label: Text 59
units.translation: How is the subtle body rejected? It is explained:

units.label: Verse 2.22
units.translation: The senses of “I” and “mine,” effort, and desire are not properties of the Self, just as leanness is not; they are known as objects and pass away, like a garment.

units.label: Text 62
units.translation: An example of difference is given:

units.label: Verse 2.23
units.deva: नोष्णिमानं दहत्यग्निः स्वरूपत्वाद्यथा ज्वलन् । तथैवात्मात्मनो विद्यादहं नैवाविशेषतः ॥ २३॥
units.iast: noṣṇimānaṃ dahatyagniḥ svarūpatvādyathā jvalan | tathaivātmātmano vidyādahaṃ naivāviśeṣataḥ || 23||
units.translation: Just as blazing fire does not burn its own heat because heat is its nature, one should likewise know the “I” as not distinct from the Self.

gloss.en: because it is its own nature

units.label: Text 65
units.deva: एकस्यात्मनः कर्मकर्तृभावः सर्वथा नोपपद्यत इति श्रुत्वा मीमांसकः प्रत्यवतिष्ठते । अहंप्रत्ययग्राह्यत्वाद्ग्राहक आत्मेति तन्निवृत्त्यर्थमाह ।
units.iast: ekasyātmanaḥ karmakartṛbhāvaḥ sarvathā nopapadyata iti śrutvā mīmāṃsakaḥ pratyavatiṣṭhate | ahaṃpratyayagrāhyatvādgrāhaka ātmeti tannivṛttyarthamāha |
units.translation: After hearing that one and the same Self cannot be both agent and object of action, the Mīmāṃsaka objects: “The Self is the knower because it is grasped by the cognition ‘I.’” To remove this view, he says:

units.label: Verse 2.24
units.deva: यत्कर्मको हि यो भावो नासौ तत्कर्तृको यतः । घटप्रत्ययवत्तस्मान्नाहं स्याद्द्रष्टृकर्मकः ॥ २४॥
units.iast: yatkarmako hi yo bhāvo nāsau tatkartṛko yataḥ | ghaṭapratyayavattasmānnāhaṃ syāddraṣṭṛkarmakaḥ || 24||
units.translation: Whatever is the object of an action is not its agent. Therefore the “I” cannot be an object of the seer, just as a pot is the object of the thought “pot.”

units.label: Text 68
units.deva: अत्राह प्रत्यक्षेणात्मनः कर्मकर्तृत्वाभ्युपगमेतत्पादोपजीविनानुमानेन प्रत्यक्षोत्सारणमयुक्तमिति चोद्यं तन्निराकरणाय प्रत्यक्षोपन्यासः ।
units.iast: atrāha pratyakṣeṇātmanaḥ karmakartṛtvābhyupagametatpādopajīvinānumānena pratyakṣotsāraṇamayuktamiti codyaṃ tannirākaraṇāya pratyakṣopanyāsaḥ |
units.translation: An objection is raised: “Direct perception accepts that the Self is both agent and object. It is wrong to use an inference that depends on perception to set perception aside.” Direct perception is now cited to answer it.

units.label: Verse 2.25
units.deva: यत्र यो दृश्यते द्रष्ट्रा तस्यैवासौ गुणो न तु । द्रष्टृस्थं दृश्यतां यस्मान्नैवेयाद्द्रष्टृबोधवत् ॥ २५॥
units.iast: yatra yo dṛśyate draṣṭrā tasyaivāsau guṇo na tu | draṣṭṛsthaṃ dṛśyatāṃ yasmānnaiveyāddraṣṭṛbodhavat || 25||
units.translation: What is seen by a seer is a quality of the thing seen, not of the seer. What belongs to the seer cannot itself become an object of sight, just as the seer’s awareness cannot.

units.label: Text 71
units.deva: प्रत्यक्षेणैव भवदभिमतस्य प्रत्यक्षस्याभासीकृतत्वात् सुस्थमेवानुमानम् । अतस्तदेव प्रक्रियते तत्र च विकल्पदूषणाभिधानम् ।
units.iast: pratyakṣeṇaiva bhavadabhimatasya pratyakṣasyābhāsīkṛtatvāt susthamevānumānam | atastadeva prakriyate tatra ca vikalpadūṣaṇābhidhānam |
units.translation: Since direct perception itself has shown that your supposed perception is illusory, the inference stands firm. He now states the inference and its alternatives.

units.label: Verse 2.26
units.deva: नात्मना न तदंशेन गुणः स्वस्थोऽवगम्यते । अभिन्नत्वात्समत्वाच्च निरंशत्वादकर्मतः ॥ २६॥
units.iast: nātmanā na tadaṃśena guṇaḥ svastho'vagamyate | abhinnatvātsamatvācca niraṃśatvādakarmataḥ || 26||
units.translation: A quality is not known to inhere in the Self either through the Self itself or through a part of it, because the Self is non-different, homogeneous, partless, and not an object.

gloss.en: because it is not an object

units.label: Text 74
units.deva: न युगपन्नपि क्रमेणोभयथा चैकस्य धर्मिणो ग्राह्यग्राहकत्वमुपपद्यत इति प्रतिपादनायाह ।
units.iast: na yugapannapi krameṇobhayathā caikasya dharmiṇo grāhyagrāhakatvamupapadyata iti pratipādanāyāha |
units.translation: To show that the same substance cannot be both the knower and the known, either simultaneously or in sequence, he says:

units.label: Verse 2.27
units.deva: द्रष्टृत्वेनोपयुक्तत्वात्तदैव स्यान्न दृश्यता । कालान्तरे चेद्दृश्यत्वं न ह्यद्रष्टृकमिष्यते ॥ २७॥
units.iast: draṣṭṛtvenopayuktatvāttadaiva syānna dṛśyatā | kālāntare ceddṛśyatvaṃ na hyadraṣṭṛkamiṣyate || 27||
units.translation: When engaged as the seer, it cannot at that same time be seen. If it were seen at another time, that would not be accepted, since a seen thing without a seer is not admitted.

gloss.en: because it is engaged in that role

units.label: Text 77
units.deva: सन्तु काममनात्मधर्मा ममत्वादयो यथोक्तन्यायबलादनात्मतयैव च तेषु व्यवहारादहंरूपस्य तु प्रत्यगात्मसंबन्धितयैव प्रसिद्धेरहंब्रह्मास्मीति श्रुतेश्चानात्मधर्मत्वमयुक्तमिति चेत्तन्न ।
units.iast: santu kāmamanātmadharmā mamatvādayo yathoktanyāyabalādanātmatayaiva ca teṣu vyavahārādahaṃrūpasya tu pratyagātmasaṃbandhitayaiva prasiddherahaṃbrahmāsmīti śruteścānātmadharmatvamayuktamiti cettanna |
units.translation: One might object: “Let ‘mine’ and desire be properties of the not-Self, as reason shows; ordinary usage confirms that. But ‘I’ is known only in relation to the inward Self, and the revelation ‘I am Brahman’ shows that it cannot belong to the not-Self.” This is not so.

units.label: Verse 2.28
units.deva: अहंधर्मस्त्वभिन्नश्चेदहंब्रह्मेति वाक्यतः । गौरोऽहमित्यनैकान्तो वाक्यं तद्व्यपनेतृ तत् ॥ २८॥
units.iast: ahaṃdharmastvabhinnaścedahaṃbrahmeti vākyataḥ | gauro'hamityanaikānto vākyaṃ tadvyapanetṛ tat || 28||
units.translation: If the ego-“I” were non-different [from the Self] because of the sentence “I am Brahman,” that would be inconclusive: the sentence “I am fair” can be cancelled.

units.label: Text 80
units.translation: How does that sentence remove the error? The answer is:

units.label: Verse 2.29
units.deva: योऽयं स्थाणुः पुमानेष पुंधिया स्थाणुधीरिव । ब्रह्मास्मीतिधियाशेषा ह्यहंबुद्धिर्निवर्त्यते ॥ २९॥
units.iast: yo'yaṃ sthāṇuḥ pumāneṣa puṃdhiyā sthāṇudhīriva | brahmāsmītidhiyāśeṣā hyahaṃbuddhirnivartyate || 29||
units.translation: Just as recognizing “post” cancels the mistaken thought “person” about a post, the understanding “I am Brahman” removes the whole ego-thought.

units.label: Text 83
units.deva: अहंपरिच्छेदव्यावृत्तौ न किंचिदव्यावृत्तं द्वैतजातमवशिष्यते द्वितीयसंबन्धस्य तन्मूलत्वात् । अत आह ।
units.iast: ahaṃparicchedavyāvṛttau na kiṃcidavyāvṛttaṃ dvaitajātamavaśiṣyate dvitīyasaṃbandhasya tanmūlatvāt | ata āha |
units.translation: When the limited notion “I” is removed, no duality remains; the relation to a second thing has that notion as its root. Therefore he says:

units.label: Verse 2.30
units.deva: निवृत्तायामहंबुद्धौ ममधीः प्रविलीयते । अहंबीजा हि सा सिद्ध्येत्तमोऽभावे कुतः फणी ॥ ३०॥
units.iast: nivṛttāyāmahaṃbuddhau mamadhīḥ pravilīyate | ahaṃbījā hi sā siddhyettamo'bhāve kutaḥ phaṇī || 30||
units.translation: When the “I”-thought has ceased, the “mine”-thought dissolves; for it is rooted in the “I.” Without darkness, where could a snake appear?

units.label: Text 86
units.translation: The example is explained to show the point intended:

units.label: Verse 2.31
units.deva: तमोऽभिभूतचित्तो हि रज्ज्वां पश्यति रोषणम् । भ्रान्त्या भ्रान्त्या विना तस्मान्नोरगं स्रजि वीक्षते ॥ ३१॥
units.iast: tamo'bhibhūtacitto hi rajjvāṃ paśyati roṣaṇam | bhrāntyā bhrāntyā vinā tasmānnoragaṃ sraji vīkṣate || 31||
units.translation: A mind overcome by darkness sees something frightening—a false snake—in a rope through error; therefore, without error, one does not see a snake in a garland.

gloss.en: whose mind is overcome by darkness

units.label: Text 89
units.translation: The ego is not a property of the Self because it is not continuous with it.

units.label: Verse 2.32
units.deva: आत्मनश्चेदहंधर्मो यायान्मुक्तिसुषुप्तयोः । यतो नान्वेति तेनायमन्यदीयो भवेदहम् ॥ ३२॥
units.iast: ātmanaścedahaṃdharmo yāyānmuktisuṣuptayoḥ | yato nānveti tenāyamanyadīyo bhavedaham || 32||
units.translation: If “I”-ness were a property of the Self, it would persist in liberation and deep sleep. Since it does not persist there, this “I” belongs to something else.

units.label: Text 92
units.translation: If ego is accepted as a property of the Self, an unavoidable defect follows:

units.label: Verse 2.33
units.deva: यद्यात्मधर्मोऽहङ्कारो नित्यत्वं तस्य बोधवत् । नित्यत्वे मोक्षशास्त्राणां वैयर्थं प्राप्नुयाद् ध्रुवम् ॥३३॥
units.iast: yadyātmadharmo'haṅkāro nityatvaṃ tasya bodhavat | nityatve mokṣaśāstrāṇāṃ vaiyarthaṃ prāpnuyād dhruvam ||33||
units.translation: If ego-sense were a property of the Self, it would be permanent like awareness; if it were permanent, the scriptures on liberation would surely be useless.

units.label: Text 95
units.translation: One might answer that ego is a natural property [of the Self], like the fruit of a mango. That is not so.

units.label: Verse 2.34
units.deva: आम्रादेः परिणामित्वाद्गुणहानिर्गुणान्तरैः । अविकारि तु तद्ब्रह्म "न हि द्रष्टुरि"तिश्रुतेः ॥ ३४॥
units.iast: āmrādeḥ pariṇāmitvādguṇahānirguṇāntaraiḥ | avikāri tu tadbrahma "na hi draṣṭuri"tiśruteḥ || 34||
units.translation: A mango changes, losing one quality as other qualities arise. Brahman, however, is changeless, as scripture says that the seer’s seeing does not cease.

gloss.en: of a mango and the like

units.label: Text 98
units.translation: Since ego arises and passes away, the Self that bears it would also be impermanent.

units.label: Verse 2.35
units.translation: If awareness rested on what comes and goes, it too would be impermanent; a property that arises and passes away does indeed transform its bearer.

units.label: Text 101
units.translation: One might say, “Let it be impermanent; why object, since it is established by a means of knowledge?” That is not so.

units.label: Verse 2.36
units.deva: सदाविलुप्तसाक्षित्वं स्वतस्सिद्धं न पार्यते । अपह्नोतुं घटस्येव कुशाग्रीयधियात्मनः ॥ ३६॥
units.iast: sadāviluptasākṣitvaṃ svatassiddhaṃ na pāryate | apahnotuṃ ghaṭasyeva kuśāgrīyadhiyātmanaḥ || 36||
units.translation: The Self’s ever-unbroken witnessing is self-established and cannot be denied, even by the sharpest intellect, just as one cannot deny a plainly seen pot.

gloss.en: the state of being an uninterrupted witness
by an intellect sharp as a kusa-grass tip

units.label: Text 104
units.translation: For this reason, understand that ego is not a property of the Self.

units.label: Verse 2.37
units.deva: प्रमाणैश्चावगम्यत्वाद्घटादिवदहंदृशेः । यतो ऋद्धिः प्रमाणानां स कथं तैः प्रसिध्यति ॥ ३७॥
units.iast: pramāṇaiścāvagamyatvādghaṭādivadahaṃdṛśeḥ | yato ṛddhiḥ pramāṇānāṃ sa kathaṃ taiḥ prasidhyati || 37||
units.translation: The ego-cognition is known through means of knowledge, like a pot. But because the Self is what makes those means effective, how could it be established by them?

gloss.en: like a pot and other things

units.label: Text 107
units.translation: Moreover, the property and its bearer have opposed natures, so their relation is impossible.

units.label: Verse 2.38
units.deva: धर्मिणश्च विरुद्धत्वान्न दृश्यगुणसङ्गतिः । मारुतान्दोलितज्वालं शैत्यं नाग्निं सिसृप्सति ॥ ३८॥
units.iast: dharmiṇaśca viruddhatvānna dṛśyaguṇasaṅgatiḥ | mārutāndolitajvālaṃ śaityaṃ nāgniṃ sisṛpsati || 38||
units.translation: Because a property and its bearer have opposed natures, an observed quality cannot belong to its bearer: cold does not enter a fire whose flame is tossed by the wind.

gloss.en: whose flame is tossed by the wind

units.label: Text 110
units.translation: Therefore accept this without hesitation:

units.label: Verse 2.39
units.deva: द्रष्टृत्वं दृश्यता चैव नैकस्मिन्नेकदा क्वचित् । दृश्यदृश्यो न च द्रष्टा द्रष्टुर्दर्शी दृशिर्न च ॥३९॥
units.iast: draṣṭṛtvaṃ dṛśyatā caiva naikasminnekadā kvacit | dṛśyadṛśyo na ca draṣṭā draṣṭurdarśī dṛśirna ca ||39||
units.translation: Seerhood and being seen never occur in one thing at the same time. The seen thing is not the seer; the seer is not an object for what is seen, and seeing itself does not see the seer.

gloss.en: the seen thing; what is seen

units.label: Text 113
units.translation: If this were otherwise, all ordinary dealings would collapse. For:

units.label: Verse 2.40
units.deva: द्रष्टापि यदि दृश्याया आत्मेयात्कर्मतां धियः । यौगपद्यमदृश्यत्वं वैयर्थ्यं चाप्नुयाच्छृतिः ॥ ४०॥
units.iast: draṣṭāpi yadi dṛśyāyā ātmeyātkarmatāṃ dhiyaḥ | yaugapadyamadṛśyatvaṃ vaiyarthyaṃ cāpnuyācchṛtiḥ || 40||
units.translation: If the seer, the Self, became an object of the intellect, which is itself seen, scripture would have to affirm both objecthood and non-objecthood at once and would be pointless.

gloss.en: the state of being an object

units.label: Text 116
units.translation: Why? Because:

units.label: Verse 2.41
units.deva: नालुप्तदृष्टेर्दृश्यत्वं दृश्यत्वे द्रष्टृता कुतः । स्याच्चेद्दृगेकं निर्दृश्यं जगद्वा स्यादसाक्षिकम् ॥ ४१॥
units.iast: nāluptadṛṣṭerdṛśyatvaṃ dṛśyatve draṣṭṛtā kutaḥ | syācceddṛgekaṃ nirdṛśyaṃ jagadvā syādasākṣikam || 41||
units.translation: The uninterrupted Seer cannot be an object; if it were seen, how could it remain the seer? If sight alone became an object, either it would be the only unseen thing or the world would have no witness.

units.label: Text 119
units.translation: A scriptural example is introduced to strengthen the argument:

units.label: Verse 2.42
units.deva: आर्तमन्यद्दृशेः सर्वं "नेति नेती"ति चासकृत् । वदन्ती निर्गुणं ब्रह्म कथं श्रुतिरुपेक्ष्यते ॥ ४२॥
units.iast: ārtamanyaddṛśeḥ sarvaṃ "neti netī"ti cāsakṛt | vadantī nirguṇaṃ brahma kathaṃ śrutirupekṣyate || 42||
units.translation: Everything other than the Seer is subject to distress; scripture repeatedly says “not this, not this” and declares Brahman to be without qualities. How could scripture be ignored?

units.label: Verse 2.43
units.translation: The great elements and ego are called the “field.” Even according to the Lord of the Universe’s teaching, the Seer has no relation to duality.

units.label: Text 124
units.translation: The subject is now brought to a close.

units.label: Verse 2.44
units.deva: एवमेतद्धिरुग्ज्ञेयं मिथ्यासिद्धमनात्मकम् । मोहमूलं सुदुर्बोधं द्वैतं युक्तिभिरात्मनः ॥ ४४॥
units.iast: evametaddhirugjñeyaṃ mithyāsiddhamanātmakam | mohamūlaṃ sudurbodhaṃ dvaitaṃ yuktibhirātmanaḥ || 44||
units.translation: Thus duality is to be understood as distinct from the Self: it is falsely established, not-Self, rooted in delusion, and very hard to grasp by reasoning.

units.label: Text 127
units.translation: If one asks how duality is falsely established,

units.label: Verse 2.45
units.translation: No separate reality apart from the Self can be established. Therefore ego and the rest are imagined in the Self as though they were the Self.

units.label: Text 130
units.translation: This is thus an expansion of ignorance.

units.label: Verse 2.46
units.deva: दृश्याः शब्दादयः क्लृप्ता द्रष्टृ च ब्रह्म निर्गुणम् । अहं तदुभयं बिभ्रद्भ्रान्तिमात्मनि यच्छति ॥४६॥
units.iast: dṛśyāḥ śabdādayaḥ klṛptā draṣṭṛ ca brahma nirguṇam | ahaṃ tadubhayaṃ bibhradbhrāntimātmani yacchati ||46||
units.translation: Objects such as sound are imagined; the Seer is qualityless Brahman. The ego, taking up both roles, casts delusion upon the Self.

units.label: Text 133
units.translation: It is for this very reason that difference is imagined in the undivided Self.

units.label: Verse 2.47
units.deva: दृगेका सर्वभूतेषु भाति दृश्यैरनेकवत् । जलभाजनभेदेन मयूखस्रग्विभेदवत् ॥ ४७॥
units.iast: dṛgekā sarvabhūteṣu bhāti dṛśyairanekavat | jalabhājanabhedena mayūkhasragvibhedavat || 47||
units.translation: The Seer is one and shines in all beings, yet appears many through the things seen, like a single garland of sunrays seeming divided among separate water vessels.

gloss.en: because of differences among water vessels
like the apparent division of a garland of rays

units.label: Text 136
units.translation: An example is given to help understand the point:

units.label: Verse 2.48
units.translation: Friend, neutral, and enemy are roles one person is given through another’s imagining; likewise, differences in undivided consciousness depend on the inner instrument.

units.label: Verse 2.49
units.deva: अपहारो यथा भानोः सर्वतो जलपात्रकैः । तत्क्रियाकृतिदेशाप्तिस्तथा बुद्धिभिरात्मनः ॥ ४९॥
units.iast: apahāro yathā bhānoḥ sarvato jalapātrakaiḥ | tatkriyākṛtideśāptistathā buddhibhirātmanaḥ || 49||
units.translation: Just as the sun is appropriated by many water vessels and made to seem to take on their actions, forms, and locations, so the intellects appropriate the Self in the same way.

units.label: Text 141
units.translation: Contradictory qualities cannot really abide in one thing;

units.label: Verse 2.50
units.translation: Since imagined things are unreal, conflicting qualities may appear together, as the same woman may seem desirable, impure, or delicious.

units.label: Text 144
units.deva: न चायं क्रियाकारकफलात्मक आभास ईषदपि परमार्थवस्तु स्पृशति तस्य मोहमात्रोपादानत्वात् ।
units.iast: na cāyaṃ kriyākārakaphalātmaka ābhāsa īṣadapi paramārthavastu spṛśati tasya mohamātropādānatvāt |
units.translation: This appearance of action, agent, and result does not touch reality even slightly, since it is caused only by delusion.

units.label: Verse 2.51
units.deva: अभूताभिनिवेशेन स्वात्मानं वञ्चयत्ययम् । असत्यपि द्वितीयेऽर्थे सोमशर्मपिता यथा ॥ ५१॥
units.iast: abhūtābhiniveśena svātmānaṃ vañcayatyayam | asatyapi dvitīye'rthe somaśarmapitā yathā || 51||
units.translation: Through attachment to what is unreal, a person deceives himself, like Somaśarman’s father, even though no second thing exists.

gloss.en: through fixation on what is unreal

units.label: Text 147
units.translation: His eyes are veiled by ignorance of things as they truly are;

units.label: Verse 2.52
units.deva: सुभ्रूः सुनासा सुमुखी सुनेत्रा चारुहासिनी । कल्पनामात्रसंमोहाद्रामेत्यालिङ्गतेऽशुचिम् ॥ ५२॥
units.iast: subhrūḥ sunāsā sumukhī sunetrā cāruhāsinī | kalpanāmātrasaṃmohādrāmetyāliṅgate'śucim || 52||
units.translation: Imagining her as fine-browed, lovely-nosed, beautiful-faced, bright-eyed, and smiling, he embraces the impure woman as “Rāmā,” deluded by imagination alone.

units.label: Text 150
units.deva: सर्वस्यानर्थजातस्य जिहासितस्य मूलमहंकार एव तस्यात्मनात्मोपरागात् । न तु परमार्थत आत्मनोऽविद्यया तत्कार्येण वा संबधोऽभूदस्ति भविष्यति वा तस्यापरिलिप्तदृष्टिस्वाभाव्यात् ।
units.iast: sarvasyānarthajātasya jihāsitasya mūlamahaṃkāra eva tasyātmanātmoparāgāt | na tu paramārthata ātmano'vidyayā tatkāryeṇa vā saṃbadho'bhūdasti bhaviṣyati vā tasyāpariliptadṛṣṭisvābhāvyāt |
units.translation: The ego is the root of every kind of misery to be abandoned, because it colors the Self with itself. In truth, the Self has never been, is not, and will never be connected with ignorance or its effects, since vision is by nature unstained.

units.label: Verse 2.53
units.deva: दृश्यानुरक्तं तद्द्रष्टृ दृश्यं द्रष्ट्रनुरञ्जितम् । अहंवृत्त्योहयं रक्तं तन्नाशेऽद्वैततात्मनः ॥ ५३॥
units.iast: dṛśyānuraktaṃ taddraṣṭṛ dṛśyaṃ draṣṭranurañjitam | ahaṃvṛttyohayaṃ raktaṃ tannāśe'dvaitatātmanaḥ || 53||
units.translation: The seer is colored by what is seen, and what is seen is colored by the seer; the ego-thought colors them both. When it ceases, the Self is non-dual.

units.label: Text 153
units.deva: इह केचिच्चोदयन्ति योऽयमन्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यामनात्मतयोत्सारितोऽहंकारो वाक्यार्थप्रतिपत्तये सोऽयं विपरीतार्थः संवृत्तो यस्मादहं ब्रह्मास्मीति ब्रह्माहंपदार्थयोः सामानाधिकरण्यश्रवणादनात्मार्थेन सामानाधिकरण्यं प्राप्नोति । वक्तव्या च प्रत्यगात्मनि तस्य वृत्तिरिति सोच्यते प्रसिद्धलक्षणागुणवृत्तिभिः ।
units.iast: iha keciccodayanti yo'yamanvayavyatirekābhyāmanātmatayotsārito'haṃkāro vākyārthapratipattaye so'yaṃ viparītārthaḥ saṃvṛtto yasmādahaṃ brahmāsmīti brahmāhaṃpadārthayoḥ sāmānādhikaraṇyaśravaṇādanātmārthena sāmānādhikaraṇyaṃ prāpnoti | vaktavyā ca pratyagātmani tasya vṛttiriti socyate prasiddhalakṣaṇāguṇavṛttibhiḥ |
units.translation: Some object: “The ego, which was rejected as not-Self through agreement and exclusion, has now been brought in with the opposite meaning. When the identity ‘I am Brahman’ is heard, the words ‘I’ and ‘Brahman’ are placed in apposition, so ‘I’ must refer to the not-Self. Its use for the inward Self must still be explained.” The answer is given through common, indirect, and figurative usage.

units.label: Verse 2.54
units.deva: नाज्ञासिषमिति प्राह सुषुप्तादुत्थितोऽपि हि । अयोदाहादिवत्तेन लक्षणं परमात्मनः ॥ ५४॥
units.iast: nājñāsiṣamiti prāha suṣuptādutthito'pi hi | ayodāhādivattena lakṣaṇaṃ paramātmanaḥ || 54||
units.translation: One who has risen from deep sleep says, “I knew nothing.” That “I” indirectly indicates the Supreme Self, as when one says that iron burns.

gloss.en: as in the case of iron burning and the like

units.label: Verse 2.55
units.translation: Because the Self is inward, exceedingly subtle, and the focus of sustained inquiry, it is indicated through the “I”-thought after the other mental modes are set aside.

gloss.en: because of sustained attention to the Self

units.label: Verse 2.56
units.deva: आत्मना चाविनाभावमथवा विलयं व्रजेत् । न तु पक्षान्तरं यायादतश्चाहंधियोच्यते ॥ ५६॥
units.iast: ātmanā cāvinābhāvamathavā vilayaṃ vrajet | na tu pakṣāntaraṃ yāyādataścāhaṃdhiyocyate || 56||
units.translation: The ego-thought either remains inseparable from the Self or dissolves into it; it has no third possibility. Therefore the Self may also be referred to through the “I”-thought.

units.label: Text 160
units.translation: What sort of thing is the reality being indicated?

units.label: Verse 2.57
units.deva: नामादिभ्यः परो भूमा निष्कलोऽकारकोऽक्रियः । स एवात्मवतामात्मा स्वतस्सिद्धः स एव नः ॥ ५७॥
units.iast: nāmādibhyaḥ paro bhūmā niṣkalo'kārako'kriyaḥ | sa evātmavatāmātmā svatassiddhaḥ sa eva naḥ || 57||
units.translation: Beyond names and the rest is the Infinite: partless, not an agent, and actionless. That alone is the Self of the Self-realized, self-established; that is the Self we teach.

units.label: Text 163
units.deva: अज्ञानोत्थबुद्ध्यादिकर्तृत्वोपाधिमात्मानं परिगृह्यैवान्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यामहं सुखी दुःखी चेत्यहंकारादेरनात्मधर्मत्वमुक्तं केवलात्माभ्युपगमेऽशक्यत्वात्फलाभावाच्च ।
units.translation: The “I” and the rest were said to be properties of the not-Self by agreement and exclusion, because one takes the Self to be qualified by agency and other conditions that arise from ignorance. The pure Self alone cannot be “happy” or “sad,” and accepting it as such would bring no result.

units.label: Text 164
units.translation: Now, relying on the witnessing status imagined through ignorance, he refutes every change, agency, and other modification:

units.label: Verse 2.58
units.translation: The Self, the one unbroken witness, beholds the dance of all minds; without itself acting, it sees what is constant and what changes, as if through a blink.

gloss.en: while not acting as a looker

units.label: Text 167
units.deva: ननु सर्वसिद्धान्तानामपि स्वस्वदृष्ट्यपेक्षयोपपन्नत्वादितरेतरदृष्ट्यपेक्षया दुस्स्थितसिद्धिकत्वान्नैकत्रापि विश्वासं पश्यामो न च सर्वतार्किकैरदूषितं समर्थितं सर्वतार्किकोपद्रवापसर्पणाय वर्त्म संभावयामः ।
units.iast: nanu sarvasiddhāntānāmapi svasvadṛṣṭyapekṣayopapannatvāditaretaradṛṣṭyapekṣayā dussthitasiddhikatvānnaikatrāpi viśvāsaṃ paśyāmo na ca sarvatārkikairadūṣitaṃ samarthitaṃ sarvatārkikopadravāpasarpaṇāya vartma saṃbhāvayāmaḥ |
units.translation: One may object: “Every philosophical system seems sound from its own point of view, yet fails from the standpoint of the others. We can trust none of them, nor can we find a path that has been defended without objection by all logicians.”

units.label: Text 168
units.translation: The answer: consider it without anxiety, since every system of reasoning rests on direct experience. It is said:

units.label: Verse 2.59
units.translation: The questioner is addressed: debaters, grievously afflicted by the fever of logic, bewilder one another with a web of words used as armor.

gloss.en: with a web of words as protective covering

units.label: Text 171
units.deva: अत्रापि चोदयन्ति । अनुभवात्मनोऽपि विक्रियाभ्युपगमेऽनभ्युपगमेऽपि दोष एव । यस्मादाह ।
units.iast: atrāpi codayanti | anubhavātmano'pi vikriyābhyupagame'nabhyupagame'pi doṣa eva | yasmādāha |
units.translation: An objection is raised here: “Whether one accepts change or no change in the Self that is experience itself, a fault follows.” For it is said:

units.label: Verse 2.60
units.deva: "वर्षातपाभ्यां किं व्योम्नश्चर्मण्येव तयोः फलम् । चर्मोपमश्चेत्सोऽनित्यः खतुल्यश्चेदसत्समः " ॥ ६०॥
units.iast: "varṣātapābhyāṃ kiṃ vyomnaścarmaṇyeva tayoḥ phalam | carmopamaścetso'nityaḥ khatulyaścedasatsamaḥ " || 60||
units.translation: What effect do rain and sunlight have on the sky? Their effect is only on leather. If the Self were like leather, it would be impermanent; if like the sky, it would be unreal.

units.label: Verse 2.61
units.deva: बुद्धिजन्मनि पुंसश्च विकृतिर्यद्यनित्यता । अथाविकृतिरेवायं प्रमातेति न युज्यते ॥ ६१॥
units.iast: buddhijanmani puṃsaśca vikṛtiryadyanityatā | athāvikṛtirevāyaṃ pramāteti na yujyate || 61||
units.translation: If a person changes when intellect arises, he is impermanent; if he is entirely changeless, he cannot be the knower. Neither view is tenable.

units.label: Text 176
units.translation: The answer to this is:

units.label: Verse 2.62
units.deva: ऊर्ध्वं गच्छति धूमे खं भिद्यते स्विन्न भिद्यते । न भिद्यते चेत्स्थास्नुत्वं भिद्यते चेद्भिदास्य का ॥ ६२॥
units.iast: ūrdhvaṃ gacchati dhūme khaṃ bhidyate svinna bhidyate | na bhidyate cetsthāsnutvaṃ bhidyate cedbhidāsya kā || 62||
units.translation: As smoke rises, is the sky split or not? If it is not split, it remains whole; if split, what is the division?

units.label: Text 179
units.translation: To explain this point, he says:

units.label: Verse 2.63
units.translation: The changeless Self seems to be an experiencer through the delusion of the “I”-thought, just as motion is imagined in mountains because of a boat’s movement.

gloss.en: the state of being an experiencer
from the illusion of a moving boat

units.label: Text 182
units.translation: Another example is given to make the point clear:

units.label: Verse 2.64
units.deva: यथा जात्यमणेः शुभ्रा ज्वलन्ती निश्चला शिखा । संनिध्यसंनिधानेषु घटादीनामविक्रिया ॥ ६४॥
units.iast: yathā jātyamaṇeḥ śubhrā jvalantī niścalā śikhā | saṃnidhyasaṃnidhāneṣu ghaṭādīnāmavikriyā || 64||
units.translation: Like the bright, steady flame of a fine jewel, the Self remains unchanged whether pots and other objects are present or absent.

units.label: Text 185
units.translation: To indicate the particular point intended here, he says:

units.label: Verse 2.65
units.deva: यदवस्था व्यनक्तीति तदवस्थैव सा पुनः । भण्यते न व्यनक्तीति घटादीनामसंनिधौ ॥ ६५॥
units.iast: yadavasthā vyanaktīti tadavasthaiva sā punaḥ | bhaṇyate na vyanaktīti ghaṭādīnāmasaṃnidhau || 65||
units.translation: It is described as remaining in the same state whether it is said to illumine or not to illumine, when pots and other objects are absent.

units.label: Text 188
units.translation: And in this case,

units.label: Verse 2.66
units.translation: Like a lamp, the Supreme Self illumines all intellects; it remains unchanged whether mental states are present or absent.

units.label: Verse 2.67
units.deva: न प्रकाशक्रिया काचिदस्य स्वात्मनि विद्यते । उपचारात्क्रिया सास्य यः प्रकाशस्य संनिधिः ॥ ६७॥
units.iast: na prakāśakriyā kācidasya svātmani vidyate | upacārātkriyā sāsya yaḥ prakāśasya saṃnidhiḥ || 67||
units.translation: No act of illumination exists in the Self itself; the “act” attributed to it figuratively is simply an object’s presence in its light.

units.label: Text 193
units.translation: Do not suspect that this is merely the Sāṃkhya conclusion, because:

units.label: Verse 2.68
units.deva: यथा विशुद्ध आकाशे सहसैवाभ्रमण्डलम् । भूत्वा विलीयते तद्वदात्मनीहाखिलं जगत् ॥ ६८॥
units.iast: yathā viśuddha ākāśe sahasaivābhramaṇḍalam | bhūtvā vilīyate tadvadātmanīhākhilaṃ jagat || 68||
units.translation: Just as a mass of clouds suddenly appears in a clear sky and then dissolves, so the whole universe arises in the Self and dissolves there.

units.label: Text 196
units.deva: तस्मादेष कूटस्थो न द्वैतं मनागपि स्पृशति । यतः ।
units.iast: tasmādeṣa kūṭastho na dvaitaṃ manāgapi spṛśati | yataḥ |
units.translation: Therefore this immutable Self is not touched by duality in the least. For:

units.label: Verse 2.69
units.translation: Appearances in forms beginning with sound flash into awareness and vanish moment by moment; the one eternal, non-sequential Seer-Self seems to pervade the intellect constantly.

gloss.en: appearances in forms beginning with sound

units.label: Text 199
units.deva: एवं च सति बुद्धेः परिणामित्वं युक्तम् ।
units.iast: evaṃ ca sati buddheḥ pariṇāmitvaṃ yuktam |
units.translation: Thus it is reasonable that the intellect changes.

units.label: Verse 2.70
units.translation: The Self knows past, future, and present objects all at once; the intellect does not know them as the Self does, so the intellect undergoes change.

units.label: Text 202
units.translation: From this the point is established.

units.label: Verse 2.71
units.deva: अपश्यन्पश्यतीं बुद्धिमशृण्वन् शृण्वतीं तथा । निर्यत्नोऽविक्रियोऽनिच्छन्निच्छन्तीं चाप्यलुप्तदृक् ॥ ७१॥
units.iast: apaśyanpaśyatīṃ buddhimaśṛṇvan śṛṇvatīṃ tathā | niryatno'vikriyo'nicchannicchantīṃ cāpyaluptadṛk || 71||
units.translation: Not seeing, the Self witnesses the intellect that sees; not hearing, it witnesses the intellect that hears. Effortless, changeless, and without desire, its seeing never fails, even as the intellect desires.

units.label: Verse 2.72
units.deva: द्विषन्तीमद्विषन्नात्मा कुप्यन्तीं चाप्यकोपनः । निर्दुःखो दुःखिनीं चैव निस्सुखः सुखिनीमपि ॥ ७२॥
units.iast: dviṣantīmadviṣannātmā kupyantīṃ cāpyakopanaḥ | nirduḥkho duḥkhinīṃ caiva nissukhaḥ sukhinīmapi || 72||
units.translation: The Self does not hate a hateful mind or become angry with an angry mind; free from suffering, it witnesses the suffering mind, and without pleasure it witnesses the happy mind.

units.label: Verse 2.73
units.translation: Not deluded, the Self witnesses a deluded mind; not imagining, it witnesses an imagining mind; not remembering, it witnesses a remembering mind; not sleeping, it witnesses the mind repeatedly asleep.

units.label: Verse 2.74
units.deva: सर्वाकारां निराकारः स्वार्थोऽस्वार्थां निरिङ्गनः । निस्त्रिकालस्त्रिकालस्थां कूटस्थः क्षणभङ्गुराम् ॥ ७४॥
units.iast: sarvākārāṃ nirākāraḥ svārtho'svārthāṃ niriṅganaḥ | nistrikālastrikālasthāṃ kūṭasthaḥ kṣaṇabhaṅgurām || 74||
units.translation: The intellect takes every form, while the Self is formless; the intellect exists for another’s sake, while the Self exists for itself. The Self is unmoving and beyond time; the intellect exists in time and perishes moment by moment.

units.label: Verse 2.75
units.deva: निरपेक्षश्च सापेक्षां पराचीं प्रत्यगद्वयः । सावधिं निर्गतेयत्तः सर्वदेहेषु पश्यति ॥ ७५॥
units.iast: nirapekṣaśca sāpekṣāṃ parācīṃ pratyagadvayaḥ | sāvadhiṃ nirgateyattaḥ sarvadeheṣu paśyati || 75||
units.translation: The independent, inward, non-dual Self, limitless and present in every body, sees the intellect that is dependent, outward-facing, and bounded.

units.label: Text 213
units.translation: For this reason the point should be understood:

units.label: Verse 2.76
units.deva: दुःखी यदि भवेदात्मा कस्साक्षी दुःखिनो भवेत् । दुःखिनः साक्षितायुक्ता साक्षिणो दुःखिता तथा ॥ ७६॥
units.iast: duḥkhī yadi bhavedātmā kassākṣī duḥkhino bhavet | duḥkhinaḥ sākṣitāyuktā sākṣiṇo duḥkhitā tathā || 76||
units.translation: If the Self were the sufferer, who would witness the suffering one? The sufferer cannot properly be the witness; otherwise the witness too would suffer.

units.label: Text 216
units.translation: He explains the preceding statement:

units.label: Verse 2.77
units.deva: नर्ते स्याद्विक्रियां दुःखी साक्षिता का विकारिणः । धीविक्रियासहस्राणां साक्ष्यतोऽहमविक्रियः ॥ ७७॥
units.iast: narte syādvikriyāṃ duḥkhī sākṣitā kā vikāriṇaḥ | dhīvikriyāsahasrāṇāṃ sākṣyato'hamavikriyaḥ || 77||
units.translation: Without undergoing change, a sufferer could not be a witness; how could something changing itself be the witness? I am changeless because I witness thousands of changes in the intellect.

gloss.en: of thousands of changes in the intellect

units.label: Text 219
units.translation: To establish through experience that the Self alone is unchanging amid all that changes, he says:

units.label: Verse 2.78
units.deva: प्रमाणतन्निभेष्वस्या नोच्छित्तिर्मम संविदः । मत्तोऽन्यद्रूपमाभाति यत्तत्स्यात्क्षणभङ्गि हि ॥ ७८॥
units.iast: pramāṇatannibheṣvasyā nocchittirmama saṃvidaḥ | matto'nyadrūpamābhāti yattatsyātkṣaṇabhaṅgi hi || 78||
units.translation: There is no break in my awareness amid valid cognitions and their apparent counterparts; whatever form appears apart from me is momentary.

gloss.en: among valid cognitions and their apparent counterparts

units.label: Verse 2.79
units.deva: उत्पत्तिस्थितिभङ्गेषु कुम्भस्य वियतो यथा । नोत्पत्तिस्थितिनाशास्स्युर्बुद्धेरेवं ममापि च ॥७९॥
units.iast: utpattisthitibhaṅgeṣu kumbhasya viyato yathā | notpattisthitināśāssyurbuddherevaṃ mamāpi ca ||79||
units.translation: Just as a pot arises, persists, and breaks while space does not, so arising, persistence, and destruction belong to the intellect, not to me.

units.label: Text 224
units.translation: The connection with pleasure, pain, and the like is directly experienced; it is not accepted merely on faith.

units.label: Verse 2.80
units.deva: सुखदुःखादिसंबन्धां यथा दण्डेन दण्डिनम् । राधको वीक्षते बुद्धिं साक्षी तद्वदसंहतः ॥ ८०॥
units.iast: sukhaduḥkhādisaṃbandhāṃ yathā daṇḍena daṇḍinam | rādhako vīkṣate buddhiṃ sākṣī tadvadasaṃhataḥ || 80||
units.translation: An ascetic sees an ascetic burdened with a staff; likewise, the unattached Witness sees the intellect bound to pleasure and pain while remaining unaffected.

gloss.en: bound to pleasure, pain, and the rest

units.label: Text 227
units.translation: This is another reason why the intellect undergoes change:

units.label: Verse 2.81
units.deva: येनैवास्या भवेद्योगः सुखकुम्भादिना धियः । तं विदन्ती तदैवान्यं वेत्ति नातो विकारिणी ॥ ८१॥
units.iast: yenaivāsyā bhavedyogaḥ sukhakumbhādinā dhiyaḥ | taṃ vidantī tadaivānyaṃ vetti nāto vikāriṇī || 81||
units.translation: The intellect knows only what it is connected with—happiness, a pot, or the like. It does not know another thing at that same time; therefore it is changeful.

gloss.en: with precisely what; with that alone
with happiness, a pot, and the like

units.label: Text 230
units.deva: अस्याश्च क्षणभङ्गरत्वे स्वयमेवात्मा साक्षी । न हि कूटस्थावबोधमन्तरेण बुद्धेरेवाविर्भावतिरोभावादिसिद्धिरस्ति ।
units.iast: asyāśca kṣaṇabhaṅgaratve svayamevātmā sākṣī | na hi kūṭasthāvabodhamantareṇa buddherevāvirbhāvatirobhāvādisiddhirasti |
units.translation: The Self itself witnesses the momentary nature of the intellect. Without changeless awareness, the intellect’s arising and disappearance could not be established.

units.label: Verse 2.82
units.deva: परिणामिधियां वृत्तं नित्याक्रमदृगात्मना । षड्भावविक्रियामेति व्याप्तं खेनाङ्करो यथा ॥ ८२॥
units.iast: pariṇāmidhiyāṃ vṛttaṃ nityākramadṛgātmanā | ṣaḍbhāvavikriyāmeti vyāptaṃ khenāṅkuro yathā || 82||
units.translation: The activity of changing intellects undergoes the six changes of state, pervaded by the eternal, non-sequential Seer-Self, just as a sprout is pervaded by space.

units.label: Text 233
units.translation: Here is the reasoning for the changelessness of the existent Self:

units.label: Verse 2.83
units.deva: स्मृतिस्वप्नप्रबोधेषु न कश्चित्प्रत्ययो धियः । दृशाव्याप्तोऽस्त्यतो नित्यमविकारी स्वयंदृशिः ॥ ८३॥
units.iast: smṛtisvapnaprabodheṣu na kaścitpratyayo dhiyaḥ | dṛśāvyāpto'styato nityamavikārī svayaṃdṛśiḥ || 83||
units.translation: No mental cognition in memory, dream, or waking is without the Seer's light; therefore the self-revealing Seer is eternal and changeless.

units.label: Text 236
units.deva: एवं तावत्पराभ्युपगतप्रक्रियाप्रस्थानेन निरस्ताशेषविकारैकात्म्यं प्रतिपादितमुपपत्तिभिः । अथाधुना श्रौतीं प्रक्रियामवलम्ब्योच्यते ।
units.iast: evaṃ tāvatparābhyupagataprakriyāprasthānena nirastāśeṣavikāraikātmyaṃ pratipāditamupapattibhiḥ | athādhunā śrautīṃ prakriyāmavalambyocyate |
units.translation: Thus, using the position admitted by the opponent, it has been shown through reasoning that the one Self is free from every change. Now the point is stated by relying on the scriptural method.

units.label: Verse 2.84
units.deva: अस्तु वा परिणामोऽस्य दृशेः कूटस्थरूपतः । कल्पितोऽपि मृषैवासौ दण्डस्येवाप्सु वक्रता ॥ ८४॥
units.iast: astu vā pariṇāmo'sya dṛśeḥ kūṭastharūpataḥ | kalpito'pi mṛṣaivāsau daṇḍasyevāpsu vakratā || 84||
units.translation: Even if one grants a change in this Seer, whose nature is firm and changeless, that imagined change is false—like a stick appearing crooked in water.

gloss.en: because of its firm, changeless nature

units.label: Verse 2.85
units.deva: षट्सु भावविकारेषु निषिद्धेश्वेवमात्मनि । दोषः कश्चिदिहासक्तुं न शक्यस्तार्किकश्वभिः ॥ ८५॥
units.iast: ṣaṭsu bhāvavikāreṣu niṣiddheśvevamātmani | doṣaḥ kaścidihāsaktuṃ na śakyastārkikaśvabhiḥ || 85||
units.translation: Once the six changes of state have thus been ruled out in the Self, no fault can be fastened on it here, even by the “dogs of logic.”

gloss.en: by the dogs of logic; by logicians

units.label: Text 241
units.translation: The reasoning is now stated, taking up the same subject: the intellect changes, while the Self remains immutable.

units.label: Verse 2.86
units.deva: प्रत्यर्थं तु विभिद्यन्ते बुद्धयो विषयोन्मुखाः । न भिदावगतेस्तद्वत्सर्वास्ताश्चिन्निभा यतः ॥ ८६॥
units.iast: pratyarthaṃ tu vibhidyante buddhayo viṣayonmukhāḥ | na bhidāvagatestadvatsarvāstāścinnibhā yataḥ || 86||
units.translation: Intellects turned toward objects differ according to each object. Awareness does not differ that way, since all those intellects reflect consciousness.

units.label: Text 244
units.translation: Each intellect knows only the object connected with itself;

units.label: Verse 2.87
units.deva: सावशेषपरिच्छेदिन्यत एव न कृत्स्नवित् । नो चेत्परिणमेद्बुद्धिः सर्वज्ञा स्वात्मवद्भवेत् ॥ ८७॥
units.iast: sāvaśeṣaparicchedinyata eva na kṛtsnavit | no cetpariṇamedbuddhiḥ sarvajñā svātmavadbhavet || 87||
units.translation: The intellect knows in a limited, incomplete way and therefore does not know everything. If it did not change, it would be all-knowing like the Self.

gloss.en: if not; if it did not

units.label: Text 247
units.translation: Since awareness is one,

units.label: Verse 2.88
units.iast: caṇḍālabuddheryad draṣṭṛ tadeva brahmabuddhidṛk | ekaṃ tadubhayorjyotirbhāsyabhedādanekavat || 88||
units.translation: The Seer of an outcaste’s intellect is the very same as the Seer of Brahmā’s intellect; the one light in both appears as many because the objects it illumines differ.

units.label: Text 250
units.translation: Why? Because

units.label: Verse 2.89
units.deva: अवस्थादेशकालादिभेदो नास्त्यनयोर्यतः । तस्माज्जगद्धियां वृत्तं ज्योतिरेकं सदेक्षते ॥ ८९॥
units.iast: avasthādeśakālādibhedo nāstyanayoryataḥ | tasmājjagaddhiyāṃ vṛttaṃ jyotirekaṃ sadekṣate || 89||
units.translation: There is no difference of state, place, time, and so on between these two. Therefore the one eternal light witnesses the activity of the intellects in the world.

gloss.en: difference of state, place, time, and the like
of the intellects in the world

units.label: Text 253
units.translation: One might object: “If the Self is one in every body, then even one awakened to the truth would remain connected with every suffering associated with other bodies.” That is not so.

units.label: Verse 2.90
units.deva: बोधात्प्रागपि दुःखित्वं नान्यदेहोत्थमस्ति नः । बोधादूर्ध्वं कुतस्तत्स्याद्यत्र स्वगतमप्यसत् ॥ ९०॥
units.iast: bodhātprāgapi duḥkhitvaṃ nānyadehotthamasti naḥ | bodhādūrdhvaṃ kutastatsyādyatra svagatamapyasat || 90||
units.translation: Even before knowledge, our suffering does not arise from another body. How could it do so after knowledge, when even suffering arising in one’s own body is then understood to be unreal?

units.label: Text 256
units.translation: This should not be taken as my own unsupported opinion. Why?

units.label: Text 257
units.translation: Because it is grounded in revelation.

units.label: Verse 2.91
units.translation: Perception, which appears in the forms of sound and the rest and is subject to rejecting and taking up, is illumined by the unchanging Self, says the Śruti.

gloss.en: appearing in the forms of sound and the like
having the nature of rejecting and taking up
of the Self; by the Self

units.label: Text 260
units.translation: Which passage of revelation?

units.label: Verse 2.92
units.deva: दृष्टेर्द्रष्टारमात्मानं न पश्येर्दृश्यमानया । विज्ञातारमरे केन विजानीयाद्धियां पतिम् ॥ ९२॥
units.iast: dṛṣṭerdraṣṭāramātmānaṃ na paśyerdṛśyamānayā | vijñātāramare kena vijānīyāddhiyāṃ patim || 92||
units.translation: You cannot see the Seer of seeing by means of what is itself seen. Dear one, by what could you know the Knower, the lord of the intellects?

units.label: Text 263
units.translation: Since this point is established by every means of knowledge, those who argue otherwise are like people blind from birth and deserve compassion.

units.label: Verse 2.93
units.deva: तदेतदद्वयं ब्रह्म निर्विकारं कुबुद्धिभिः । जात्यन्धगजदृष्ट्येव कोटिशः परिकल्प्यते ॥ ९३॥
units.iast: tadetadadvayaṃ brahma nirvikāraṃ kubuddhibhiḥ | jātyandhagajadṛṣṭyeva koṭiśaḥ parikalpyate || 93||
units.translation: People of poor understanding conceive this non-dual, changeless Brahman in countless ways, like people born blind trying to picture an elephant.

gloss.en: by the seeing of an elephant

units.label: Text 266
units.translation: Since they cannot accept what is established by means of knowledge, they are indeed to be pitied.

units.label: Text 267
units.translation: He states the point:

units.label: Verse 2.94
units.deva: यद्यद्विशेषणं दृष्टं नात्मनस्तदनन्वयात् । खस्य कुम्भादिवत्तस्मादात्मा स्यान्निर्विशेषणः ॥ ९४॥
units.iast: yadyadviśeṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ nātmanastadananvayāt | khasya kumbhādivattasmādātmā syānnirviśeṣaṇaḥ || 94||
units.translation: No distinguishing property that is observed belongs to the Self, since such properties do not adhere to it. Just as space is not confined by a pot, the Self is without qualifications.

gloss.en: because it does not adhere; because there is no connection
as with a pot and the like

units.label: Text 270
units.translation: Difference does not touch the Self because its nature is false. Therefore he says:

units.label: Verse 2.95
units.deva: अवगत्यात्मनो यस्मादागमापायि कुम्भवत् । साहंकारमिदं विश्वं तस्मात्तत्स्यात्कचादिवत् ॥ ९५॥
units.iast: avagatyātmano yasmādāgamāpāyi kumbhavat | sāhaṃkāramidaṃ viśvaṃ tasmāttatsyātkacādivat || 95||
units.translation: Since this world with ego comes and goes in awareness like a pot, it is as unreal as the hair-like specks seen before the eyes.

gloss.en: of the Self whose nature is awareness

units.label: Text 273
units.translation: The entire work of inference is only this: to grasp a distinction.

units.label: Text 274
units.translation: This is stated:

units.label: Verse 2.96
units.translation: Inference establishes that the intellect is a property of the not-Self; the Self’s non-duality is established simply by its being the Self.

gloss.en: being a property of the not-Self

units.label: Text 277
units.deva: यद्यप्ययं ग्रहीतृग्रहणग्राह्यगृहीतितत्फलात्मक आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्तः संसारोऽन्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यामनात्मतया निर्माल्यवदपविद्धः । तथापि तु नैवासौ स्वतस्सिद्धात्म व्यतिरिक्तानात्मप्रकृतिपदार्थव्यपाश्रयः सांख्यानामिव ।
units.iast: yadyapyayaṃ grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyagṛhītitatphalātmaka ābrahmastambaparyantaḥ saṃsāro'nvayavyatirekābhyāmanātmatayā nirmālyavadapaviddhaḥ | tathāpi tu naivāsau svatassiddhātma vyatiriktānātmaprakṛtipadārthavyapāśrayaḥ sāṃkhyānāmiva |
units.translation: Though saṃsāra, from Brahmā down to a clump of grass, consisting of knower, knowing, known, and their results, has been discarded as not-Self through agreement and exclusion, like a withered garland, it does not depend on a material principle separate from the self-established Self, as the Sāṃkhyas claim.

units.label: Text 278
units.translation: What, then, is its basis?

units.label: Text 279
units.translation: It rests on ignorance of the Self, which is not examined and is reflected in the self-established, unborn, unceasing, immutable awareness of the Self. Ignorance is its material cause. To explain this point, he says:

units.label: Verse 2.97
units.deva: ऋते ज्ञानं न सन्त्यर्था अस्ति ज्ञानमृतेऽपि तान् । एवं धियो हिरुग्ज्योतिर्विविच्यादनुमानतः ॥ ९७॥
units.iast: ṛte jñānaṃ na santyarthā asti jñānamṛte'pi tān | evaṃ dhiyo hirugjyotirvivicyādanumānataḥ || 97||
units.translation: Objects do not exist apart from knowledge, while knowledge exists even without them. By this inference, one distinguishes the light from the intellect.

gloss.en: the light set apart; the distinct light

units.label: Text 282
units.deva: यस्मात्प्रमाणप्रमेयव्यवहार आत्मानवबोधाश्रय एव तस्मात्सिद्धमात्मनोऽप्रमेयत्वम् । नैव हि कार्यं स्वकारणमतिलङ्घ्यान्यत्राकारक आस्पदमुपनिबध्नाति ।
units.iast: yasmātpramāṇaprameyavyavahāra ātmānavabodhāśraya eva tasmātsiddhamātmano'prameyatvam | naiva hi kāryaṃ svakāraṇamatilaṅghyānyatrākāraka āspadamupanibadhnāti |
units.translation: Since the dealings between means of knowledge and their objects rest only on ignorance of the Self, the Self is established as beyond objectification. An effect does not set its own cause aside and find a footing elsewhere.

units.label: Text 283
units.translation: Therefore he says:

units.label: Verse 2.98
units.deva: व्यवधीयन्त एवामी बुद्धिदेहघटादयः । आत्मत्वादात्मनः केन व्यवधानं मनागपि ॥ ९८॥
units.iast: vyavadhīyanta evāmī buddhidehaghaṭādayaḥ | ātmatvādātmanaḥ kena vyavadhānaṃ manāgapi || 98||
units.translation: Intellect, body, pot, and the like are known through an intermediary. Since the Self is already the Self, what could mediate it even slightly?

gloss.en: are mediated; are known through an intermediary
intellect, body, pot, and the rest

units.label: Text 286
units.translation: Because the intellect and the rest are not themselves awareness, their non-awareness rests on delusion alone.

units.label: Verse 2.99
units.translation: The intellect and the rest are not established without a means of knowledge. Since immediate awareness is the desired result, what could the knowing Self depend on?

gloss.en: of the intellect and the rest
because immediate awareness is the desired result

units.label: Text 289
units.translation: The earlier distinction is repeated to establish the mutual superimposition that will be explained next:

units.label: Verse 2.100
units.translation: Just as the Seer is distinct from the cognition of a pot and from the pot itself, so the Seer is distinct from the “I”-cognition, from the “I” that is known, and from the sufferer.

gloss.en: from the cognition of a pot

units.label: Text 292
units.deva: एवमेतयोरात्मानात्मनोः स्वतः परतः सिद्धयोर्लौकिकरज्जु सर्पाध्यारोपवदविद्योपाश्रय एवेतरेतराध्यारोप इत्येतदाह ।
units.iast: evametayorātmānātmanoḥ svataḥ parataḥ siddhayorlaukikarajju sarpādhyāropavadavidyopāśraya evetaretarādhyāropa ityetadāha |
units.translation: Thus the mutual superimposition of the Self and not-Self—each established in itself and in the other—is supported only by ignorance, like the snake superimposed on a rope.

units.label: Verse 2.101
units.deva: अभ्रयानं यथा मोहाच्छशभृत्यध्यवस्यति । सुखित्वादीन् धियो धर्मांस्तद्वदात्मनि मन्यते ॥ १०१॥
units.iast: abhrayānaṃ yathā mohācchaśabhṛtyadhyavasyati | sukhitvādīndhiyo dharmāṃstadvadātmani manyate || 101||
units.translation: Just as, through delusion, someone thinks the moon moves along with the clouds, so one regards qualities of the intellect—happiness and the like—as belonging to the Self.

units.label: Verse 2.102
units.deva: दग्धृत्वं च यथा वह्नेरयसो मन्यते कुधीः । चैतन्यं तद्वदात्मीयं मोहात्कर्तरि मन्यते ॥ १०२॥
units.iast: dagdhṛtvaṃ ca yathā vahnerayaso manyate kudhīḥ | caitanyaṃ tadvadātmīyaṃ mohātkartari manyate || 102||
units.translation: Just as an unwise person thinks the power to burn belongs to iron, though it belongs to fire, so through delusion one thinks the Self’s consciousness belongs to the doer.

units.label: Text 297
units.deva: सर्व एवायमात्मानात्मविभागः प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणवर्त्मन्युनपतितोऽविद्योत्सङ्गवर्त्येव न परमात्मव्यपाश्रयः । अस्याश्चाविद्यायाः सर्वानर्थहेतोः कुतो निवृत्तिरिति चेत्तदाह ।
units.iast: sarva evāyamātmānātmavibhāgaḥ pratyakṣādipramāṇavartmanyunapatito'vidyotsaṅgavartyeva na paramātmavyapāśrayaḥ | asyāścāvidyāyāḥ sarvānarthahetoḥ kuto nivṛttiriti cettadāha |
units.translation: The whole division between Self and not-Self that appears through perception and the other means of knowledge exists only in the lap of ignorance; it does not depend on the Supreme Self. How is this ignorance removed? He says:

units.label: Verse 2.103
units.deva: दुःखराशेर्विचित्रस्य सेयं भ्रान्तिश्चिरन्तनी । मूलं संसारवृक्षस्य तद्बाधस्तत्त्वदर्शनात् ॥ १०३॥
units.iast: duḥkharāśervicitrasya seyaṃ bhrāntiścirantanī | mūlaṃ saṃsāravṛkṣasya tadbādhastattvadarśanāt || 103||
units.translation: This ancient delusion is the root of the manifold mass of suffering and of the tree of saṃsāra; it is removed by seeing reality.

units.label: Text 300
units.deva: तद्बाधस्तत्त्वदर्शनादिति कुतः संभाव्यत इति चेदत आहागोपालाविपालपण्डितमियमेव प्रसिद्धिः ।
units.iast: tadbādhastattvadarśanāditi kutaḥ saṃbhāvyata iti cedata āhāgopālāvipālapaṇḍitamiyameva prasiddhiḥ |
units.translation: If one asks how seeing reality could remove it, that is well known to everyone, from cowherd to scholar:

units.label: Verse 2.104
units.deva: अप्रमोत्थं प्रमोत्थेन ज्ञानं ज्ञानेन बाध्यते । अहिरज्ज्वादिवद्बाधो देहाद्यात्ममतेस्तथा ॥ १०४॥
units.iast: apramotthaṃ pramotthena jñānaṃ jñānena bādhyate | ahirajjvādivadbādho dehādyātmamatestathā || 104||
units.translation: Knowledge arising from invalid cognition is sublated by knowledge arising from valid cognition. Likewise, the view that the body and the rest are the Self is sublated, as with a snake mistaken for a rope.

gloss.en: by what arises from valid cognition
as with a snake, rope, and the like
of the view that the body and the rest are the Self

units.label: Text 303
units.translation: Because the Self differs from ordinary objects of knowledge, the result of a means of knowledge is not the acquisition of something previously unknown.

units.label: Verse 2.105
units.translation: The “result” is spoken of as merely the destruction of ignorance. It is not right to say that something previously unknown is made known, since awareness has a single nature.

gloss.en: because awareness has a single nature

units.label: Text 306
units.translation: Since the knower and the rest are produced only by ignorance of the Self,

units.label: Verse 2.106
units.deva: न विदन्त्यात्मनः सत्तां द्रष्टृदर्शनगोचराः । न चान्योन्यमतोऽमीषां ज्ञेयत्वं भिन्नसाधनम् ॥ १०६॥
units.iast: na vidantyātmanaḥ sattāṃ draṣṭṛdarśanagocarāḥ | na cānyonyamato'mīṣāṃ jñeyatvaṃ bhinnasādhanam || 106||
units.translation: The knower, the act of knowing, and the known do not reveal the Self’s existence; nor can they establish one another. Each is knowable only through a means distinct from itself.

gloss.en: do not know; do not reveal
within the range of knower and knowing

units.label: Text 309
units.translation: To show the distinctive nature of the knower and the rest, he says:

units.label: Verse 2.107
units.deva: बाह्य आकारवान् ग्राह्यो ग्रहणं निश्चयादिमत् । अन्वय्यहमिति ज्ञेयः साक्षी त्वात्मा ध्रुवः सदा ॥ १०७॥
units.iast: bāhya ākāravān grāhyo grahaṇaṃ niścayādimat | anvayyahamiti jñeyaḥ sākṣī tvātmā dhruvaḥ sadā || 107||
units.translation: The known is external and has form; cognition has certainty and the like; the “I” that continues through experience is the knower. But the Witness is the Self, constant forever.

units.label: Text 312
units.translation: The Self is free of saṃsāra, which consists of the divisions of all agents, actions, and results. Because the Self witnesses those divisions, he says:

units.label: Verse 2.108
units.translation: Amid the division into perceiver, perceiving, and perceived, the Self remains undivided: witness of loss and gain, yet free of both.

gloss.en: in the division into perceiver, perceiving, and perceived
of loss and gain; rejection and acceptance

units.label: Text 315
units.translation: If one asks why the divisions of knower and the rest cannot be established by themselves, he says:

units.label: Verse 2.109
units.deva: स्वसाधन स्वयं नष्टो न नाशं वेत्त्यभावतः । अत एव न चान्येषामतोऽसौ भिन्नसाक्षिकः ॥ १०९॥
units.iast: svasādhana svayaṃ naṣṭo na nāśaṃ vettyabhāvataḥ | ata eva na cānyeṣāmato'sau bhinnasākṣikaḥ || 109||
units.translation: An instrument, once destroyed, cannot know its own destruction or that of anything else, because it no longer exists. Therefore it must be witnessed by something distinct from it.

units.label: Text 318
units.translation: If one argues that the knower and the rest must first be established by another witness, and that this witness too requires another, leading to an infinite regress, that is not so, because the witness does not depend on an external cause. He says:

units.label: Verse 2.110
units.deva: धीवन्नापेक्षते सिद्धिमात्मान्यस्मादविक्रियः । निरपेक्षमपेक्ष्यैव सिध्यन्त्यन्ये न तु स्वयम् ॥ ११०॥
units.iast: dhīvannāpekṣate siddhimātmānyasmādavikriyaḥ | nirapekṣamapekṣyaiva sidhyantyanye na tu svayam || 110||
units.translation: Unlike the intellect, the changeless Self does not depend on anything else for its establishment. All other things are established only by depending on what is independent; they are not established by themselves.

units.label: Text 321
units.deva: यतो ग्राहकादिष्वात्मभावोऽविद्यानिबन्धन एव तस्मादन्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यां विभज्यानात्मनः स्वयम् ।
units.iast: yato grāhakādiṣvātmabhāvo'vidyānibandhana eva tasmādanvayavyatirekābhyāṃ vibhajyānātmanaḥ svayam |
units.translation: Since the “I” notion in the knower and the rest is grounded in ignorance, distinguish it from the Self through agreement and exclusion.

units.label: Verse 2.111
units.deva: उत्पत्तिस्थितिनाशेषु योऽवगत्यैव वर्तते । जगतोऽविकारयावेहि तमस्मीति न नश्वरम् ॥ १११॥
units.iast: utpattisthitināśeṣu yo'vagatyaiva vartate | jagato'vikārayāvehi tamasmīti na naśvaram || 111||
units.translation: He who remains as awareness through the world’s arising, persistence, and destruction—know him as changeless: “I am that,” not the perishable.

units.label: Text 324
units.translation: This magical duality of the not-Self arises from unexamined ignorance reflected in the self-established awareness of the Self. Its parts depend on one another for their existence and are not established by themselves.

units.label: Verse 2.112
units.deva: न स्वयं स्वस्य नानात्वं नावगत्यात्मना यतः । नोभाभ्यामप्यतस्सिद्धमद्वैतं द्वैतबाधया ॥ ११२॥
units.iast: na svayaṃ svasya nānātvam nāvagatyātmanā yataḥ | nobhābhyāmapyatas siddhamadvaitaṃ dvaitabādhayā || 112||
units.translation: Plurality cannot establish itself as real, nor can the Self as awareness establish it, nor can both together. Therefore non-duality is established by the sublation of duality.

gloss.en: by the Self whose nature is awareness

units.label: Text 327
units.translation: A scriptural example is introduced to strengthen understanding of what has been said:

units.label: Verse 2.113
units.deva: नित्यावगतिरूपत्वात्कारकादिर्न चात्मनः । अस्थूलं नेतिनेतीति न जायत इति श्रुतिः ॥ ११३॥
