units.iast: nityāvagatirūpatvātkārakādirna cātmanaḥ | asthūlaṃ netinetīti na jāyata iti śrutiḥ || 113||
units.translation: Because the Self is eternally awareness, it has no agency or other factors of action. The Śruti says of it, “Not gross; not this, not this; it is not born.”

gloss.en: because its nature is eternal awareness
agency and the other factors of action

units.label: Text 330
units.translation: Since this entire dualistic display of knower and the rest rests only on ignorance and cannot establish itself, while the Self is already established and need not be attained,

units.label: Verse 2.114
units.translation: If intellect, body, pot, and the like are excluded from the Self, they should ultimately be understood as objects of non-perception, the sixth means of knowledge.

gloss.en: intellect, body, pot, and the rest
fit to be known by the sixth means of knowledge

units.label: Text 333
units.translation: How is this conclusion reached through reasoning? Because:

units.label: Verse 2.115
units.deva: नित्यां संविदमाश्रित्य स्वतस्सिद्धामविक्रियाम् । सिद्धायन्ते धियो बोधास्तांश्चाश्रित्य घटादयः ॥ ११५॥
units.iast: nityāṃ saṃvidamāśritya svatassiddhāmavikriyām | siddhāyante dhiyo bodhāstāṃścāśritya ghaṭādayaḥ || 115||
units.translation: Relying on eternal, self-established, changeless awareness, intellects and cognitions are established; relying on them, pots and the like are established.

units.label: Text 336
units.deva: यस्मान्न कयाचिदपि युक्त्यात्मनः कारकत्वं क्रियात्वं फलत्वं चोपपद्यते तस्मादात्मवस्तुयाथात्म्यानवबोधमात्रोपादानत्वान्नभसीव रजोधूमतुषार नीहारनीलत्वाद्यध्यासो यथोक्तात्मनि सर्वोऽयं क्रियाकारकफलात्मकसंसारोऽहंममत्वयत्नेच्छादिमिथ्याध्यास एवेति सिद्धमिममर्थमाह ।
units.iast: yasmānna kayācidapi yuktyātmanaḥ kārakatvaṃ kriyātvaṃ phalatvaṃ copapadyate tasmādātmavastuyāthātmyānavabodhamātropādānatvānnabhasīva rajodhūmatuṣāra nīhāranīlatvādyadhyāso yathoktātmani sarvo'yaṃ kriyākārakaphalātmakasaṃsāro'haṃmamatvayatnecchādimithyādhyāsa eveti siddhamimamarthamāha |
units.translation: Since no reasoning can establish the Self as agent, action, or result, all this saṃsāra—consisting of action, agent, and fruit—is only a false superimposition, like dust, smoke, frost, mist, and blueness upon the sky. Its only basis is ignorance of the true nature of the Self. Thus the ego, “mine,” effort, desire, and the rest are false superimpositions. He states the point:

units.label: Verse 2.116
units.deva: अहंमिथ्याभिशापेन दुःख्यात्मा तद्बुभुत्सया । इतः श्रुतिं तया नेतीत्युक्तः कैवल्यमास्थितः ॥ ११६॥
units.iast: ahaṃmithyābhiśāpena duḥkhyātmā tadbubhutsayā | itaḥ śrutiṃ tayā netītyuktaḥ kaivalyamāsthitaḥ || 116||
units.translation: The Self seems to suffer under the curse of the false “I.” Wanting to know its true nature, it turns to the Śruti, is taught by it “not this, not this,” and abides in liberation.

gloss.en: by the curse of the false “I”
from the desire to know that

units.label: Text 339
units.deva: तस्यास्य मुमुक्षोः श्रौताद्वचसः स्वप्ननिमित्तोत्सारितनिद्रस्येवेयं निश्चितार्था प्रमा जायते ।
units.iast: tasyāsya mumukṣoḥ śrautādvacasaḥ svapnanimittotsāritanidrasyeveyaṃ niścitārthā pramā jāyate |
units.translation: For this seeker, certain knowledge arises from the words of revelation, like one awakened from sleep caused by a dream.

units.label: Verse 2.117
units.deva: नाहं न च ममात्मत्वात्सर्वदानात्मवर्जितः । भानाविव तमोध्यासोऽपह्नवश्च तथा मयि ॥ ११७॥
units.iast: nāhaṃ na ca mamātmatvātsarvadānātmavarjitaḥ | bhānāviva tamodhyāso'pahnavaśca tathā mayi || 117||
units.translation: “There is no separate ‘I’ or ‘mine’: by nature I am the Self, always free of the not-Self. As darkness is superimposed on light and then removed, so ignorance and its removal are superimposed on me.”

gloss.en: because I am the Self by nature

units.label: Text 342
units.translation: Having thus understood the nature of the Self, the seeker laments:

units.label: Verse 2.118
units.deva: यत्र त्वस्येति साटोपं कृत्स्नद्वैतनिषेधिनीम् । प्रोत्सारयन्तीं संसारमप्यश्रौषं न किं श्रुतिम् ॥ ११८॥
units.iast: yatra tvasya iti sāṭopaṃ kṛtsnadvaitaniṣedhinīm | protsārayantīṃ saṃsāramapyaśrauṣaṃ na kiṃ śrutim || 118||
units.translation: “When all this has become the Self”—why did I not hear that emphatic Śruti, which rejects all duality and sweeps away saṃsāra?

gloss.en: “but when all this has become the Self”

units.label: Verse 2.119
units.translation: Having realized the Self as “Om,” he is partless, not an agent, and actionless; as though detached from the intellect and the rest, he has attained solitude.

gloss.en: from the intellect and the rest

units.label: Chapter colophon
units.translation: Thus ends the second chapter.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Chapter heading
units.translation: Now begins the third chapter.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 2
units.deva: सर्वोऽयं प्रमितिप्रमाणप्रमेयप्रमातृलक्षण आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्तो मिथ्याध्यास एवेति बहुश उपपत्तिभिरतिष्ठिपम् । आत्मा च जन्मादिषड्भावविकारवर्जितः कूटस्थबोध एवेति स्फुटीकृतम् । तयोश्च मिथ्याध्यासकूटस्थात्मनोर्नान्तरेणाज्ञानं संबन्धोऽन्यत्र चोदनापरिप्रापितात् यथा "इयमेवर्गग्निः साम" इति । तच्चाज्ञानं स्वात्ममात्र निमित्तं न संभवतीति कस्यचित्कस्मिंश्चिद्विषये भवतीत्यभ्युपगन्तव्यम् । इह च पदार्थद्वयं निर्द्धारितमात्मानात्मा च । तत्रानात्मनस्तावन्नाज्ञानेनाभिसंबन्धः । तस्य हि स्वरूपमेवाज्ञानं न हि स्वतोऽज्ञानस्याज्ञानं घटते । संभवदप्यज्ञानस्वभावेऽज्ञानं कमतिशयं जनयेत् । न च तत्र ज्ञानप्राप्तिरस्ति येन तत्प्रतिषेधात्मकमज्ञानं स्यात् । अनात्मनश्चाज्ञानप्रसूतत्त्वात् । न हि पूर्वसिद्धं सत्ततोलब्धात्मलाभस्य सेत्स्यत आश्रयस्याश्रयि संभवति । तदनपेक्षस्य च तस्य निस्स्वभावत्वात् । एतेभ्य एव हेतुभ्यो नानात्मविषयमज्ञानं संभवतीति ग्राह्यम् । एवं तावन्नानात्मनोऽज्ञानित्वं नापि तद्विषयमज्ञानम् । पारिशेष्यादात्मन एवास्त्वज्ञानं तस्याज्ञोऽस्मीत्यनुभवदर्शनात् । "सोऽहं भगवो मन्त्रविदेवास्मि नात्मवित् "इति श्रुतेः ।
units.iast: sarvo'yaṃ pramitipramāṇaprameyapramātṛlakṣaṇa ābrahmastambaparyanto mithyādhyāsa eveti bahuśa upapattibhiratiṣṭhipam | ātmā ca janmādiṣaḍbhāvavikāravarjitaḥ kūṭasthabodha eveti sphuṭīkṛtam | tayośca mithyādhyāsakūṭasthātmanornāntareṇājñānaṃ saṃbandho'nyatra codanāpariprāpitāt yathā "iyamevargagniḥ sāma" iti | taccājñānaṃ svātmamātra nimittaṃ na saṃbhavatīti kasyacitkasmiṃścidviṣaye bhavatītyabhyupagantavyam | iha ca padārthadvayaṃ nirddhāritamātmānātmā ca | tatrānātmanastāvannājñānenābhisaṃbandhaḥ | tasya hi svarūpamevājñānaṃ na hi svato'jñānasyājñānaṃ ghaṭate | saṃbhavadapyajñānasvabhāve'jñānaṃ kamatiśayaṃ janayet | na ca tatra jñānaprāptirasti yena tatpratiṣedhātmakamajñānaṃ syāt | anātmanaścājñānaprasūtattvāt | na hi pūrvasiddhaṃ sattatolabdhātmalābhasya setsyata āśrayasyāśrayi saṃbhavati | tadanapekṣasya ca tasya nissvabhāvatvāt | etebhya eva hetubhyo nānātmaviṣayamajñānaṃ saṃbhavatīti grāhyam | evaṃ tāvannānātmano'jñānitvaṃ nāpi tadviṣayamajñānam | pāriśeṣyādātmana evāstvajñānaṃ tasyājño'smītyanubhavadarśanāt | "so'haṃ bhagavo mantravidevāsmi nātmavit "iti śruteḥ |
units.translation: It has been established through many arguments that the whole world, from Brahmā down to a clump of grass, consisting of knower, means of knowledge, objects of knowledge, and cognition, is only a false superimposition. It has also been made clear that the Self is changeless awareness, free from the six modifications beginning with birth. The relation between this false superimposition and the changeless Self requires ignorance; it is not otherwise possible, as in a scriptural sentence such as “this very Ṛc is fire.” That ignorance cannot arise from the Self alone, so it must be admitted to occur in some subject with respect to some object. Two things have been established here: the Self and the not-Self. Ignorance cannot belong to the not-Self: its very nature is ignorance, and ignorance cannot be ignorance of itself. Even if ignorance could belong to something already ignorant, what further ignorance could it produce? Nor can the not-Self be the locus in which knowledge arises, for it is itself produced by ignorance. What already exists cannot have a support in something that comes into existence only afterward. And if ignorance did not depend on it, the not-Self would have no nature of its own. For these reasons, ignorance cannot have the not-Self as its object. Thus the not-Self is neither ignorant nor the object of ignorance. By elimination, ignorance must belong to the Self, since we experience, “I am ignorant,” and scripture says, “I know the mantras, but I do not know the Self.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 3
units.deva: न चात्मनोऽज्ञानस्वरूपता तस्य चैतन्यमात्रस्वाभाव्या दतिशयश्च संभवति ज्ञानविपरिलोपो ज्ञानप्राप्तेश्च संभवस्तस्य ज्ञानकारित्वात् । न च अज्ञानकार्यत्वं कूटस्थात्मस्वाभाव्यादज्ञानानपेक्षस्य चात्मनः स्वत एव स्वरूपसिद्धेर्युक्तमात्मन एवाज्ञत्वम् । किंविषयं पुनस्तदात्मनोऽज्ञानम् । आत्मविषयमिति ब्रूमः । नन्वात्मनोऽपि ज्ञानस्वरूपत्वादनन्यत्वाच्च ज्ञानप्रकृतित्वादिभ्यश्च हेतुभ्यो नैवाज्ञानं घटते । घटत एव । कथम् ।
units.iast: na cātmano'jñānasvarūpatā tasya caitanyamātrasvābhāvyā datiśayaśca saṃbhavati jñānaviparilopo jñānaprāpteśca saṃbhavastasya jñānakāritvāt | na ca ajñānakāryatvaṃ kūṭasthātmasvābhāvyādajñānānapekṣasya cātmanaḥ svata eva svarūpasiddheryuktamātmana evājñatvam | kiṃviṣayaṃ punastadātmano'jñānam | ātmaviṣayamiti brūmaḥ | nanvātmano'pi jñānasvarūpatvādananyatvācca jñānaprakṛtitvādibhyaśca hetubhyo naivājñānaṃ ghaṭate | ghaṭata eva | katham |
units.translation: But the Self cannot have ignorance as its nature, since its nature is pure consciousness alone. Nor can it contain a further quality called ignorance, since knowledge and ignorance oppose one another. If the Self is the source of knowledge, how could ignorance arise in it? Nor is it reasonable that ignorance should be produced by the Self, whose nature is immutable and whose reality is established by itself, independently of ignorance. What, then, is the object of this ignorance belonging to the Self? We say: the Self itself. One may object that ignorance is impossible because the Self is knowledge itself, is not other than knowledge, and is the source of knowledge. It is possible. How?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 4
units.translation: The division [between Self and not-Self] is caused only by ignorance, as the snake-appearance is caused by a rope.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 5
units.deva: तस्मात्तदपनुत्तौ द्वैतानर्थाभावः । तदपनोदश्च वाक्यादेव तत्पदपदार्थाभिज्ञस्य । अतो वाक्यव्याख्यानायाध्याय आरभ्यते । तत्र यथोक्तेन प्रकारेण तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्योपनिविष्टपदपदार्थयोः कृतान्वयव्यतिरेकः ।
units.iast: tasmāttadapanuttau dvaitānarthābhāvaḥ | tadapanodaśca vākyādeva tatpadapadārthābhijñasya | ato vākyavyākhyānāyādhyāya ārabhyate | tatra yathoktena prakāreṇa tattvamasyādivākyopaniviṣṭapadapadārthayoḥ kṛtānvayavyatirekaḥ |
units.translation: When ignorance is removed, there is no harm of duality. Its removal comes from the sentence alone, for one who knows the meanings of its words. Therefore this chapter begins to explain the sentence. The word-meanings in “That thou art” are connected through the agreement and exclusion already described.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.1
units.deva: यदा तत्त्वमस्यादेर्ब्रह्मास्मीत्यवगच्छति । प्रध्वस्ताहंममो नैति तदा गीर्मनसोः सृतिम् ॥ १॥
units.iast: yadā tattvamasyāderbrahmāsmītyavagacchati | pradhvastāhaṃmamo naiti tadā gīrmanasoḥ sṛtim || 1||
units.translation: When someone understands “I am Brahman” as the meaning of texts such as “That thou art,” the notions “I” and “mine” are destroyed, and he goes beyond the reach of words and mind.

gloss.en: from “That thou art” and similar texts

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 8
units.deva: यदैव तदर्थं त्वमर्थेऽवैति तदैवावाक्यार्थतां प्रतिपद्यते गीर्मनसोः सृतिं न प्रतिपद्यत इति । कुत एतद्ध्यवसीयते । यस्मात् ।
units.iast: yadaiva tadarthaṃ tvamarthe'vaiti tadaivāvākyārthatāṃ pratipadyate gīrmanasoḥ sṛtiṃ na pratipadyata iti | kuta etaddhyavasīyate | yasmāt |
units.translation: When he understands the meaning of “That” through the meaning of “thou,” the sentence then passes beyond the course of speech and mind. How is this understood? Because:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.2
units.deva: तत्पदं प्रकृतार्थं स्यात्त्वंपदं प्रत्यगात्मनि । नीलोत्पलवदेताभ्यां दुःख्यनात्मत्ववारणे ॥ २॥
units.iast: tatpadaṃ prakṛtārthaṃ syāttvaṃpadaṃ pratyagātmani | nīlotpalavadetābhyāṃ duḥkhy anātmatvavāraṇe || 2||
units.translation: The word “That” has its stated meaning, while “thou” refers to the inmost Self. Together, as in “blue lotus,” they exclude the direct senses of suffering and not-Selfhood.

gloss.en: in the inmost Self; referring to the inmost Self

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 11
units.deva: एवं कृतान्वयव्यतिरेको वाक्यादेवावाक्यार्थं प्रतिपद्यत इत्युक्तमतस्तद्व्याख्यानाय सूत्रोपन्यासः ।
units.iast: evaṃ kṛtānvayavyatireko vākyādevāvākyārthaṃ pratipadyata ityuktamatastadvyākhyānāya sūtropanyāsaḥ |
units.translation: It has been said that, after agreement and exclusion, the meaning beyond the sentence is understood from the sentence alone. A concise rule is now stated to explain this:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.3
units.translation: There is apposition, a qualifier–qualified relation, and an indicator–indicated relation between the word meanings and the inmost Self.

gloss.en: the relation of qualifier and qualified
the relation of what is indicated and its indicator
between the word meanings and the inmost Self

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 14
units.deva: अस्मिन् सूत्र उपन्यस्ते कश्चिच्चोदयति योऽयं वाक्यार्थप्रतिपत्तौ पूर्वाध्यायेनान्वयव्यतिरेकलक्षणो न्यायः सर्वकर्मसंन्यासपूर्वकोऽभिहितः किमयं विधिपरिप्रापितः किं वा स्वरसत एवात्र पुमान्प्रवर्तत इति । किंचातः । शृणु ।
units.iast: asmin sūtra upanyaste kaściccodayati yo'yaṃ vākyārthapratipattau pūrvādhyāyenānvayavyatirekalakṣaṇo nyāyaḥ sarvakarmasaṃnyāsapūrvako'bhihitaḥ kimayaṃ vidhipariprāpitaḥ kiṃ vā svarasata evātra pumānpravartata iti | kiṃcātaḥ | śṛṇu |
units.translation: When this rule is stated, someone objects: “The method described in the previous chapter—agreement and exclusion, preceded by the renunciation of all action—is required for understanding the sentence. Is a person brought to it by an injunction, or does he engage in it naturally? What follows? Listen.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 15
units.deva: यद्यात्मवस्तुसाक्षात्करणाय विधिपरिप्रापितोऽयं न्यायस्तदावश्यमात्मवस्तुसाक्षात्करणाय व्यावृत्तशुभाशुभकर्मराशिरेकाग्रमना अन्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यां यथोक्ताभ्यामात्मदर्शनं करोति ।
units.iast: yadyātmavastusākṣātkaraṇāya vidhipariprāpito'yaṃ nyāyastadāvaśyamātmavastusākṣātkaraṇāya vyāvṛttaśubhāśubhakarmarāśirekāgramanā anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ yathoktābhyāmātmadarśanaṃ karoti |
units.translation: If this method is enjoined for direct realization of the Self, then a person must turn away from all good and evil actions, make the mind one-pointed, and realize the Self through the agreement and exclusion described above.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 16
units.deva: अपरिसमाप्यात्मदर्शनं ततः प्रच्यवमान आरूढपतितो भवति । यदि पुनर्यदृच्छातः प्रवर्तते तदा न कश्चिद्दोष इति । विधिपरिप्रापित इति ब्रूमो यत आह ।
units.iast: aparisamāpyātmadarśanaṃ tataḥ pracyavamāna ārūḍhapatito bhavati | yadi punaryadṛcchātaḥ pravartate tadā na kaściddoṣa iti | vidhipariprāpita iti brūmo yata āha |
units.translation: If he falls away before completing realization of the Self, he becomes one who has fallen from the path. But if he takes it up by chance, there is no fault. We say it is enjoined, because scripture says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.4
units.translation: One equipped with disciplines such as calm should directly see the Self in the Self, having wholly set aside the “you”—the not-Self—through reasoning by agreement and exclusion.

gloss.en: equipped with calm and the other disciplines

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.5
units.deva: युष्मदर्थे परित्यक्ते पूर्वोक्तैर्हेतुभिः श्रुतिः । वीक्षापन्नस्य कोऽस्मीति तत्त्वमित्याह सौहृदात् ॥ ५॥
units.iast: yuṣmadarthe parityakte pūrvoktairhetubhiḥ śrutiḥ | vīkṣāpannasya ko'smīti tattvamityāha sauhṛdāt || 5||
units.translation: When the meaning of “you” has been wholly set aside for the reasons given above, the Śruti compassionately tells the seeker who asks “Who am I?”: “That thou art.”

gloss.en: of the one who has entered inquiry

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 21
units.deva: अत्रापि चोदयन्ति सांख्याः । शरीरेन्द्रियमनोबुद्धिष्वनात्मस्वात्मेति निस्सन्धिबन्धनं मिथ्याज्ञानमज्ञानं तन्निबन्धनो ह्यात्मनोऽनेकानर्थसंबन्धस्तस्य चान्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यामेव निरस्तत्त्वान्निर्विषयं तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यं प्राप्तम् । तस्माद्वाक्यस्य चैष महिमा योऽयमात्मानात्मनोर्विभाग इति । तन्निराकरणायेदमुच्यते ।
units.iast: atrāpi codayanti sāṃkhyāḥ | śarīrendriyamanobuddhiṣvanātmasvātmeti nissandhibandhanaṃ mithyājñānamajñānaṃ tannibandhano hyātmano'nekānarthasaṃbandhastasya cānvayavyatirekābhyāmeva nirastattvānnirviṣayaṃ tattvamasyādivākyaṃ prāptam | tasmādvākyasya caiṣa mahimā yo'yamātmānātmanorvibhāga iti | tannirākaraṇāyedamucyate |
units.translation: The Sāṃkhyas object: “Ignorance is the unbroken false cognition ‘I am’ regarding what is not-Self—the body, senses, mind, and intellect. The Self’s many connections with misery are rooted in this ignorance, which has been removed by agreement and exclusion. Therefore sentences such as ‘That thou art’ have no object; their only function is to distinguish the Self from not-Self.” This is answered:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.6
units.deva: भेदसंविदिदं ज्ञानं भेदाभावश्च साक्षिणि । कार्यमेतदविद्याया ज्ञात्मना त्याजयेद्वचः ॥ ६॥
units.iast: bhedasaṃvididaṃ jñānaṃ bhedābhāvaśca sākṣiṇi | kāryametadavidyāyā jñātmanā tyājayedvacaḥ || 6||
units.translation: Cognition of difference—and even the thought “there is no difference in the Witness”—is an effect of ignorance. The teaching should lead one to relinquish it through knowledge of the Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 24
units.translation: On hearing the words “a sentence removes them through knowledge of the Self,” someone asks:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 25
units.deva: मिथ्याज्ञानव्यतिरेकेणात्मानवबोधस्याभावात्किं वाक्येन निवर्तते । अज्ञानं हि नाम ज्ञानाभावस्तस्य चावस्तुस्वाभाव्यात्कुतः संसारकारणत्वं न ह्यसतः सज्जन्मेष्यते "कुतस्तु खलु सोम्यैवं स्यात् " इति "कथमसतः सज्जायेत " इति श्रुतेरिति । अत्रोच्यते ।
units.iast: mithyājñānavyatirekeṇātmānavabodhasyābhāvātkiṃ vākyena nivartate | ajñānaṃ hi nāma jñānābhāvastasya cāvastusvābhāvyātkutaḥ saṃsārakāraṇatvaṃ na hyasataḥ sajjanmeṣyate "kutastu khalu somyaivaṃ syāt " iti "kathamasataḥ sajjāyeta " iti śruteriti | atrocyate |
units.translation: “Apart from false cognition, there is no separate ignorance of the Self; what, then, is removed by the sentence? Ignorance is merely the absence of knowledge, and, being unreal, how could it cause saṃsāra? What is unreal does not give birth to what is real. Scripture says, ‘How could this be so, dear one?’ and ‘How could the real arise from the unreal?’” The answer is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.7
units.deva: अज्ञात एव सर्वोऽर्थः प्राग्यतो बुद्धिजन्मनः । एकेनैव सता संश्च सन्नज्ञातो भवेत्ततः ॥ ७॥
units.iast: ajñāta eva sarvo'rthaḥ prāgyato buddhijanmanaḥ | ekenaiva satā saṃśca sannajñāto bhavettataḥ || 7||
units.translation: Every object is unknown before a cognition of it arises; yet, as an existent, it exists through the one Being. That one reality is therefore what remains unknown.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 28
units.translation: The previous verse has said that what exists may yet be unknown.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 29
units.translation: When one asks, “What is that existent yet unknown thing?”, its nature is stated:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.8
units.deva: प्रमित्सायां य आभाति स्वयं मातृप्रमाणयोः । स्वमहिम्ना च यस्सिद्धः सोऽज्ञातार्थोऽवसीयताम् ॥ ८॥
units.iast: pramitsāyāṃ ya ābhāti svayaṃ mātṛpramāṇayoḥ | svamahimnā ca yassiddhaḥ so'jñātārtho'vasīyatām || 8||
units.translation: When one seeks to know, the Self shines by itself in both the knower and the means of knowing, and is established by its own power. Understand it as the reality that remains unknown.

gloss.en: when there is a desire to know
in the knower and the means of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 32
units.deva: अत्र केचिदाहुः । यत्किंचिदिह वाक्यं लौकिकं वैदिकं वा तत्सर्वं संसर्गात्मकमेव वाक्यार्थं गमयति ।
units.iast: atra kecidāhuḥ | yatkiṃcidiha vākyaṃ laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ vā tatsarvaṃ saṃsargātmakameva vākyārthaṃ gamayati |
units.translation: Some say that every sentence, whether worldly or Vedic, conveys a meaning based on relation.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 33
units.deva: अतस्तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्येभ्यः संसर्गात्मकमहं ब्रह्मेति विज्ञाय तावन्निदिध्यासीत यावदवाक्यार्थात्मकः प्रत्यगात्मविषयोऽवबोधोऽहं ब्रह्मेति समभिजायते ।
units.iast: atastattvamasyādivākyebhyaḥ saṃsargātmakamahaṃ brahmeti vijñāya tāvannididhyāsīta yāvadavākyārthātmakaḥ pratyagātmaviṣayo'vabodho'haṃ brahmeti samabhijāyate |
units.translation: Therefore, from sentences such as “That thou art,” one first understands the relational meaning “I am Brahman,” then meditates until direct knowledge of the inward Self arises, beyond the meaning of the sentence.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 34
units.translation: They say liberation is attained from that very knowledge. To refute this, it is said:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.9
units.translation: Through exclusion of apposition and related connections, as with pot-space and the space beyond it, the direct meaning of “That” and “thou” becomes clear to us as what no sentence can express.

gloss.en: of apposition and the other relations
of pot-space and space beyond the pot
what is not the meaning of a sentence

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 37
units.translation: If one asks how a meaning beyond relation is understood, the power of qualifier and qualified is explained:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.10
units.deva: निर्दुःखित्वं त्वमर्थस्य तदर्थेन विशेषणात् । प्रत्यक्ता च तदर्थस्य त्वंपदेनास्य संनिधेः ॥ १०॥
units.iast: nirduḥkhitvaṃ tvamarthasya tadarthena viśeṣaṇāt | pratyaktā ca tadarthasya tvaṃpadenāsya saṃnidheḥ || 10||
units.translation: The word “That” qualifies “thou” as free from suffering; the word “thou,” by its presence, conveys that the meaning of “That” is the inmost Self.

gloss.en: because of its presence beside it

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 40
units.translation: Apposition and the relation between qualifier and qualified have been stated briefly; he now explains what is indicated and its indication:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.11
units.translation: The Self’s changeless awareness and inwardness are natural, not accidental. They are the basis of the intellect’s knowership and ego-sense; through them the Self is figuratively indicated as “knower” and “I.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 43
units.deva: बुद्धेः कूटस्थबोधप्रत्यक्त्वनिमित्ते बोद्धृताप्रत्यक्त्वे ये त्वसाधारणे तयोर्विशेषवचनम् ।
units.iast: buddheḥ kūṭasthabodhapratyaktvanimitte boddhṛtāpratyaktve ye tvasādhāraṇe tayorviśeṣavacanam |
units.translation: The intellect’s inwardness is due to changeless awareness; its distinctive features—knowing and the sense of “I”—are explained:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.12
units.deva: बोद्धृता कर्तृता बुद्धेः कर्मता स्यादहन्तया । तयोरैक्यं यथा बुद्धौ पूर्वयोरेवमात्मनि ॥ १२॥
units.iast: boddhṛtā kartṛtā buddheḥ karmatā syādahaṃtayā | tayoraikyaṃ yathā buddhau pūrvayorevamātmani || 12||
units.translation: The intellect’s knowership is a kind of agency, and through the “I”-sense it is an object. Just as these two are joined in the intellect, their counterparts are one in the Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 46
units.deva: यथा बुद्धौ पूर्वयोरेवमात्मनीत्यतिदेशेन बुद्धिसाधर्म्य विधानान्नानात्वप्रसक्तौ तदपवादार्थमाह ।
units.iast: yathā buddhau pūrvayorevamātmanītyatideśena buddhisādharmya vidhānānnānātvaprasaktau tadapavādārthamāha |
units.translation: Since the comparison would imply that the Self shares the intellect’s properties and is therefore many, he rejects that implication:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.13
units.deva: धर्मधर्मित्वभेदोऽस्याः सोऽपि नैवात्मनो यतः । प्रत्यग्ज्योतिरतोऽभिन्नं भेदहेतोरसंभवात् ॥ १३॥
units.iast: dharmadharmitvabhedo'syāḥ so'pi naivātmanaḥ yataḥ | pratyagjyotirato'bhinnaṃ bhedahetorasaṃbhavāt || 13||
units.translation: The distinction between a quality and its bearer belongs to the intellect, not the Self. The Self is therefore an undivided inward light, since no cause of division exists.

gloss.en: the distinction between a property and its bearer

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 49
units.translation: He shows that there is no cause of division:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.14
units.deva: न कस्यांचिदवस्थायां बोधप्रत्यक्त्वयोर्भिदा । व्यभिचारोऽथवा दृष्टो यथाहन्तद्विदोस्सदा ॥ १४॥
units.iast: na kasyāṃcidavasthāyāṃ bodhapratyaktvayorbhidā | vyabhicāro'thavā dṛṣṭo yathāhantadvidossadā || 14||
units.translation: Awareness and inwardness are not separate in any state. Variation is seen instead between the “I” and the one who knows that “I.”

gloss.en: between the “I” and the knower of it

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 52
units.translation: Since only the intellect, produced by ignorance, is divided and not the Self, this is established:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.15
units.deva: कूटस्थबोधतोऽद्वैतं साक्षात्त्वं प्रत्यगात्मनः । कूटस्थबोधाद्बोद्ध्री धीः स्वतो हीयं विनश्वरी ॥ १५॥
units.iast: kūṭasthabodhato'dvaitaṃ sākṣāttvaṃ pratyagātmanaḥ | kūṭasthabodhādboddhrī dhīḥ svato hīyaṃ vinaśvarī || 15||
units.translation: Because the inmost Self is changeless awareness, it is directly present and non-dual. The intellect functions as a knower through that same changeless awareness, though it is perishable in itself.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 55
units.deva: अथाधुना प्रकृतस्यैव परिणामिनः कूटस्थस्य च लक्षणमुच्यते ।
units.iast: athādhunā prakṛtasyaiva pariṇāminaḥ kūṭasthasya ca lakṣaṇamucyate |
units.translation: The changing and the changeless, which are under discussion, are now defined.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.16
units.deva: विशेषं कंचिदाश्रित्य यत्स्वरूपं प्रतीयते । प्रत्यभिज्ञाप्रमाणेन परिणामी स देहवत् ॥ १६॥
units.iast: viśeṣaṃ kaṃcidāśritya yatsvarūpaṃ pratīyate | pratyabhijñāpramāṇena pariṇāmī sa dehavat || 16||
units.translation: That whose nature is known by reference to a particular feature—such as “I am happy” or “I am sad”—is changing like the body; this is established through recognition.

gloss.en: through recognition as a means of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.17
units.deva: सामान्याच्च विशेषाच्च स्वमहिम्नैव यो भवेत् । व्युत्थायाप्यविकारी स्यात्कुम्भाकाशादिवत्तु सः ॥ १७॥
units.iast: sāmānyācca viśeṣācca svamahimnaiva yo bhavet | vyutthāyāpyavikārī syātkumbhākāśādivattu saḥ || 17||
units.translation: That which exists in its own incomparable power, beyond both generality and particularity, remains changeless even after emerging, like the space within pots.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 60
units.translation: The inward awareness of both the Self and the intellect has been stated; their distinctive marks are now given:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.18
units.deva: बुद्धेर्यत्प्रत्यगात्मत्वं तत्स्याद्देहाद्युपाश्रयात् । आत्मनस्तु स्वरूपं तन्नभसः सुषिता यथा ॥ १८॥
units.iast: buddheryatpratyagātmatvaṃ tatsyāddehādyupāśrayāt | ātmanastu svarūpaṃ tannabhasaḥ suṣitā yathā || 18||
units.translation: The intellect’s inwardness depends on the body and the rest; the Self’s inwardness is its very nature, as hollowness is the nature of space.

gloss.en: because it depends on the body and the rest

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.19
units.deva: बोद्धृत्वं तद्वदेवास्याः प्रत्ययोत्पत्तिहेतुतः । आत्मनस्तु स्वरूपं तत्तिष्ठन्तीव महीभृतः ॥ १९॥
units.iast: boddhṛtvaṃ tadvadevāsyāḥ pratyayotpattihetutaḥ | ātmanastu svarūpaṃ tattiṣṭhantīva mahībhṛtaḥ || 19||
units.translation: The intellect is a knower because it causes cognitions to arise. The Self’s own nature, by contrast, remains as it is, like mountains standing firm.

gloss.en: because it is the cause of cognitions arising

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 65
units.deva: तयोः कूटस्थपरिणामिनोरात्मानवबोध एव संबन्धहेतुर्न पुनर्वास्तवः कश्चिदपि संबन्ध उपपद्यत इत्याह ।
units.iast: tayoḥ kūṭasthapariṇāminorātmānavabodha eva saṃbandhaheturna punarvāstavaḥ kaścidapi saṃbandha upapadyata ityāha |
units.translation: Ignorance alone is the supposed link between the changeless Self and the changing intellect; no real connection between them is possible.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.20
units.translation: The intellect alone is divided into right, doubtful, and false cognitions. Through delusion, the Seer is made to seem to accept and reject these changing states.

gloss.en: the character of rejection and acceptance

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 68
units.translation: If one asks how the changeless Self is established, it is because:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.21
units.deva:
न हानं हानमात्रेण नोदयोऽपीयता यतः ।
तत्सिद्धिः स्यात्तु तद्धीने हानादानविधर्मके ॥ २१॥
units.iast:
na hānaṃ hānamātreṇa nodayo'pīyatā yataḥ |
tatsiddhiḥ syāttu taddhīne hānādānavidharmake || 21||
units.translation: The loss of a cognition cannot be known by that loss alone, nor its arising by that arising; both are established in what is distinct from taking up and laying down.

gloss.en: by that much; through that alone
in what is free of those changes
distinct in nature from loss and taking up

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 71
units.translation: Thus:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.22
units.deva:
आगमापायिहेतुभ्यां धूत्वा सर्वाननात्मनः ।
ततस्तत्त्वमसीत्येतद्धन्त्यस्मदि निजं तमः ॥ २२॥
units.iast:
āgamāpāyihetubhyāṃ dhūtvā sarvānanātmanaḥ |
tatastattvamasītyetaddhantyasmadi nijaṃ tamaḥ || 22||
units.translation: Having rejected all the not-Selves by reasoning about what arises and passes away, the sentence “That thou art” then destroys our own ignorance.

gloss.en: by the two reasons concerning arising and passing away

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 74
units.deva: इत्यादि पुनःपुनरुच्यते ग्रन्थलाघवाद्बुद्धिलाघवं प्रयोजकमिति । तत्र यद्यपि तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यादुपादित्सिताद्वितीयात्मार्थवत्पारोक्ष्यसद्वितीयार्थः प्रतीयते ।
units.iast: ityādi punaḥpunarucyate granthalāghavādbuddhilāghavaṃ prayojakamiti | tatra yadyapi tattvamasyādivākyādupāditsitādvitīyātmārthavatpārokṣyasadvitīyārthaḥ pratīyate |
units.translation: This point is repeated again and again because the brevity of the treatise is meant to aid understanding. Although “That thou art” may appear to convey both the intended non-dual Self and a remote, dual meaning,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 75
units.deva: तथापि तु नैवासावर्थः श्रुत्या तात्पर्येण प्रतिपिपादयिषितः प्रागपेतस्य प्रतीतत्वादितीममर्थमाह ।
units.iast: tathāpi tu naivāsāvarthaḥ śrutyā tātparyeṇa pratipipādayiṣitaḥ prāgapetasya pratītatvāditīmamarthamāha |
units.translation: that remote meaning is not what revelation intends, since it has already been understood before the sentence. He says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.23
units.deva:
तदित्येतत्पदं लोके बह्वर्थप्रतिपादकम् ।
अपरित्यज्य पारोक्ष्यमभिधानोत्थमेव तत् ॥ २३॥
units.iast:
tadityetatpadaṃ loke bahvarthapratipādakam |
aparityajya pārokṣyamabhidhānotthameva tat || 23||
units.translation: In ordinary usage, the word “That” conveys many meanings, yet it keeps the remoteness that arises from the word itself.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.24
units.deva:
त्वमित्यपि पदं तद्वत्साक्षान्मात्रार्थवाचि तु ।
संसारितामसंत्यज्य सापि स्यादभिधानजा ॥ २४॥
units.iast:
tvamityapi padaṃ tadvatsākṣānmātrārthavāci tu |
saṃsāritāmasaṃtyajya sāpi syādabhidhānajā || 24||
units.translation: Likewise, “thou” directly refers only to someone immediately present; without setting aside transmigrant identity, that too is produced by the word.

gloss.en: expressing only an immediately present referent

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 80
units.translation: Since remoteness and suffering are contradictory purposes, they are not intended here. He says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.25
units.deva:
उद्दिश्यमानं वाक्यस्थं नोद्देशनगुणात्वितम् ।
आकाङ्क्षितपदार्थेन संसर्गं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ २५॥
units.iast:
uddiśyamānaṃ vākyasthaṃ noddeśanaguṇātvitam |
ākāṅkṣitapadārthena saṃsargaṃ pratipadyate || 25||
units.translation: What a sentence intends is not endowed with the qualities of a word’s direct denotation; it connects with the meaning the sentence requires.

gloss.en: endowed with the quality of direct denotation
with the meaning of the expected word

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 83
units.translation: Since this is so, even though the meanings of “that” and “thou” are not directly asserted in their contradictory forms, their relation as qualifier and qualified serves only to reveal the sentence meaning, which is free of a relation between separate things. This is the conclusion.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.26
units.deva:
तदो विशेषणार्थत्वं विशेष्यत्वं त्वमस्तथा ।
लक्ष्यलक्षणसंबन्धस्तयोः स्यात्प्रत्यगात्मना ॥ २६॥
units.iast:
tado viśeṣaṇārthatvaṃ viśeṣyatvaṃ tvamastathā |
lakṣyalakṣaṇasaṃbandhastayoḥ syātpratyagātmanā || 26||
units.translation: “That” has the force of a qualifier, while “thou” is what is qualified; their relation as indicator and indicated is through the innermost Self.

gloss.en: having the force of a qualifier
relation of what is indicated to its indicator

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 86
units.translation: How can the meaning of an indicator be something whose contradictory, unintended sense is being negated?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.27
units.deva:
लक्षणं सर्पवद्रज्ज्वाः प्रतीचः स्यादहं तथा ।
तद्बाधेनैव वाक्यार्थं वेत्ति सोऽपि तदाश्रयात् ॥ २७॥
units.iast:
lakṣaṇaṃ sarpavadrajjvāḥ pratīcaḥ syādahaṃ tathā |
tadbādhenaiva vākyārthaṃ vetti so'pi tadāśrayāt || 27||
units.translation: “I” indicates the innermost Self as a false snake indicates a rope; by correcting that mistaken appearance, one understands the sentence’s meaning, which itself rests on that reality.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 89
units.translation: This understanding of the sentence meaning belongs to one who knows agreement and difference through presence and absence.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 90
units.translation: For this reason:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.28
units.translation: The more this person turns inward, negating the body and the rest, the more the meaning of “That” enters the meaning of “thou.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 93
units.deva: कस्मात्पुनः कारणाद्देहाद्यनात्मत्वप्रतिपत्तावेवात्मा तदर्थमात्मत्वेनाभिलिङ्गते न विपर्यय इति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: kasmātpunaḥ kāraṇāddehādyanātmatvapratipattāvevātmā tadarthamātmatvenābhiliṅgate na viparyaya iti | ucyate |
units.translation: Why, when one recognizes the body and the rest as not-Self, is the Self marked out as the meaning of “that” by its very Selfhood, and not the reverse? The answer is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 94
units.deva: प्रत्यगात्मानवबोधस्यनात्मस्वाभाव्यात्तदभिनिर्वृत्तश्चायं बुद्ध्यादिदेहान्तस्तस्मिन्नात्मत्वमविद्याकृतमेवात्मत्वमिवानात्मत्वमपि साविद्यस्यैव । यतो निरविद्यो विद्वानवाक्यार्थरूप एव केवलोऽवशिष्यते तस्मादुच्यते ।
units.iast: pratyagātmānavabodhasyanātmasvābhāvyāttadabhinirvṛttaścāyaṃ buddhyādidehāntastasminnātmatvamavidyākṛtamevātmatvamivānātmatvamapi sāvidyasyaiva | yato niravidyo vidvānavākyārtharūpa eva kevalo'vaśiṣyate tasmāducyate |
units.translation: Because the innermost Self is not recognized, the mind and everything down to the body arise as not-Self; Selfhood attributed to them is created by ignorance. For one still under ignorance, even their apparent not-Selfhood is likewise bound up with ignorance. Once ignorance is gone, the knower remains alone as the very meaning of the sentence, beyond direct designation. Therefore it is said:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.29
units.deva:
देहादिव्यवधानत्वात्तदर्थं स्वयमप्यतः ।
पारोक्ष्येणैव जानाति साक्षात्त्वं तदनात्मनः ॥ २९॥
units.iast:
dehādivyavadhānatvāttadarthaṃ svayamapyataḥ |
pārokṣyeṇaiva jānāti sākṣāttvaṃ tadanātmanaḥ || 29||
units.translation: Because the body and the rest stand between, one knows the meaning of “That” only indirectly, even though it is oneself; what is not-Self appears immediate.

gloss.en: because the body and the rest intervene

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 97
units.translation: An example is offered to make the stated point easier to understand.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.30
units.deva:
प्रत्यगुद्भुतपित्तस्य यथा बाह्यार्थपीतता ।
चैतन्यं प्रत्यगात्मीयं बहिर्वद्दृश्यते तथा ॥ ३०॥
units.iast:
pratyagudbhutapittasya yathā bāhyārthapītatā |
caitanyaṃ pratyagātmīyaṃ bahirvaddṛśyate tathā || 30||
units.translation: Just as, when bile arises within, an external object appears yellow, so the consciousness belonging to the innermost Self appears to be outside.

gloss.en: the yellowness of an external object

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 100
units.translation: Since this is so, understand the point clearly:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.31
units.deva:
पदान्युद्धृत्य वाक्येभ्यो ह्यन्वयव्यतिरेकतः ।
पदार्थांल्लोकतो बुद्ध्वा वेत्ति वाक्यार्थमञ्जसा ॥ ३१॥
units.iast:
padānyuddhṛtya vākyebhyo hyanvayavyatirekataḥ |
padārthāṃllokato buddhvā vetti vākyārthamañjasā || 31||
units.translation: By drawing words out of sentences and noting what is present and absent, one learns their meanings from ordinary usage and readily understands the sentence meaning.

gloss.en: through agreement and difference; presence and absence

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 103
units.deva: कुतः पुनः सामान्यमात्रवृत्तेः पदस्य वाक्यार्थप्रतिपत्तिहेतुत्वमिति । बाढम् ।
units.iast: kutaḥ punaḥ sāmānyamātravṛtteḥ padasya vākyārthapratipattihetutvamiti | bāḍham |
units.translation: How can a word, which applies only to a general meaning, serve as a means of understanding the meaning of a sentence? The reply is: Certainly it can.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.32
units.deva:
सामान्यं हि पदं ब्रूते विशेषो वाक्यकर्तृकः ।
श्रुत्यादिप्रतिबद्धं सद्विशेषार्थं भवेत्पदम् ॥ ३२॥
units.iast:
sāmānyaṃ hi padaṃ brūte viśeṣo vākyakartṛkaḥ |
śrutyādipratibaddhaṃ sadviśeṣārthaṃ bhavetpadam || 32||
units.translation: A word expresses a general meaning; a particular meaning is supplied by the sentence. When scripture and other context constrain it, a word conveys a specific meaning.

gloss.en: constrained by scripture and other context

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 106
units.deva: अन्वयव्यतिरेकपुरस्सरं वाक्यमेव सामानाधिकरण्यादिनाविद्या पटलप्रध्वंसद्वारेण मुमुक्षुं स्वाराज्येऽभिषेचयति न त्वन्वयव्यतिरेकमात्रसाध्योऽयमर्थ इत्याह ।
units.iast: anvayavyatirekapurassaraṃ vākyameva sāmānādhikaraṇyādināvidyā paṭalapradhvaṃsadvāreṇa mumukṣuṃ svārājye'bhiṣecayati na tvanvayavyatirekamātrasādhyo'yamartha ityāha |
units.translation: It is the sentence itself, using co-reference and the like, preceded by reasoning through agreement and difference, that destroys the veil of ignorance and enthrones the seeker in his own sovereignty. This meaning is not established by agreement and difference alone, as the following verse says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.33
units.deva:
बुद्ध्यादीनामनात्मत्वं लिङ्गादपि च सिध्यति ।
निवृत्तिस्तावता नेतीत्यतो वाक्यं समाश्रयेत् ॥ ३३॥
units.iast:
buddhyādīnāmanātmatvaṃ liṅgādapi ca sidhyati |
nivṛttistāvatā netītyato vākyaṃ samāśrayet || 33||
units.translation: Reasoning can also establish that the intellect and the rest are not the Self. That alone does not bring cessation; therefore one should rely on the scriptural sentence “not this.”

gloss.en: of the intellect and the rest

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 109
units.translation: He says that one who relies on inference alone not only fails to attain the desired meaning but also falls into error:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.34
units.deva:
अनादृत्य श्रुतिं मोहादतो बौद्धास्तमस्विनः ।
आपेदिरे निरात्मत्वमनुमानैकचक्षुषः ॥ ३४॥
units.iast:
anādṛtya śrutiṃ mohādato bauddhāstamasvinaḥ |
āpedire nirātmatvamanumānaikacakṣuṣaḥ || 34||
units.translation: Through delusion, the Buddhists who disregard scripture, darkened by ignorance, reach the doctrine that there is no Self, with inference as their only eye.

gloss.en: the doctrine that there is no Self
those whose only eye is inference

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 112
units.deva: न चानादरे कारणमस्ति । यस्मात्सर्वत्रैवानादरनिमित्तं प्रमाणस्य प्रमाणान्तरप्रतिपन्नप्रतिपादनं वा विपरीतप्रतिपादनं वा संशयितप्रतिपादनं वा न वा प्रतिपादनमिति -- न चैतेषामन्यतमदपि कारणमस्ति ।
units.iast: na cānādare kāraṇamasti | yasmātsarvatraivānādaranimittaṃ pramāṇasya pramāṇāntarapratipannapratipādanaṃ vā viparītapratipādanaṃ vā saṃśayitapratipādanaṃ vā na vā pratipādanamiti -- na caiteṣāmanyatamadapi kāraṇamasti |
units.translation: There is no reason to disregard scripture. A means of knowledge may be set aside if it merely repeats what another means has established, teaches the opposite, leaves its result doubtful, or yields no result. None of these is the case here.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 113
units.translation: For scripture says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.35
units.deva:
मानान्तरानवष्टब्धं निर्दुःख्यात्मानमञ्जसा ।
बोधयन्ती श्रुतिः केन न प्रमाणमितीर्यते ॥ ३५॥
units.iast:
mānāntarānavaṣṭabdhaṃ nirduḥkhyātmānamañjasā |
bodhayantī śrutiḥ kena na pramāṇamitīryate || 35||
units.translation: The scripture directly reveals the sorrowless Self, not grasped by any other means of knowledge; on what ground, then, is it called an invalid means?

gloss.en: not grasped by any other means of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 116
units.translation: Nor does it leave the matter uncertain, because:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.36
units.deva:
सर्वसंशयहेतौ हि निरस्ते कथमात्मनि ।
जायेत संशयो वाक्यादनुमानेन युष्मदि ॥ ३६॥
units.iast:
sarvasaṃśayahetau hi niraste kathamātmani |
jāyeta saṃśayo vākyādanumānena yuṣmadi || 36||
units.translation: Once every cause of doubt has been removed, how could doubt about the Self arise from scripture, when inference concerns the “you”—what is other than the Self?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 119
units.translation: Moreover:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.37
units.deva:
यत्र स्यात्संशयो नासौ ज्ञेय आत्मेति पण्डितैः ।
न यतः संशयप्राप्तिरात्मनोऽवगतित्वतः ॥ ३७॥
units.iast:
yatra syātsaṃśayo nāsau jñeya ātmeti paṇḍitaiḥ |
na yataḥ saṃśayaprāptirātmano'vagatitvataḥ || 37||
units.translation: Wherever doubt can arise, the wise know that this is not the Self; no doubt can arise about the Self because awareness is its nature.

gloss.en: because it is awareness; directly known

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 122
units.translation: That scripture is unable to reveal the Self has already been ruled out completely. For it says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.38
units.deva:
बोधेऽप्यनुभवो यस्य न कथंचन जायते ।
तं कथं बोधयेच्छास्त्रं लोष्टं नरसमाकृतिम् ॥ ३८॥
units.iast:
bodhe'pyanubhavo yasya na kathaṃcana jāyate |
taṃ kathaṃ bodhayecchāstraṃ loṣṭaṃ narasamākṛtim || 38||
units.translation: For someone in whom direct experience never arises even when awareness is present, how could scripture awaken him? He would be a clod of earth shaped like a person.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 125
units.deva: अन्वयव्यतिरेकपुरस्सरं वाक्यमेवावाक्यार्थरूपमात्मानं प्रतिपादयतीत्यस्य पक्षस्य द्रढिम्न श्रुत्युदाहरणमुपन्यस्यति ।
units.iast: anvayavyatirekapurassaraṃ vākyamevāvākyārtharūpamātmānaṃ pratipādayatītyasya pakṣasya draḍhimna śrutyudāharaṇamupanyasyati |
units.translation: To strengthen the view that the sentence of scripture, preceded by reasoning through agreement and difference, teaches the Self beyond ordinary sentence meaning, he gives a scriptural example:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.39
units.deva:
जिघ्राणीममहं गन्धमिति यो वेत्त्यविक्रियः ।
स आत्मा तत्परं ज्योतिः शिरसीदं वचः श्रुतेः ॥ ३९॥
units.iast:
jighrāṇīmamahaṃ gandhamiti yo vettyavikriyaḥ |
sa ātmā tatparaṃ jyotiḥ śirasīdaṃ vacaḥ śruteḥ || 39||
units.translation: The changeless one who knows the thought “Let me smell this fragrance” is the Self, the supreme Light; these are the crowning words of scripture.

gloss.en: at the head; as the crown

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 128
units.deva: यथा "तत्सत्यं स आत्मा तत्त्वमसि " इत्यस्य शेषत्वेनान्वयव्यतिरेकश्रुतिर्यथा "य एषोऽक्षिणिपुरुषो दृश्यते " इत्याद्या "अथ यो वेदेदं जिघ्राणि " इत्यन्ता तथा "अहं ब्रह्मास्मि " इत्यस्य शेषः ।
units.iast: yathā "tatsatyaṃ sa ātmā tattvamasi " ityasya śeṣatvenānvayavyatirekaśrutiryathā "ya eṣo'kṣiṇipuruṣo dṛśyate " ityādyā "atha yo vededaṃ jighrāṇi " ityantā tathā "ahaṃ brahmāsmi " ityasya śeṣaḥ |
units.translation: Just as the teaching “That is the real; that is the Self; you are that” is clarified by the passages on agreement and difference beginning “the person seen in the eye” and ending “now, the one who knows ‘I smell this’,” so too those passages explain “I am Brahman.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.40
units.deva:
अहमः प्रत्यगात्मार्थो निरस्ताशेषयुष्मदः ।
बम्भणीति श्रुतिर्न्याय्या योऽयमित्यादिनाऽसकृत् ॥ ४०॥
units.iast:
ahamaḥ pratyagātmārtho nirastāśeṣayuṣmadaḥ |
bambhaṇīti śrutirnyāyyā yo'yamityādinā'sakṛt || 40||
units.translation: When every meaning of “you”—all that is not-Self—has been removed, the meaning of “I” is the innermost Self. Scripture repeatedly and fittingly declares this in passages beginning “He who is this one.”

gloss.en: the meaning is the innermost Self
by the passage beginning with it and the like

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 131
units.deva: कथं पुनरयमर्थोऽवसीयते अहंव्याजेनात्रात्मार्थो बुबोधयिषित इति । यतः ।
units.iast: kathaṃ punarayamartho'vasīyate ahaṃvyājenātrātmārtho bubodhayiṣita iti | yataḥ |
units.translation: How is it established that the intended meaning of the word “I” here is the Self? Because:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.41
units.deva:
एष आत्मा स्वयंज्योती रविसोमाग्निवाक्षु सः ।
इतेष्वस्तं दृगेवास्ते भासयंचित्तचेष्टितम् ॥ ४१॥
units.iast:
eṣa ātmā svayaṃjyotī ravisomāgnivākṣu saḥ |
iteṣvastaṃ dṛgevāste bhāsayaṃcittaceṣṭitam || 41||
units.translation: This is the Self, self-luminous. When the sun, moon, fire, and speech have set, this Seer alone remains, illuminating the activity of the mind.

gloss.en: in the sun, moon, fire, and speech

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 134
units.translation: The sage explains the point in response to a question:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.42
units.deva:
आत्मनैवेत्युपश्रुत्य कोऽयमात्मेत्युदीरिते ।
बुद्धेः परं स्वतोमुक्तमात्मानं मुनिरभ्यधात् ॥ ४२॥
units.iast:
ātmanaivetyupaśrutya ko'yamātmetyudīrite |
buddheḥ paraṃ svatomuktamātmānaṃ munirabhyadhāt || 42||
units.translation: Having heard “by the Self alone,” when asked “What is this Self?”, the sage described the Self as beyond the intellect and free by its own nature.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 137
units.deva: यस्माच्चात्मात्राहंव्याजेन प्रत्यङ्मात्रो जिग्राहयिषितस्तस्मादहंवृत्तिः स्वरूपस्य विलयेनैव वाक्यार्थावगमाय कारणत्वं प्रतिपद्यत इतीममर्थमाह ।
units.iast: yasmāccātmātrāhaṃvyājena pratyaṅmātro jigrāhayiṣitastasmādahaṃvṛttiḥ svarūpasya vilayenaiva vākyārthāvagamāya kāraṇatvaṃ pratipadyata itīmamarthamāha |
units.translation: Because the Self meant here by “I” is intended to be understood as the innermost witness alone, the “I”-thought serves to reveal the sentence meaning only by dissolving into its own true nature. This is expressed in the following verse:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.43
units.deva:
अहंवृत्त्यैव तद्ब्रह्म यस्मादेषोऽवगच्छति ।
तत्स्वरूपलयेनातः कारणं स्यादहंकृतिः ॥ ४३॥
units.iast:
ahaṃvṛttyaiva tadbrahma yasmādeṣo'vagacchati |
tatsvarūpalayenātaḥ kāraṇaṃ syādahaṃkṛtiḥ || 43||
units.translation: Since this seeker understands that Brahman through the “I”-thought alone, the ego serves as the means by dissolving into that reality’s own nature.

gloss.en: by dissolving into that reality’s own nature

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 140
units.deva: अत एव च यः प्रतिज्ञातोऽर्थो "नाहंग्राह्ये न तद्धीने "इत्यादिः स युक्तिभिरुपपादित इति कृत्वोपसंह्रियते ।
units.iast: ata eva ca yaḥ pratijñāto'rtho "nāhaṃgrāhye na taddhīne "ityādiḥ sa yuktibhirupapādita iti kṛtvopasaṃhriyate |
units.translation: Thus the point stated earlier—that the Self is not grasped as an object, nor dependent on an object—is established by reasoning. The author concludes:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.44
units.translation: If the meaning of “I” has been grasped, why does the knower not attain the Self? If you say it conflicts with perception and other means of knowledge, the teaching about the inward Self is not speaking about the outward “you.”

gloss.en: when the meaning of “I” has been grasped
because of conflict with perception and the rest
the teaching about the inward Self

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 143
units.translation: He clarifies the meaning of the preceding verse:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.45
units.deva:
पराञ्च्येव तु सर्वाणि प्रत्यक्षादीनि नात्मनि ।
प्रतीच्येव प्रवृत्तं तत्सदसीति वचोऽञ्जसा ॥ ४५॥
units.iast:
parāñcyeva tu sarvāṇi pratyakṣādīni nātmani |
pratīcyeva pravṛttaṃ tatsadasīti vaco'ñjasā || 45||
units.translation: Perception and the other means of knowledge are directed outward, not toward the Self; the statement “You are That Reality” is plainly directed inward.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 146
units.translation: Therefore, using agreement and difference, one should separate the Self from the knower, means of knowledge and objects of knowledge that are taken up and discarded, as one draws the pith from a reed. Then, from sentences such as “you are that,” one should know the Self as beyond anything previously established. This is stated here:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.46
units.deva:
अहं दुःखी सुखी चेति येनायं प्रत्ययोऽध्रुवः ।
अवगत्यन्त आभाति स म आत्मेति वाक्यधीः ॥ ४६॥
units.iast:
ahaṃ duḥkhī sukhī ceti yenāyaṃ pratyayo'dhruvaḥ |
avagatyanta ābhāti sa ma ātmeti vākyadhīḥ || 46||
units.translation: The thought “I am unhappy” or “I am happy” is fleeting; what makes it shine and become known is my Self—this is how the sentence is understood.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 149
units.deva: प्रमाणान्तरानवष्टब्धं निरस्ताशेषकार्यकारणात्मकद्वैतप्रपञ्चं सत्यज्ञानानन्दलक्षणमात्मानं तत्त्वमस्यहंब्रह्मास्मीत्यादिवाक्यं संशयितमिथ्याज्ञानाज्ञानप्रध्वंसमुखेन साक्षादपरोक्षात्करतलन्यस्तामलकवत्प्रतिपादयत्येवेत्यसकृदभिहितम् । तत्र केचिदाहुः -- तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यैर्यथावस्थितवस्तुयाथात्म्यान्वाख्याननिष्ठैर्नयथोक्तोऽर्थः प्रतिपत्तुं शक्यतेऽभिधाश्रुतित्वात्तेषाम् ।
units.iast: pramāṇāntarānavaṣṭabdhaṃ nirastāśeṣakāryakāraṇātmakadvaitaprapañcaṃ satyajñānānandalakṣaṇamātmānaṃ tattvamasyahaṃbrahmāsmītyādivākyaṃ saṃśayitamithyājñānājñānapradhvaṃsamukhena sākṣādaparokṣātkaratalanyastāmalakavatpratipādayatyevetyasakṛdabhihitam | tatra kecidāhuḥ -- tattvamasyādivākyairyathāvasthitavastuyāthātmyānvākhyānaniṣṭhairnayathokto'rthaḥ pratipattuṃ śakyate'bhidhāśrutitvātteṣām |
units.translation: It has been said repeatedly that a sentence such as “you are that” or “I am Brahman” does directly reveal the Self—whose nature is reality, awareness and bliss, untouched by any other means of knowledge and free of the entire duality of effects and causes—by removing doubt, false knowledge and ignorance, like a fruit placed in one’s palm. Some object: “Sentences such as ‘you are that,’ which merely describe the nature of an existing thing as it is, cannot reveal the meaning you claim, because they are heard in their literal, declarative sense.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 150
units.deva: न हि लोकेऽभिधाश्रुतेः प्रमाणान्तरनिरपेक्षायानद्यास्तीरे फलानि सन्तीत्यादिकायाः प्रामाण्यमभ्युपगतम् ।
units.iast: na hi loke'bhidhāśruteḥ pramāṇāntaranirapekṣāyānadyāstīre phalāni santītyādikāyāḥ prāmāṇyamabhyupagatam |
units.translation: For in ordinary usage, the authority of a literal statement that needs no other means of knowledge—such as ‘fruit is on the far bank of the river’—is not accepted.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 151
units.deva: अतो नियोगमुखेनैवाभिधाश्रुतेः प्रामाण्यं युक्तं प्रमाणान्तरनिरपेक्षत्वान्नियोगस्य । अस्य परिहारार्थमशेषप्रत्यक्षादिप्रमेयत्वनिराकरणद्वारेणातीन्द्रियार्थविषयत्वादभिधाश्रुतेः प्रामाण्यं सुप्तपुरुषप्रबोधकवाक्यस्येव वक्तव्यमित्ययमारम्भः ।
units.iast: ato niyogamukhenaivābhidhāśruteḥ prāmāṇyaṃ yuktaṃ pramāṇāntaranirapekṣatvānniyogasya | asya parihārārthamaśeṣapratyakṣādiprameyatvanirākaraṇadvāreṇātīndriyārthaviṣayatvādabhidhāśruteḥ prāmāṇyaṃ suptapuruṣaprabodhakavākyasyeva vaktavyamityayamārambhaḥ |
units.translation: They therefore claim that a literal scriptural statement is authoritative only as an injunction, since an injunction does not depend on another means of knowledge. To answer this, the author begins: a literal scriptural statement is authoritative about a supersensible matter, because that matter is not an object of perception and the other means of knowledge—just as a sentence that awakens a sleeping person is authoritative.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.47
units.translation: The Self is the very nature of constant awareness and depends on no other means of knowledge; because it lacks qualities such as sound, doubt cannot arise about it.

gloss.en: because its nature is constant awareness
because it needs no other means of knowledge
because it lacks qualities such as sound

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.48
units.translation: The Self is not known through perception and the other empirical means, which are like what craving spits out; because it is the innermost Self and exists for itself, it cannot be made an object of knowledge.

gloss.en: through perception and the other means
because it is the innermost Self
because it is not an object of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 156
units.translation: Scripture states this same point:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.49
units.deva:
दिदृक्षितपरिच्छिन्नपराग्रूपादिसंश्रयात् ।
विपरीतमतो दृष्ट्या स्वतोबुद्धं न पश्यति ॥ ४९॥
units.iast:
didṛkṣitaparicchinnaparāgrūpādisaṃśrayāt |
viparītamato dṛṣṭyā svatobuddhaṃ na paśyati || 49||
units.translation: Since vision depends on limited, outward, formed things that can be seen, it does not see their opposite: what is self-revealed.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.50
units.deva:
न्यायसिद्धमतो वक्ति दृष्टेर्द्रष्टारमात्मनः ।
न पश्येत्प्रत्यगात्मानं प्रमाणं श्रुतिरादरात् ॥ ५०॥
units.iast:
nyāyasiddhamato vakti dṛṣṭerdraṣṭāramātmanaḥ |
na paśyetpratyagātmānaṃ pramāṇaṃ śrutirādarāt || 50||
units.translation: Reason establishes this, so scripture rightly says that the Self is the seer of seeing. One cannot see the innermost Self as an object; scripture is the authoritative source here.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 161
units.translation: Another reason is given for why the Self is not an object of inference:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.51
units.deva:
प्रत्यक्षस्य पराक्त्वान्न संबन्धग्रहणं यतः ।
आत्मनोऽतोऽनुमित्यास्यानुभवो न कथंचन ॥ ५१॥
units.iast:
pratyakṣasya parāktvānna saṃbandhagrahaṇaṃ yataḥ |
ātmano'to'numityāsyānubhavo na kathaṃcana || 51||
units.translation: Because perception is directed outward, it cannot grasp its relation to the Self; therefore inference can never give direct experience of the Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 164
units.deva: एवमयं प्रमातृप्रमाणप्रमेयव्यवहारः सर्व एव पराचीनविषय एव न प्रतीचिनमात्मानमवगाहयितुमलम् ।
units.iast: evamayaṃ pramātṛpramāṇaprameyavyavahāraḥ sarva eva parācīnaviṣaya eva na pratīcinamātmānamavagāhayitumalam |
units.translation: Thus the entire transaction of knower, means of knowledge and known objects concerns things outward; it cannot reach the inward Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 165
units.deva: एवं च सत्यनेनैव यथोक्तोऽर्थोऽवसातुं शक्यत इत्याह ।
units.iast: evaṃ ca satyanenaiva yathokto'rtho'vasātuṃ śakyata ityāha |
units.translation: Since this is so, the point already explained can be established by this very reasoning:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.52
units.deva:
प्रमाणव्यवहारोऽयं सर्व एव पराग्यतः ।
सुविचार्याप्यतोऽनेन युष्मद्येव दिदृक्षते ॥ ५२॥
units.iast:
pramāṇavyavahāro'yaṃ sarva eva parāgyataḥ |
suvicāryāpyato'nena yuṣmadyeva didṛkṣate || 52||
units.translation: Every operation of the means of knowledge is directed outward; even after careful examination, by this means one seeks only what is other than the Self.

gloss.en: operation of the means of knowledge
in the “you”; what is other than the Self

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 168
units.translation: Since the sentence meaning “I am Brahman” cannot be reached by ordinary perception and the other means of knowledge:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.53
units.deva:
अन्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्यां निरस्याप्राणतो यतेः ।
वीक्षापन्नस्य कोऽस्मीति तदसीति श्रुतिर्जगौ ॥ ५३॥
units.iast:
anvayavyatirekābhyāṃ nirasyāprāṇato yateḥ |
vīkṣāpannasya ko'smīti tadasīti śrutirjagau || 53||
units.translation: To the renunciate who, by reasoning through presence and absence, has set aside everything up to the life-breath and, perplexed, asks “Who am I?”, scripture answers, “You are That.”

gloss.en: through agreement and difference; presence and absence

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 171
units.translation: This reasoning through agreement and difference culminates in the sentence meaning becoming clear to one who understands it: “I am Brahman.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 172
units.translation: The distinction between seer and seen, and between the witness and what arises and subsides, is stated here in a concise form accepted by scripture:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.54
units.translation: Because it is seen, the body is not-Self like a pot; the senses are like the body, the mind is known like the senses, and the intellect with its decisions and the rest is like the mind.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 175
units.translation: The same point follows from the Self’s witnessing all effects and causes as they arise and disappear:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.55
units.deva:
प्रागसद्याति पश्चात्सत्सच्च यायादसत्तथा ।
अनात्माभिजनं तत्स्याद्विपरीतः स्वयं दृशिः ॥ ५५॥
units.iast:
prāgasadyāti paścātsatsacca yāyādasattathā |
anātmābhijanaṃ tatsyādviparītaḥ svayaṃ dṛśiḥ || 55||
units.translation: What is absent before, comes to exist later, and what exists later passes into non-existence: that is of the nature of not-Self. The opposite, the self-evident Seer, is the Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 178
units.deva: तत्र घटादीनां दृश्यानामनात्मत्वं द्रष्ट्रात्मपूर्वकं प्रत्यक्षेणैव प्रमाणेनोपलभ्यानात्मनश्चासाधारणान् धर्मानवधार्य तैर्दृश्यत्वागमापायादिभिर्धर्मैः शरीरेन्द्रियमनोनिश्चयादिवृत्तीरनात्मतया व्युदस्याहंवृत्तिमतोऽपि दृश्यत्वाविशेषाद्द्रष्टृपूर्वकत्वमवसीयते । तदेतदाह ।
units.iast: tatra ghaṭādīnāṃ dṛśyānāmanātmatvaṃ draṣṭrātmapūrvakaṃ pratyakṣeṇaiva pramāṇenopalabhyānātmanaścāsādhāraṇān dharmānavadhārya tairdṛśyatvāgamāpāyādibhirdharmaiḥ śarīrendriyamanoniścayādivṛttīranātmatayā vyudasyāhaṃvṛttimato'pi dṛśyatvāviśeṣāddraṣṭṛpūrvakatvamavasīyate | tadetadāha |
units.translation: The not-Selfhood of visible things such as pots is directly evident, with the seer as its ground. Their distinctive properties are recognized; then, by their being seen and by their arising and passing away, the body, senses, mind and its judgments are set aside as not-Self. Since the “I”-thought is also seen, it too is known to depend on a seer. This is expressed as follows:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.56
units.deva:
घटादयो यथा लिङ्गं स्युः परंपरयाहमः ।
दृश्यत्वादहमप्येवं लिङ्गं स्याद्द्रष्टुरात्मनः ॥ ५६॥
units.iast:
ghaṭādayo yathā liṅgaṃ syuḥ paraṃparayāhamaḥ |
dṛśyatvādahamapyevaṃ liṅgaṃ syāddraṣṭurātmanaḥ || 56||
units.translation: Just as pots and the rest are, through a chain of dependence, signs of the “I,” so the “I,” because it is seen, is a sign of the Self as Seer.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 181
units.deva: ननु द्रष्टृदर्शनदृश्यानां जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तेष्वागमापायदर्शनाद्यसाक्षिकौ तेषामागमापायौ स आगमापायविभागरहित आत्मा यथा यन्निबन्धनौ जगतः प्रकाशाप्रकाशौ स प्रकाशाप्रकाशविभागरहितः सूर्य इति ।
units.iast: nanu draṣṭṛdarśanadṛśyānāṃ jāgratsvapnasuṣupteṣvāgamāpāyadarśanādyasākṣikau teṣāmāgamāpāyau sa āgamāpāyavibhāgarahita ātmā yathā yannibandhanau jagataḥ prakāśāprakāśau sa prakāśāprakāśavibhāgarahitaḥ sūrya iti |
units.translation: One might object: the seer, seeing and seen are all observed to arise and disappear in waking, dream and deep sleep. Their arising and disappearance are known by a witness; that witness is the Self, free of arising and disappearance. Just as the sun, on which the world’s light and darkness depend, is free of that division—

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 182
units.deva: यदा चैवं तदा वाक्यावगम्यस्यार्थस्यानुदितानस्तमितविज्ञानमात्रस्वभावस्यानुमानेनैव प्रतिपन्नत्वात्पुनरपि वाक्यस्य निर्विषयत्वप्रसङ्गः । नैष दोषः ।
units.iast: yadā caivaṃ tadā vākyāvagamyasyārthasyānuditānastamitavijñānamātrasvabhāvasyānumānenaiva pratipannatvātpunarapi vākyasya nirviṣayatvaprasaṅgaḥ | naiṣa doṣaḥ |
units.translation: if so, the meaning taught by the sentence, whose nature is awareness without beginning or end, has already been established by inference. The scriptural sentence would then have no subject matter. This is no fault:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 183
units.deva: लिङ्गव्यवधानेन तत्प्रतिपत्तेः । ननु साक्षादपरोक्षादात्मस्वभावेनानात्मनो हानोपादानयोः संबन्धग्रहणात्कमतिशयं वाक्यं कुर्यात् । मैवं वोचः ।
units.iast: liṅgavyavadhānena tatpratipatteḥ | nanu sākṣādaparokṣādātmasvabhāvenānātmano hānopādānayoḥ saṃbandhagrahaṇātkamatiśayaṃ vākyaṃ kuryāt | maivaṃ vocaḥ |
units.translation: because that conclusion is reached only through an intervening sign. But if the Self is already directly and immediately experienced as one’s own nature, and one can distinguish what is not-Self in order to give it up or take it up, what further work could the sentence do? Do not say this.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 184
units.translation: The conclusion depends on an inferential sign.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 185
units.deva: न हि लिङ्गव्यवधानेनात्मप्रतिपत्तिः साक्षात्प्रतिपत्तिर्भवति "यमेवैष वृणुते तेन लभ्यः " इति श्रुतेः । अत आह ।
units.iast: na hi liṅgavyavadhānenātmapratipattiḥ sākṣātpratipattirbhavati "yamevaiṣa vṛṇute tena labhyaḥ " iti śruteḥ | ata āha |
units.translation: Knowing the Self through an intervening sign is not direct knowledge. Scripture says, “The Self is attained by the one whom it chooses.” Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.57
units.translation: An inferential sign proves only existence, so it cannot fully reveal a sentence’s meaning; this Self, beyond the alternatives “is” and “is not,” is understood from scripture.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 188
units.deva: ननु यदि व्यावृत्तसदसद्विकल्पजालं वस्त्वभीष्टं वाक्याद्भवतस्तथापि तूत्सार्यते वाक्यविषया तृष्णा -- यस्मादन्तरेणापि वाक्यश्रवणं निरस्ताशेषविकल्पमागोपालाविपालपण्डितं सुषुप्ते वस्तु सिद्धमतो नार्थो वाक्यश्रवणेन । नैतदेवम् ।
units.iast: nanu yadi vyāvṛttasadasadvikalpajālaṃ vastvabhīṣṭaṃ vākyādbhavatastathāpi tūtsāryate vākyaviṣayā tṛṣṇā -- yasmādantareṇāpi vākyaśravaṇaṃ nirastāśeṣavikalpamāgopālāvipālapaṇḍitaṃ suṣupte vastu siddhamato nārtho vākyaśravaṇena | naitadevam |
units.translation: Another objection: “If the reality you want is the thing beyond all alternatives of existence and nonexistence, the desire for a scriptural sentence can still be set aside. Even without hearing one, that reality is present in deep sleep, where every distinction is absent, from the cowherd to the learned scholar. So hearing scripture is unnecessary.” This is not so.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 189
units.deva: किं कारणम् । सर्वानर्थबीजस्यात्मानवबोधस्य सुषुप्ते संभवात् । यदि हि सुषुप्तेऽज्ञानं नाभविष्यदन्तरेणापि वेदान्तवाक्यश्रवणमनन निदिध्यासनान्यहं ब्रह्मास्मीत्यध्यवसायात्सर्वप्राणभूतामपि स्वरसत एव सुषुप्तप्रतिपत्तेः सकलसंसारोच्छित्तिप्रसङ्गः । न च कैवल्यात्पुनरुत्थानं न्याय्यमनिर्मोक्षप्रसङ्गात् । न चान्य एव सुषुप्तोऽन्य एवोत्थित इति शक्यं वक्तुं नाद्राक्षमहं सुषुप्तेऽन्यत् किंचिदपीत्युत्तितस्य प्रत्यभिज्ञादर्शनात् । तस्मादवश्यं सुषुप्तेऽज्ञानमभ्युपगन्तव्यम् । ननु यदि तत्राज्ञानमभविष्यद्रागद्वेषघटाज्ञानादिवत्प्रत्यक्षमभविष्यद्यथेह लोके घटं न जानामीत्यज्ञानमव्यवहितं प्रत्यक्षम् । अत्रोच्यते । न । अभिव्यञ्जकाभावात् । कथमभिव्यञ्जकाभाव इति चेच्छृणु ।
units.iast: kiṃ kāraṇam | sarvānarthabījasyātmānavabodhasya suṣupte saṃbhavāt | yadi hi suṣupte'jñānaṃ nābhaviṣyadantareṇāpi vedāntavākyaśravaṇamanana nididhyāsanānyahaṃ brahmāsmītyadhyavasāyātsarvaprāṇabhūtāmapi svarasata eva suṣuptapratipatteḥ sakalasaṃsārocchittiprasaṅgaḥ | na ca kaivalyātpunarutthānaṃ nyāyyamanirmokṣaprasaṅgāt | na cānya eva suṣupto'nya evotthita iti śakyaṃ vaktuṃ nādrākṣamahaṃ suṣupte'nyat kiṃcidapītyuttitasya pratyabhijñādarśanāt | tasmādavaśyaṃ suṣupte'jñānamabhyupagantavyam | nanu yadi tatrājñānamabhaviṣyadrāgadveṣaghaṭājñānādivatpratyakṣamabhaviṣyadyatheha loke ghaṭaṃ na jānāmītyajñānamavyavahitaṃ pratyakṣam | atrocyate | na | abhivyañjakābhāvāt | kathamabhivyañjakābhāva iti cecchṛṇu |
units.translation: Why not? Because ignorance, the seed of every misfortune, persists in deep sleep. If ignorance were absent there, then even without hearing, reflecting on and contemplating the Vedānta sentences, everyone—from the smallest living creature onward—would naturally wake from sleep convinced “I am Brahman”; the whole of worldly bondage would thereby end. Nor would it make sense to rise again after liberation, for that would make liberation impossible. One also cannot say that the sleeper and the one who wakes are different people: the person who wakes recognizes, “I saw nothing else while asleep.” Ignorance must therefore be admitted to persist in deep sleep. An objection follows: if ignorance were present there, it should be directly perceived, as attachment, aversion or ignorance of a pot is perceived here when one says, “I do not know the pot.” The answer is no, because there is no revealer of it. If asked how there can be no revealer, listen:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.58
units.deva:
बाह्यां वृत्तिमनुत्पाद्य व्यक्तिः स्यान्नाहमो यथा ।
नर्तेऽन्तःकरणं तद्वद्ध्वान्तस्य व्यक्तिराञ्जसी ॥ ५८॥
units.iast:
bāhyāṃ vṛttimanutpādya vyaktiḥ syānnāhamo yathā |
narte'ntaḥkaraṇaṃ tadvaddhvāntasya vyaktirāñjasī || 58||
units.translation: Just as the “I” does not appear without producing an outward mental activity, ignorance does not become clear unless the inner instrument, the mind, is manifest.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 192
units.deva: कश्चिदतिक्रान्तं प्रतिस्मृत्य "दृश्यत्वादहमप्येवं लिङ्गं स्याद्द्रष्टुरात्मनः " इति निर्युक्तिकमभिहितमित्याह । किं कारणम् ।
units.iast: kaścidatikrāntaṃ pratismṛtya "dṛśyatvādahamapyevaṃ liṅgaṃ syāddraṣṭurātmanaḥ " iti niryuktikamabhihitamityāha | kiṃ kāraṇam |
units.translation: Someone recalls the earlier argument and says that the claim ‘because it is seen, the “I” too is a sign of the witnessing Self’ was made without proof. Why?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 193
units.deva: अहंतज्ज्ञात्रोर्विवेकाप्रसिद्धेः । यथेह घटदेवदत्तयोर्ग्राह्यग्राहकत्वेन स्फुटतरो विभागः प्रसिद्धो लोके न तथेहाहंकारतज्ज्ञात्रोर्विभागोऽस्तीति तस्मादसाध्वेतदभिहितमिति । अत्रोच्यते ।
units.iast: ahaṃtajjñātrorvivekāprasiddheḥ | yatheha ghaṭadevadattayorgrāhyagrāhakatvena sphuṭataro vibhāgaḥ prasiddho loke na tathehāhaṃkāratajjñātrorvibhāgo'stīti tasmādasādhvetadabhihitamiti | atrocyate |
units.translation: “Because no distinction between the ‘I’ and the knower is established. In ordinary life the difference between a pot and Devadatta, as object and perceiver, is quite clear; there is no such evident difference between the ego and the one who knows it. So that claim is unsound.” The reply is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.59
units.deva:
दाह्यदाहकतैकत्र यथा स्याद्वह्निदारुणोः ।
ज्ञेयज्ञातृकतैवं स्यादहंज्ञात्रोः परस्परम् ॥ ५९॥
units.iast:
dāhyadāhakataikatra yathā syādvahnidāruṇoḥ |
jñeyajñātṛkataivaṃ syādahaṃjñātroḥ parasparam || 59||
units.translation: Just as fire and wood have the relation of burning and being burned in one place, so the “I” and its knower stand in the relation of known and knower.

gloss.en: the state of being burned and burning
the state of known and knower

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 196
units.deva: एवं तावदविद्योत्थस्यान्तःकरणस्य बाह्यविषयनिमित्तरूपावच्छेदायाहंवृत्तिर्व्याप्रियते । तयावच्छिन्नं सत्कूटस्थप्रत्यगात्मोपादानावबोधरूपस्याव्यवधानतया विषयभावं प्रतिपद्यत इति । तत्र तयोर्ज्ञात्रहंतारूपयो रवभासकावभास्यसंबन्धव्यतिरेकेण नान्यत्संबन्धान्तरमुपपद्यते । अहंतारूपं त्वात्मसात्कृत्वाऽहंकञ्चुकं परिधायोपकार्यत्वोपकारकत्वक्षमः सन् बाह्यविषयेणोपकारिणापकारिणा वात्मात्मीयं संबन्धं प्रतिपद्यते ।
units.iast: evaṃ tāvadavidyotthasyāntaḥkaraṇasya bāhyaviṣayanimittarūpāvacchedāyāhaṃvṛttirvyāpriyate | tayāvacchinnaṃ satkūṭasthapratyagātmopādānāvabodharūpasyāvyavadhānatayā viṣayabhāvaṃ pratipadyata iti | tatra tayorjñātrahaṃtārūpayo ravabhāsakāvabhāsyasaṃbandhavyatirekeṇa nānyatsaṃbandhāntaramupapadyate | ahaṃtārūpaṃ tvātmasātkṛtvā'haṃkañcukaṃ paridhāyopakāryatvopakārakatvakṣamaḥ san bāhyaviṣayeṇopakāriṇāpakāriṇā vātmātmīyaṃ saṃbandhaṃ pratipadyate |
units.translation: The mind, arising from ignorance, takes on a particular form when prompted by an external object; this is the “I”-thought. The changeless innermost Self, its basis and the form of awareness, then becomes its immediate object. Between the knower and the ego there is no relation other than that of illuminator and what is illuminated. By taking the “I”-form as itself and wearing the sheath of ego, the Self appears capable of being helped or harmed and enters into relation with external objects as “mine,” whether they benefit or injure it.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 197
units.translation: This is stated in the following verse:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.60
units.deva:
इदं ज्ञानं भवेज्ज्ञातुर्ममज्ञानं तथाहमः ।
अज्ञानोपाधिनेदं स्याद्विक्रियातोऽहमो मम ॥ ६०॥
units.iast:
idaṃ jñānaṃ bhavejjñāturmamajñānaṃ tathāhamaḥ |
ajñānopādhinedaṃ syādvikriyāto'hamo mama || 60||
units.translation: The Witness knows an object as “this,” while the ego knows it as “mine.” The “this” notion arises through ignorance as a limiting adjunct; “mine” is a modification of the ego.

gloss.en: through the limiting adjunct of ignorance

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 200
units.deva: एकस्यैव ज्ञातुरन्तर्बाह्यनिमित्तभेदाद्विभिन्नेऽपि विषय इदं ममेति ज्ञानं द्वैरूप्यं जायत इत्युक्तम् ।
units.iast: ekasyaiva jñāturantarbāhyanimittabhedādvibhinne'pi viṣaya idaṃ mameti jñānaṃ dvairūpyaṃ jāyata ityuktam |
units.translation: Thus, even though there is only one knower, differing inner and outer objects give rise to the two forms of cognition, ‘this’ and ‘mine.’

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 201
units.deva: अत्रोपक्रियमाणापक्रियमाणस्यैव ज्ञातुर्विषये ममप्रत्ययो भवति विपर्यये चेदंप्रत्यय इति कथमवगम्यते ।
units.iast: atropakriyamāṇāpakriyamāṇasyaiva jñāturviṣaye mamapratyayo bhavati viparyaye cedaṃpratyaya iti kathamavagamyate |
units.translation: How is it known that the thought “mine” concerns the knower only when the knower is affected, while “this” concerns what is other?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 202
units.translation: It is known through agreement and difference. How? The verse says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.61
units.deva:
अनुपक्रियमाणत्वान्न ज्ञातुः स्यादहं मम ।
घटादिवदिदं तु स्यान्मोहमात्रव्यपाश्रयात् ॥ ६१॥
units.iast:
anupakriyamāṇatvānna jñātuḥ syādahaṃ mama |
ghaṭādivadidaṃ tu syānmohamātravyapāśrayāt || 61||
units.translation: Because the Witness is untouched, it does not take the “I” as “mine”; the “I” appears as an object, like a pot, resting only on delusion.

gloss.en: because it is not affected or acted upon
of the knower; of the Witness
like a pot and other objects
because it rests solely on delusion

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 205
units.deva: मोहतत्कार्याश्रयत्वाज्ज्ञातृत्वविक्रिययोः पूर्वत्रेदंममज्ञान्वयः प्रदर्शितः । अथाधुना तद्व्यतिरेकेण व्यतिरेकप्रदर्शनार्थाह ।
units.iast: mohatatkāryāśrayatvājjñātṛtvavikriyayoḥ pūrvatredaṃmamajñānvayaḥ pradarśitaḥ | athādhunā tadvyatirekeṇa vyatirekapradarśanārthāha |
units.translation: Earlier, the agreement of ‘this’ and ‘mine’ with delusion and with changes in the knower was shown. Now, to show their absence when those conditions are absent, the author says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.62
units.deva:
विक्रियाज्ञानशून्यत्वान्नेदं न च ममात्मनः ।
उत्थितस्य सतोऽज्ञानं नाहमज्ञासिषं यतः ॥ ६२॥
units.iast:
vikriyājñānaśūnyatvānnedaṃ na ca mamātmanaḥ |
utthitasya sato'jñānaṃ nāhamajñāsiṣaṃ yataḥ || 62||
units.translation: The Self is free from change and ignorance, so “this” and “mine” do not belong to it. Only one who has awakened says, “I did not know” [anything while asleep].

gloss.en: because it is free from change and ignorance
of one who has risen; awakened

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 208
units.translation: To show how far the discrimination between Self and not-Self extends, he says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.63
units.translation: Perception and verbal testimony establish only this much; the sentence alone destroys the harmful ignorance concerning the ever-existent Self.

gloss.en: through verbal testimony and perception as means of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 211
units.translation: At the beginning of the second chapter, four kinds of listeners were introduced.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 212
units.deva: तत्र कृत्स्नानात्मनिवृत्तौ सत्यां यः प्रत्यगात्मन्यवाक्यार्थतां प्रतिपद्यते स क्षपिताशेषान्तरायहेतुरिति न तं प्रति वक्तव्यं किंचिदप्यवशिष्यते । योऽपि वाक्यश्रवणमात्रादेव प्रतिपद्यते तस्याप्यतीन्द्रिय शक्तिमत्त्वान्न किंचिदप्यपेक्षितव्यमस्ति । यश्च श्राविततत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यः स्वयमेवान्वयव्यतिरेको कृत्वा तदवसान एव वाक्यार्थं प्रतिपद्यतेऽसावपि यथार्थं प्रतिपन्न इति पूर्ववदेवोपेक्षितव्यः ।
