units.iast: tatra kṛtsnānātmanivṛttau satyāṃ yaḥ pratyagātmanyavākyārthatāṃ pratipadyate sa kṣapitāśeṣāntarāyaheturiti na taṃ prati vaktavyaṃ kiṃcidapyavaśiṣyate | yo'pi vākyaśravaṇamātrādeva pratipadyate tasyāpyatīndriya śaktimattvānna kiṃcidapyapekṣitavyamasti | yaśca śrāvitatattvamasyādivākyaḥ svayamevānvayavyatireko kṛtvā tadavasāna eva vākyārthaṃ pratipadyate'sāvapi yathārthaṃ pratipanna iti pūrvavadevopekṣitavyaḥ |
units.translation: Of these, nothing remains to be taught to one who, after all not-Self has been fully set aside, recognizes the Self within as beyond ordinary sentence meaning; every obstacle to that recognition has been destroyed. Nor does one need anything further who understands from merely hearing the sentence, because such a person has extraordinary insight. The person who, after hearing “you are that,” works through agreement and difference independently and understands the sentence meaning at its conclusion has also understood correctly; that person too may be left aside, as before.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 213
units.deva: यः पुनरन्वयव्यतिरेकौ कारयित्वापि पुनःपुनर्वाक्यं श्राव्यते यथाभूतार्थप्रतिपत्तये तस्य कृतान्वयव्यतिरेकस्य सतः कथं वाक्यं श्राव्यत इति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: yaḥ punaranvayavyatirekau kārayitvāpi punaḥpunarvākyaṃ śrāvyate yathābhūtārthapratipattaye tasya kṛtānvayavyatirekasya sataḥ kathaṃ vākyaṃ śrāvyata iti | ucyate |
units.translation: But why should the sentence be repeated for someone who has already worked through agreement and difference, so that this person may understand the truth as it is? The answer is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.64
units.deva:
नवसंख्याहृतज्ञानो दशमो विभ्रमाद्यथा ।
न वेत्ति दशमोऽस्मीति वीक्षमाणोऽपि तान्नव ॥ ६४॥
units.iast:
navasaṃkhyāhṛtajñāno daśamo vibhramādyathā |
na vetti daśamo'smīti vīkṣamāṇo'pi tānnava || 64||
units.translation: For example, a man confused by the count of nine does not know “I am the tenth,” even while looking at those nine.

gloss.en: whose understanding is confused by the count of nine

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 216
units.translation: The author now applies the meaning of the example to the point at hand:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.65
units.deva:
अपविद्धद्वयोऽप्येवं तत्त्वमस्यादिना विना ।
वेत्ति नैकलमात्मानं नान्वेष्यं चात्र कारणम् ॥ ६५॥
units.iast:
apaviddhadvayo'pyevaṃ tattvamasyādinā vinā |
vetti naikalamātmānaṃ nānveṣyaṃ cātra kāraṇam || 65||
units.translation: Likewise, even after setting duality aside, a person does not know the one, whole Self without a teaching such as “That thou art”; there is no need to investigate the cause further here.

gloss.en: one who has set duality aside
by “That thou art” and similar teachings

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 219
units.deva: नान्वेष्यं चात्र कारणमित्युक्तं तत्कस्मादिति चोदिते प्रत्याहान्वेषणासहिष्णुत्वात् । तत्कथमित्याह ।
units.iast: nānveṣyaṃ cātra kāraṇamityuktaṃ tatkasmāditi codite pratyāhānveṣaṇāsahiṣṇutvāt | tatkathamityāha |
units.translation: When asked why no investigation is needed, he replies: because this delusion cannot withstand inquiry. How?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.66
units.deva:
सेयं भ्रान्तिर्निरालम्बा सर्वन्यायविरोधिनी ।
सहते न विचारं सा तमो यद्वद्दिवाकरम् ॥ ६६॥
units.iast:
seyaṃ bhrāntirnirālambā sarvanyāyavirodhinī |
sahate na vicāraṃ sā tamo yadvaddivākaram || 66||
units.translation: This delusion is groundless and conflicts with every sound line of reasoning; it cannot endure inquiry, just as darkness cannot endure the sun.

gloss.en: opposed to every line of reasoning

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 222
units.deva: तस्याः खल्वस्या अविद्याया भ्रान्तेः सम्यग्ज्ञानोत्पत्तिद्वारेण निवृत्तिः ।
units.iast: tasyāḥ khalvasyā avidyāyā bhrānteḥ samyagjñānotpattidvāreṇa nivṛttiḥ |
units.translation: This ignorance, this delusion, is ended by the arising of right knowledge.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.67
units.deva:
बुभुत्सोच्छेदिनी चास्य सदसीत्यादिना दृढम् ।
प्रतीचि प्रतिपत्तिः स्यान्नासौ मानान्तराद्भवेत् ॥ ६७॥
units.iast:
bubhutsocchedinī cāsya sadasītyādinā dṛḍham |
pratīci pratipattiḥ syānnāsau mānāntarādbhavet || 67||
units.translation: A firm recognition of the inward Self, from teachings such as “You are Being,” ends the desire to know more; it does not arise from any other means of knowledge.

gloss.en: from teachings such as “You are Being”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 225
units.translation: If asked how a sentence can indeed reveal the truth, an example is given:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.68
units.deva:
जिज्ञासोर्दशमं यद्वन्नवातिक्रम्य ताम्यतः ।
त्वमेव दशमोऽसीति कुर्यादेवं प्रमां वचः ॥ ६८॥
units.iast:
jijñāsordaśamaṃ yadvannavātikramya tāmyataḥ |
tvameva daśamo'sīti kuryādevaṃ pramāṃ vacaḥ || 68||
units.translation: Just as the words “You yourself are the tenth” give true knowledge to a distressed seeker who has counted the nine and seeks the tenth, so the scriptural word gives true knowledge.

gloss.en: of one who desires to know

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 228
units.translation: The valid knowledge arising from hearing a sentence such as “you are that” is thus produced.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 229
units.deva: न च नैवमिति प्रत्ययान्तर जायते । तदेतद्दृष्टान्तेन प्रतिपादयति ।
units.iast: na ca naivamiti pratyayāntara jāyate | tadetaddṛṣṭāntena pratipādayati |
units.translation: And no contrary cognition arises to dislodge it. The point is explained through the example:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.69
units.deva:
दशमोऽसीति वाक्योत्था न धीरस्य विहन्यते ।
आदिमध्यावसानेषु न नवस्वस्य संशयः ॥ ६९॥
units.iast:
daśamo'sīti vākyotthā na dhīrasya vihanyate |
ādimadhyāvasāneṣu na navasvasya saṃśayaḥ || 69||
units.translation: The knowledge born from the sentence “You are the tenth” is not shaken; before, during, or after it arises, he does not doubt that he is one of the nine [he sees].

gloss.en: at the beginning, middle, and end

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.70
units.deva:
एवं तत्त्वमसीत्यस्माद्द्वैतनुत्प्रत्यगात्मनि ।
सम्यग्ज्ञातत्वमर्थस्य जायेतैव प्रमा दृढा ॥ ७०॥
units.iast:
evaṃ tattvamasītyasmāddvaitanutpratyagātmani |
samyagjñātatvamarthasya jāyetaiva pramā dṛḍhā || 70||
units.translation: In the same way, from the sentence “That thou art,” which dispels duality, firm and correct knowledge of the meaning of the inward Self arises.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 234
units.translation: It has been said that valid knowledge arises regarding the inner Self. An objection is now raised:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 235
units.deva: किं यथा घटादिप्रमेयविषया प्रमा कर्त्रादिकारकभेदानपह्नवेन जायते तथैवोताशेषकारकग्रामोपमर्देन कर्तुः प्रत्यगात्मनीति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: kiṃ yathā ghaṭādiprameyaviṣayā pramā kartrādikārakabhedānapahnavena jāyate tathaivotāśeṣakārakagrāmopamardena kartuḥ pratyagātmanīti | ucyate |
units.translation: “Does this knowledge of the inner Self arise like knowledge of an object such as a pot, without denying the distinctions between agent and the other factors? Or does it arise by dissolving the entire group of factors, with the inward Self as the agent?” The reply is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.71
units.deva:
प्रत्यक्तास्य स्वतोरूपं निष्क्रियाकारकाफलम् ।
अद्वितीयं तदिद्धा धीः प्रत्यगात्मेव लक्ष्यते ॥ ७१॥
units.iast:
pratyaktāsya svatorūpaṃ niṣkriyākārakāphalam |
advitīyaṃ tadiddhā dhīḥ pratyagātmeva lakṣyate || 71||
units.translation: Inwardness is its very nature: it is actionless, without agent, action, or result, and nondual. The intellect lit by it is loosely regarded as the inmost Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 238
units.translation: Because this is so:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.72
units.translation: Therefore even the wise take that intellect to be the Self, although their identification with sense-objects recedes as those objects grow more distant.

gloss.en: the state of being the Self

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 241
units.deva: आह । यदि वाक्यमेव यथाभूतार्थवबोधकमथ कस्य हेतोरविद्योत्थापितस्य कर्तृत्वादेरुपदेश इत्युक्ते प्रतिविधीयते ।
units.iast: āha | yadi vākyameva yathābhūtārthavabodhakamatha kasya hetoravidyotthāpitasya kartṛtvāderupadeśa ityukte pratividhīyate |
units.translation: An objection is now raised: “If the sentence itself teaches the truth as it is, why teach agency and the rest, which arise from ignorance?” The reply is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.73
units.deva:
भ्रान्तिप्रसिद्ध्यानूद्यार्थं तत्तत्वं भ्रान्तिबाधया ।
अयं नेत्युपदिश्येत तथैवं तत्त्वमित्यपि ॥ ७३॥
units.iast:
bhrāntiprasiddhyānūdyārthaṃ tattatvaṃ bhrāntibādhayā |
ayaṃ netyupadiśyeta tathaivaṃ tattvamityapi || 73||
units.translation: To undo an error, teaching first restates what the error has made familiar and then corrects it: “This is not it.” In the same way it teaches, “That thou art.”

gloss.en: through what is familiar by error

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 244
units.translation: An example is offered to make this clear:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.74
units.deva:
स्थाणुः स्थाणुरितीवोक्तिर्न नृबुद्धिं निरस्यति ।
व्यनुवादात्तथैवोक्तिर्भ्रान्तिं पुंसो न बाधते ॥ ७४॥
units.iast:
sthāṇuḥ sthāṇuritīvoktirna nṛbuddhiṃ nirasyati |
vyanuvādāttathaivoktirbhrāntiṃ puṃso na bādhate || 74||
units.translation: Saying “a post, a post” does not undo the idea that it is a man; likewise, merely repeating what is already assumed does not remove a person's error.

gloss.en: the idea that it is a man

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 247
units.translation: Since the word “thou” takes up what the listener already understands, its meanings such as being unhappy, which are merely indicated as its topic, are not intended [as the sentence’s final meaning].

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 248
units.deva: विधीयमानत्वे हि सति विरोधप्रसङ्गो न तु विधीयमाना नूद्यमानयोरिति । स्वप्रधानयोर्हि पदयोर्विरोधाशङ्का सामान्यलिङ्गतत्वात्तयोर्न विपर्यये ।
units.iast: vidhīyamānatve hi sati virodhaprasaṅgo na tu vidhīyamānā nūdyamānayoriti | svapradhānayorhi padayorvirodhāśaṅkā sāmānyaliṅgatatvāttayorna viparyaye |
units.translation: If those attributes were being newly asserted, a contradiction would follow; there is no such contradiction between what is asserted and what is merely restated. The possibility of conflict concerns two words that each primarily assert their own meaning, because the general element they share is understood by inference; it does not apply in the reverse case.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.75
units.deva:
अनालिङ्गितसामान्यौ न जिहासितवादिनौ ।
व्युत्थितौ तत्त्वमौ तस्मादन्योन्याभिसमीक्षणौ ॥ ७५॥
units.iast:
anāliṅgitasāmānyau na jihāsitavādinau |
vyutthitau tattvamau tasmādanyonyābhisamīkṣaṇau || 75||
units.translation: “That” and “thou” no longer retain their universal meanings or express the incompatible parts that must be relinquished. Freed from those parts, they can be joined in a statement of identity.

gloss.en: expressing the parts intended to be given up

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 251
units.deva: अपास्तसामान्यार्थत्वादनुवादस्थत्वाद्विधीयमानेन च सह विरोधाद्दुःखित्वादेरस्तु कामं जिहासितार्थयो रसंसर्गो यथोपन्यस्तदोषविरहात्तत्त्वमर्थयोः संसर्गोऽस्तु नीलोत्पलवदिति चेन्नैवमप्युपपद्यते । तस्मात् ।
units.iast: apāstasāmānyārthatvādanuvādasthatvādvidhīyamānena ca saha virodhādduḥkhitvāderastu kāmaṃ jihāsitārthayo rasaṃsargo yathopanyastadoṣavirahāttattvamarthayoḥ saṃsargo'stu nīlotpalavaditi cennaivamapyupapadyate | tasmāt |
units.translation: One might argue: “Let the meanings of ‘that’ and ‘thou’ be unrelated, since their shared general meanings have been removed; ‘thou’ merely restates what is known, and it conflicts with what is newly asserted. Then let the two meanings be related, as blue and lotus are related, since that avoids the stated fault.” This too does not work. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.76
units.deva:
तदर्थयोस्तु निष्ठात्मा द्वयपारोक्ष्यवर्जितः ।
नाद्वितीयं विनात्मानं नात्मा नित्यदृशा विना ॥ ७६॥
units.iast:
tadarthayostu niṣṭhātmā dvayapārokṣyavarjitaḥ |
nādvitīyaṃ vinātmānaṃ nātmā nityadṛśā vinā || 76||
units.translation: The final meaning of both is the Self, free from the remoteness attributed to either. There is no nondual reality apart from the Self, and no Self apart from the eternal Witness.

gloss.en: the Self as their final meaning
free from the remoteness of both

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 254
units.deva: अत्राह । किमिह जिहासितं किं वोपादित्सितमिति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: atrāha | kimiha jihāsitaṃ kiṃ vopāditsitamiti | ucyate |
units.translation: Someone asks: “What here is to be given up, and what is to be taken up?” The answer is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 255
units.deva: प्रत्यगात्मार्थाभिधायिनस्त्वंपदादुभयं प्रतीयतेऽहं दुःखी प्रत्यगात्मा च । तत्र च प्रत्यगात्मनोऽहं दुःखीत्यनेनाभिसंबन्ध आत्मयाथात्म्यानवबोधहेतुक एव । अतोऽहमर्थोऽपसृष्टत्वादज्ञानोत्थत्वाच्च हेय इति प्रत्यक्षतोवसीयते । तदर्थे किं हेयं किं वोपादेयमिति नावध्रियते । तत इदमभिधीयते ।
units.iast: pratyagātmārthābhidhāyinastvaṃpadādubhayaṃ pratīyate'haṃ duḥkhī pratyagātmā ca | tatra ca pratyagātmano'haṃ duḥkhītyanenābhisaṃbandha ātmayāthātmyānavabodhahetuka eva | ato'hamartho'pasṛṣṭatvādajñānotthatvācca heya iti pratyakṣatovasīyate | tadarthe kiṃ heyaṃ kiṃ vopādeyamiti nāvadhriyate | tata idamabhidhīyate |
units.translation: The word “thou,” which expresses the inner Self, conveys both the ordinary “I am unhappy” and the innermost Self. The connection between the innermost Self and “I am unhappy” is caused only by failure to know the Self as it truly is. The ordinary ego is therefore plainly to be relinquished: it is something superimposed and arises from ignorance. What, then, is to be given up or taken up in the meaning of “that”? The verse answers:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.77
units.deva: पारोक्ष्यं यत्तदर्थे स्यात्तद्धेयमहमर्थवत् । प्रतीचेवाहमोऽभेदः पारोक्ष्येणात्मनोऽपि मे ॥ ७७॥
units.iast: pārokṣyaṃ yattadarthe syāttaddheyamahamarthavat | pratīcevāhamo'bhedaḥ pārokṣyeṇātmano'pi me || 77||
units.translation: Whatever remoteness belongs to the meaning of “That” is to be set aside, just as the ego-meaning of “I” is set aside. The identity of “I” with the inward Self also seems remote because of ignorance.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 256
units.deva: कथं पुनस्तदर्थोऽद्वितीयलक्षणः प्रत्यगात्मोपाश्रयं सद्वितीयत्वं दुःखित्वं निरन्वयमपनुदतीति । उच्यते । न चैतयोर्निवर्तकनिवर्त्यभावं वयं ब्रूमः । कथं तर्हि ।
units.iast: kathaṃ punastadartho'dvitīyalakṣaṇaḥ pratyagātmopāśrayaṃ sadvitīyatvaṃ duḥkhitvaṃ niranvayamapanudatīti | ucyate | na caitayornivartakanivartyabhāvaṃ vayaṃ brūmaḥ | kathaṃ tarhi |
units.translation: How does the meaning of “that,” characterized by nonduality and apparently distinct from the inward Self, remove the Self’s apparent duality and suffering? The answer: we do not claim that one directly removes the other. How, then?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 257
units.translation: The sentence reveals the nonduality that was previously unknown in the meaning of “thou,” the inner Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 258
units.deva: अतोऽनवबोधनिरासेन तदुत्थस्य सद्वितीयत्वस्य त्वमर्थत्वस्य परोक्षत्वस्य च तदर्थस्थस्य निरसनान्न वैयधिकरण्यादि चोद्यस्यावसरोऽस्तीति । तदिदमभिधीयते ।
units.iast: ato'navabodhanirāsena tadutthasya sadvitīyatvasya tvamarthatvasya parokṣatvasya ca tadarthasthasya nirasanānna vaiyadhikaraṇyādi codyasyāvasaro'stīti | tadidamabhidhīyate |
units.translation: By removing that ignorance, it removes the resulting duality wrongly attributed to “thou,” and the indirectness wrongly attributed to “that.” Thus the objection that these qualities belong to different subjects has no place. This is stated as follows:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.78
units.deva:
तत्त्वमर्थेन संपृक्तो नानात्वं विनिवर्तयेत् ।
नापरित्यक्तपारोक्ष्यं त्वं तदर्थं सिसृप्सति ॥ ७८॥
units.iast:
tattvamarthena saṃpṛkto nānātvaṃ vinivartayet |
nāparityaktapārokṣyaṃ tvaṃ tadarthaṃ sisṛpsati || 78||
units.translation: Joined with the meaning of “thou,” “That” removes plurality; “thou” cannot approach the meaning of “That” while its remoteness remains.

gloss.en: whose remoteness has not been given up

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 261
units.deva: कस्मात्पुनः कारणात्तदर्थोऽद्वितीयलक्षणस्त्वमर्थेन प्रत्यगात्मना पृथगर्थः सन्नविद्योत्थं सद्वितीयत्वं निहन्तीति । उच्यते । विरोधात् । तदुच्यते ।
units.iast: kasmātpunaḥ kāraṇāttadartho'dvitīyalakṣaṇastvamarthena pratyagātmanā pṛthagarthaḥ sannavidyotthaṃ sadvitīyatvaṃ nihantīti | ucyate | virodhāt | taducyate |
units.translation: Why does the nondual meaning of “that,” though apparently distinct from the inner Self meant by “thou,” destroy the duality born of ignorance? The answer is: because they contradict it. Thus:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.79
units.deva:
संसारिताद्वितीयेन पारोक्ष्यं चात्मना सह ।
प्रासङ्गिकं विरुद्धत्वात्तत्त्वम्भ्यां बाधनं तयोः ॥ ७९॥
units.iast:
saṃsāritādvitīyena pārokṣyaṃ cātmanā saha |
prāsaṅgikaṃ viruddhatvāttattvambhyāṃ bādhanaṃ tayoḥ || 79||
units.translation: Transmigrant existence and remoteness are incidental attributes of the Self and conflict with one another; “That” and “thou” negate them both.

gloss.en: by the Self's apparent transmigrant duality

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 264
units.translation: Another reason is given for the power of the meanings of “that” and “thou” to remove one another’s errors:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.80
units.translation: Because “That” and “thou” are scriptural and reveal a human good unavailable from another source, their meanings negate their conflicting elements without giving up their own meaning.

gloss.en: because they concern a human good not known from another source
because they are grounded in scripture

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 267
units.deva: एवं तावद्यथोपक्रान्तेन प्रक्रियावर्त्मना न प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणान्तरैर्विरोधगन्धोऽपि संभाव्यते ।
units.iast: evaṃ tāvadyathopakrāntena prakriyāvartmanā na pratyakṣādipramāṇāntarairvirodhagandho'pi saṃbhāvyate |
units.translation: Thus, along the line of reasoning begun earlier, no conflict whatever with perception or any other means of knowledge is possible.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 268
units.deva: यदा पुनः सर्वप्रकारेणापि यतमाना नैवेमं वाक्यार्थं संभावयामः प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणान्तरविरोधत एव तस्मिन्नपि पक्ष उच्यते ।
units.iast: yadā punaḥ sarvaprakāreṇāpi yatamānā naivemaṃ vākyārthaṃ saṃbhāvayāmaḥ pratyakṣādipramāṇāntaravirodhata eva tasminnapi pakṣa ucyate |
units.translation: If, despite examining the matter in every way, one still cannot reconcile the sentence meaning with other means of knowledge and assumes a conflict, the author gives an answer to that position too:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.81
units.deva:
प्रत्यक्षादिविरुद्धं चेद्वाक्यमर्थं वदेत्क्वचित् ।
स्यात्तु तद्दृष्टिविध्यर्थं योषाग्निवदसंशयम् ॥ ८१॥
units.iast:
pratyakṣādiviruddhaṃ cedvākyamarthaṃ vadetkvacit |
syāttu taddṛṣṭividhyarthaṃ yoṣāgnivadasaṃśayam || 81||
units.translation: If any sentence were to state something contrary to perception or another means of knowledge, it would surely be intended as a figurative contemplation instruction, like “a woman is fire.”

gloss.en: contrary to perception and the rest
for the purpose of an instruction to contemplate one thing as another

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 271
units.deva: यदा तु तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यं सर्वप्रकारेणापि विचार्यमाणं न क्रियां कटाक्षेणापि वीक्षते तदा प्रसंख्यानादिव्यापारो दुस्संभाव्य इति । तदुच्यते ।
units.iast: yadā tu tattvamasyādivākyaṃ sarvaprakāreṇāpi vicāryamāṇaṃ na kriyāṃ kaṭākṣeṇāpi vīkṣate tadā prasaṃkhyānādivyāpāro dussaṃbhāvya iti | taducyate |
units.translation: But when a sentence such as “you are that,” examined in every way, does not even glance toward an action, it is hard to maintain that an activity such as repeated meditation is required. The author therefore says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.82
units.deva:
वस्त्वेकनिष्ठं वाक्यं चेन्न तस्य स्यात्क्रियार्थता ।
वस्तुनो ह्येकरूपत्वाद्विकल्पस्याप्यसंभवः ॥ ८२॥
units.iast:
vastvekaniṣṭhaṃ vākyaṃ cenna tasya syātkriyārthatā |
vastuno hyekarūpatvādvikalpasyāpyasaṃbhavaḥ || 82||
units.translation: A sentence concerned solely with an existing reality cannot have action as its purpose; reality has one nature and allows no alternatives.

gloss.en: focused solely on an existing reality

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 274
units.translation: Nor is there conflict with another means of knowledge, because their subject matters differ. How?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 275
units.translation: The author says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.83
units.deva:
अपूर्वाधिगमं कुर्वत्प्रमाणं स्यान्न चेन्न तत् ।
न विरोधस्ततो युक्तो विभिन्नार्थावबोधिनोः ॥ ८३॥
units.iast:
apūrvādhigamaṃ kurvatpramāṇaṃ syānna cenna tat |
na virodhastato yukto vibhinnārthāvabodhinoḥ || 83||
units.translation: A means of knowledge must reveal something not previously known; otherwise it is not such a means. So two means that reveal different things cannot reasonably conflict.

gloss.en: knowledge of what was not known before
between two that reveal different meanings

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 278
units.deva: य एवमपि भिन्नविषयाणां विरोधं वक्ति सोऽत्रापि विरोधं ब्रूयात् ।
units.iast: ya evamapi bhinnaviṣayāṇāṃ virodhaṃ vakti so'trāpi virodhaṃ brūyāt |
units.translation: Someone who nonetheless claims that means of knowledge with different subjects conflict could also claim a conflict in this case:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.84
units.deva:
नायं शब्दः कुतो यस्माद्रूपं पश्यामि चक्षुषा ।
इति यद्वत्तथैवायं विरोधोऽक्षजवाक्ययोः ॥ ८४॥
units.iast:
nāyaṃ śabdaḥ kuto yasmādrūpaṃ paśyāmi cakṣuṣā |
iti yadvattathaivāyaṃ virodho'kṣajavākyayoḥ || 84||
units.translation: It would be like saying, “That is not a sound—why? Because I see a form with my eyes.” Such is the supposed conflict between sense-perception and scripture.

gloss.en: between sense-born perception and a verbal text

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 281
units.deva: प्रमाणानां सतां न विरोधः श्रोत्रादीनामिव भिन्नविषयत्वात् ।
units.iast: pramāṇānāṃ satāṃ na virodhaḥ śrotrādīnāmiva bhinnaviṣayatvāt |
units.translation: “Valid means of knowledge do not conflict, since their subjects differ, as do hearing and the other senses.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 282
units.deva: ययोश्चाभिन्नविषयत्वं तयोराखुनकुलयोरिव प्रतिनियत एव बाध्यबाधकभावः स्यात् । अतस्तदुच्यते ।
units.iast: yayoścābhinnaviṣayatvaṃ tayorākhunakulayoriva pratiniyata eva bādhyabādhakabhāvaḥ syāt | atastaducyate |
units.translation: Where two means have the same subject, one has a fixed power to correct the other, as with a mongoose and a snake. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.85
units.deva:
प्रत्यक्षं चेन्न शाब्दं स्याच्छाब्दं चेदक्षजं कथम् ।
प्रत्यक्षाभासः प्रत्यक्षे ह्यागमाभास आगमे ॥ ८५॥
units.iast:
pratyakṣaṃ cenna śābdaṃ syācchābdaṃ cedakṣajaṃ katham |
pratyakṣābhāsaḥ pratyakṣe hyāgamābhāsa āgame || 85||
units.translation: If it is perceptual, it is not verbal; if verbal, how can it be sense-born? A false appearance of perception belongs to perception, and a false appearance of revelation belongs to scripture.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 285
units.deva: न च प्रतिज्ञाहेतुदृष्टान्तन्याय इह संभवति शब्दादीनां प्रत्येकं प्रमाणत्वादत आह ।
units.iast: na ca pratijñāhetudṛṣṭāntanyāya iha saṃbhavati śabdādīnāṃ pratyekaṃ pramāṇatvādata āha |
units.translation: The formal pattern of a thesis, reason and example does not apply here, because words and the other means of knowledge each have authority on their own. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.86
units.deva:
स्वमहिम्ना प्रमाणानि कुर्वन्त्यर्थावबोधनम् ।
इतरेतरसाचिव्ये प्रामाण्यं नेष्यते स्वतः ॥ ८६॥
units.iast:
svamahimnā pramāṇāni kurvantyarthāvabodhanam |
itaretarasācivye prāmāṇyaṃ neṣyate svataḥ || 86||
units.translation: Each means of knowledge reveals its object by its own power; its validity is not held to depend on help from the others.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 288
units.deva: न च सुखदुःखादिसंबन्धोऽवगत्यात्मनः प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणैर्गृह्यते येन विरोधः प्रत्यक्षादिप्रमाणैरुद्धाट्यते ।
units.iast: na ca sukhaduḥkhādisaṃbandho'vagatyātmanaḥ pratyakṣādipramāṇairgṛhyate yena virodhaḥ pratyakṣādipramāṇairuddhāṭyate |
units.translation: Nor do perception and the other means of knowledge grasp any relation between awareness and happiness, suffering and the like that could be used to show a conflict with them.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.87
units.deva:
दुःखितावगतिश्चेत्स्यान्न प्रमीयेत सात्मवत् ।
कर्मण्येव प्रमा न्याय्या न तु कर्तर्यपि क्वचित् ॥ ८७॥
units.iast:
duḥkhitāvagatiścetsyānna pramīyeta sātmavat |
karmaṇyeva pramā nyāyyā na tu kartaryapi kvacit || 87||
units.translation: If suffering belonged to awareness itself, it could not be established as an object of valid knowledge, just as the Self is not known as an object. Valid cognition properly concerns an object, never the knower.

gloss.en: would be established by valid knowledge
with regard to the agent; knower

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 291
units.deva: अभ्युपगमेऽपि च प्रसंख्यानशतेनापि नैव त्वं संभावितदोषान्मुच्यते । अत आह ।
units.iast: abhyupagame'pi ca prasaṃkhyānaśatenāpi naiva tvaṃ saṃbhāvitadoṣānmucyate | ata āha |
units.translation: Even if one grants this, a hundred practices of contemplation will not free you from the imagined fault. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.88
units.deva:
प्रमाणबद्धमूलत्वाद्दुःखित्वं केन वार्यते ।
अग्न्युष्णवन्निवृत्तिश्चेन्नैरात्म्यं ह्येति सौगतम् ॥ ८८॥
units.iast:
pramāṇabaddhamūlatvādduḥkhitvaṃ kena vāryate |
agnyuṣṇavannivṛttiścennairātmyaṃ hyeti saugatam || 88||
units.translation: If suffering is rooted in a valid means of knowledge, who could remove it? If it could be ended, one would arrive at the Buddhist doctrine of no-Self—as though heat could be separated from fire.

gloss.en: because its root is tied to a valid means of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 294
units.translation: Another view is stated:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.89
units.translation: If properly practiced contemplation were to remove suffering, how could it produce valid knowledge when that knowledge conflicts with perception and the other means?

gloss.en: because it conflicts with perception and the rest

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 297
units.deva: ननु प्रसंख्यानं नाम तत्त्वमस्यादिशब्दार्थान्वयव्यतिरेकयुक्तिविषयबुद्ध्याम्रेडनमभिधीयते तच्चानुष्ठीयमानं प्रमितिवर्धनया परिपूर्णां प्रमितिं जनयति न पुनरैकाग्र्यवर्धनयेति ।
units.iast: nanu prasaṃkhyānaṃ nāma tattvamasyādiśabdārthānvayavyatirekayuktiviṣayabuddhyāmreḍanamabhidhīyate taccānuṣṭhīyamānaṃ pramitivardhanayā paripūrṇāṃ pramitiṃ janayati na punaraikāgryavardhanayeti |
units.translation: One might say that contemplation means repeatedly turning the mind, through reasoning by agreement and difference, toward the meaning of words such as “you are that.” Practised in this way, it produces complete knowledge by increasing the knowledge itself, not by increasing one-pointedness.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 298
units.deva: यथाशेषाशुचिनीडे स्त्रीकृणपे कामिनीति निर्वस्तुकः पुरुषायासमात्रजनितः प्रत्यय इति । तन्न । यतः ।
units.iast: yathāśeṣāśucinīḍe strīkṛṇape kāminīti nirvastukaḥ puruṣāyāsamātrajanitaḥ pratyaya iti | tanna | yataḥ |
units.translation: For example, a man may imagine a woman to be desirable even though she is only a mass of impurity and the notion is produced by his own effort; this objection does not apply, because:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.90
units.translation: Whatever grows in the mind through repeated practice is only one-pointedness; means of knowledge do not reveal their objects through repetition.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.91
units.deva:
अभ्यासोपचिता कृत्स्नं भावना चेन्निवर्तयेत् ।
नैकान्तिकी निवृत्तिरस्स्याद्भावनाजं हि तत्फलम् ॥ ९१॥
units.iast:
abhyāsopacitā kṛtsnaṃ bhāvanā cennivartayet |
naikāntikī nivṛttirassyādbhāvanājaṃ hi tatphalam || 91||
units.translation: If an entire mental cultivation built up by practice could remove [bondage], its cessation would not be final, since that result would itself be produced by cultivation.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 303
units.translation: The author adds:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.92
units.deva:
दुःखस्मीत्यपि चेद्ध्वस्ता कल्पकोट्युपबृंहिता ।
स्वल्पीयोऽभ्यासजास्थास्न्वी भावनेत्यत्र का प्रमा ॥ ९२॥
units.iast:
duḥkhasmītyapi ceddhvastā kalpakoṭyupabṛṃhitā |
svalpīyo'bhyāsajāsthāsnvī bhāvanetyatra kā pramā || 92||
units.translation: If the thought “I am suffering,” strengthened over millions of ages, were destroyed, what proof is there that a much weaker conviction born of practice would remain firm?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 306
units.translation: One might say that scripture will make that conviction firm. No:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 307
units.translation: scripture only produces understanding of the nature of an existing thing as it is.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 308
units.deva: न हि पदार्थशक्त्याधानकृच्छास्त्रम् । प्रसिद्धं च लोके ।
units.iast: na hi padārthaśaktyādhānakṛcchāstram | prasiddhaṃ ca loke |
units.translation: Scripture does not implant new powers in the things it describes. This is well known in ordinary life.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.93
units.deva:
भावनाजं फलं यत्स्याद्यच्च स्यात्कर्मणः फलम् ।
न तत्स्थास्न्विति मन्तव्यं द्रविडेष्विव सङ्गतम् ॥ ९३॥
units.iast:
bhāvanājaṃ phalaṃ yatsyādyacca syātkarmaṇaḥ phalam |
na tatsthāsnviti mantavyaṃ draviḍeṣviva saṅgatam || 93||
units.translation: Neither the result of contemplation nor the result of action should be considered lasting; the verse compares both to an association in Drāviḍa, proverbial here for its impermanence.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 311
units.translation: Even if suffering in the Self is presented by perception and the other means of knowledge,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 312
units.deva: तथापि तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्योत्थप्रत्यय एव बलीयानिति निश्चयोऽव्यभिचारिप्रामाण्यवाक्योपत्तत्वात्प्रमेयस्य च स्वत एव निर्दुःखित्वसिद्धेः । प्रत्यक्षादेस्तु व्यभिचारित्वात्संभावनायाश्च पुरुषपरिकल्पनामात्रावष्टम्भत्वाच्चेति ।
units.iast: tathāpi tattvamasyādivākyotthapratyaya eva balīyāniti niścayo'vyabhicāriprāmāṇyavākyopattatvātprameyasya ca svata eva nirduḥkhitvasiddheḥ | pratyakṣādestu vyabhicāritvātsaṃbhāvanāyāśca puruṣaparikalpanāmātrāvaṣṭambhatvācceti |
units.translation: the conviction born from “you are that” is stronger: it arises from a sentence whose authority never fails, while the knowable Self is by its own nature free from suffering. Perception can err, and the appearance it supports rests only on a person’s imagination.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.94
units.deva:
निर्दुःखित्वं स्वतस्सिद्धं प्रत्यक्षादेश्च दुःखिता ।
को ह्यात्मानमनादृत्य विश्वसेद्बाह्यमानतः ॥ ९४॥
units.iast:
nirduḥkhitvaṃ svatassiddhaṃ pratyakṣādeśca duḥkhitā |
ko hyātmānamanādṛtya viśvasedbāhyamānataḥ || 94||
units.translation: Freedom from suffering is established by the Self itself, while perception and the other means report suffering. Who would disregard the Self and trust an external means of knowledge?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 315
units.translation: This is said only to explain the connection [between the passage and its context].

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.95
units.deva:
अपि प्रत्यक्षबाधेन प्रवृत्तिः प्रत्यगात्मनि ।
"पराञ्चि खानि" त्येतस्माद्वचसो गम्यते श्रुतेः ॥ ९५॥
units.iast:
api pratyakṣabādhena pravṛttiḥ pratyagātmani |
"parāñci khāni" tyetasmādvacaso gamyate śruteḥ || 95||
units.translation: Even when one must overcome perception’s outward pull, one turns toward the inward Self; scripture teaches this in the statement “the sense openings face outward.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 318
units.deva: अभ्युपगम्यैवमुच्यते न तु प्रमाणं सत्प्रमाणान्तरेण विरुध्यत इत्यसकृदवोचाम । यत्रापि वाक्यप्रत्यक्षयोर्विरोधाशङ्का तत्रापि पुरुषमोहवशादेव सा जायते न तु परमार्थत इति ।
units.iast: abhyupagamyaivamucyate na tu pramāṇaṃ satpramāṇāntareṇa virudhyata ityasakṛdavocāma | yatrāpi vākyapratyakṣayorvirodhāśaṅkā tatrāpi puruṣamohavaśādeva sā jāyate na tu paramārthata iti |
units.translation: This is said only for the sake of argument; we have repeatedly explained that one valid means of knowledge does not truly conflict with another. Even where a conflict between a scriptural sentence and perception is suspected, it arises only from a person’s delusion, not in reality.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 319
units.translation: Therefore the author says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.96
units.deva:
प्रमां चेज्जनयेद्वाक्यं प्रत्यक्षादिविरोधिनीम् ।
गौणीं प्रत्यक्षतां ब्रूयान्मुख्यार्थासंभवाद्बुधः ॥ ९६॥
units.iast:
pramāṃ cejjanayedvākyaṃ pratyakṣādivirodhinīm |
gauṇīṃ pratyakṣatāṃ brūyānmukhyārthāsaṃbhavādbudhaḥ || 96||
units.translation: If a sentence produced valid knowledge contrary to perception and the other means, the wise would treat that perception as figurative, since its literal meaning cannot stand.

gloss.en: contrary to perception and the rest
because the literal meaning is impossible

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 322
units.translation: An example is given to make this point easier to grasp:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.97
units.deva:
अग्निस्सम्यगधीतेऽसौ जहासोच्चैश्च मञ्चकः ।
यथा तद्वदहंवृत्त्या लक्ष्यतेऽनर्हयापि सः ॥ ९७॥
units.iast:
agnissamyagadhīte'sau jahāsoccaiśca mañcakaḥ |
yathā tadvadahaṃvṛttyā lakṣyate'narhayāpi saḥ || 97||
units.translation: Just as people say figuratively “the fire recites well” or “the platform laughed aloud,” the Self is indicated, though imperfectly, by the “I”-thought.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 325
units.deva: कस्मात्पुनः कारणात्साक्षादेवात्मा नाभिधीयते किमनया कल्पनयेति तत्राह ।
units.iast: kasmātpunaḥ kāraṇātsākṣādevātmā nābhidhīyate kimanayā kalpanayeti tatrāha |
units.translation: Why is the Self not stated directly, without this imagined device? The author explains:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.98
units.deva:
त्वमित्यतद्विहायान्यन्न वर्तात्मावबोधते ।
समस्तीह त्वमर्थोऽपि गुणलेशेन वर्तते ॥ ९८॥
units.iast:
tvamityatadvihāyānyanna vartātmāvabodhate |
samastīha tvamartho'pi guṇaleśena vartate || 98||
units.translation: Apart from the word “thou,” there is no other way here to know the Self; even the meaning of “thou” operates only through a trace of an attribute.

gloss.en: through a trace of an attribute

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 328
units.deva: कस्मात्पुनर्हेतोर्ह्यहमित्येतदपि गुणलेशेन वर्तते न पुनः साक्षादेवेति । विधूतसर्वकल्पनाकारणस्वाभाव्यादात्मनः अत आह ।
units.iast: kasmātpunarhetorhyahamityetadapi guṇaleśena vartate na punaḥ sākṣādeveti | vidhūtasarvakalpanākāraṇasvābhāvyādātmanaḥ ata āha |
units.translation: Why does the word “I” also operate only through a trace of attributes, rather than directly? Because the Self is naturally free of every imagined distinction. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.99
units.deva:
व्योम्नि धूमतुषाराभ्रमलिनानीव दुर्धियः ।
कल्पयेयुस्तथा मूढाः संसारं प्रत्यगात्मनि ॥ ९९॥
units.iast:
vyomni dhūmatuṣārābhramalinānīva durdhiyaḥ |
kalpayeyustathā mūḍhāḥ saṃsāraṃ pratyagātmani || 99||
units.translation: Just as foolish people imagine smoke, mist, and clouds to stain the sky, the deluded imagine the cycle of worldly bondage in the inward Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 331
units.deva: ननु सर्वकल्पनानामप्यात्मन्यत्यन्तासंभवे समानेऽहंवृत्तौ कः पक्षपाते हेतुर्येन वृत्त्यन्तराणि विधूयाहंवृत्त्यैवात्मोपलक्ष्यत इति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: nanu sarvakalpanānāmapyātmanyatyantāsaṃbhave samāne'haṃvṛttau kaḥ pakṣapāte heturyena vṛttyantarāṇi vidhūyāhaṃvṛttyaivātmopalakṣyata iti | ucyate |
units.translation: One might object: “All imagined forms are equally impossible in the Self. Why favor the ‘I’-thought and use it to indicate the Self after setting aside every other thought?” The answer is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.100
units.translation: The “I”-thought resembles awareness and, like the inward Self, lies deeper than other thoughts. For these and the reasons already given, the Self is indicated by this “I”-thought.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.101
units.deva:
वृत्तिभिर्युष्मदर्थाभिर्लक्ष्यते चेद्दृशिः परः ।
अनात्मत्वं भवेत्तस्य वितथं च वचः श्रुतेः ॥ १०१॥
units.iast:
vṛttibhiryuṣmadarthābhirlakṣyate ceddṛśiḥ paraḥ |
anātmatvaṃ bhavettasya vitathaṃ ca vacaḥ śruteḥ || 101||
units.translation: If the supreme Witness were indicated through thoughts whose meanings are objects, it would become not-Self, and scripture’s teaching would be false.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 336
units.translation: As explained:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.102
units.translation: By this slight common quality, the Self is indicated by the “I”-thought, though it is not directly named here.

gloss.en: by a slight trace of a quality
by the “I”-thought, which takes the ego as its object

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 339
units.translation: If asked why it is not stated directly:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.103
units.translation: Words denote through relation, quality, action, class, or convention. None of these applies to the Self, so it cannot be directly named.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 342
units.deva: यदि शब्दोऽभिधानाभिधेयत्वसंबन्धाङ्गीकारेण नात्मनि वर्तते कथं शब्दादहं ब्रह्मास्मीति सम्यग्बोधोत्पत्तिः ।
units.iast: yadi śabdo'bhidhānābhidheyatvasaṃbandhāṅgīkāreṇa nātmani vartate kathaṃ śabdādahaṃ brahmāsmīti samyagbodhotpattiḥ |
units.translation: If words do not apply to the Self through a relation between word and denoted thing, how can the sentence “I am Brahman” produce correct knowledge?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 343
units.translation: The reply is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.104
units.deva:
असत्ये वर्त्मनि स्थित्वा निरुपायमुपेयते ।
आत्मत्वकारणाद्विद्मो गुणवृत्त्या विबोधिताः ॥ १०४॥
units.iast:
asatye vartmani sthitvā nirupāyamupeyate |
ātmatvakāraṇādvidmo guṇavṛttyā vibodhitāḥ || 104||
units.translation: A path that is not ultimately real can lead to what has no other means of access. Awakened through a mere suggestion of a quality, we know the Self because it is our own Self.

gloss.en: in what is not ultimately real
through an indirect suggestion of a quality

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 346
units.deva: कथं पुनरभिधानमभिधेयेनानभिसंबद्धं सदनभिधेयेऽर्थे प्रमां जनयतीति । शृणु यथानभिसंबद्धमप्यनभिधे येऽर्थेऽविद्यानिराकरणमुखेन बोधयतीत्याह ।
units.iast: kathaṃ punarabhidhānamabhidheyenānabhisaṃbaddhaṃ sadanabhidheye'rthe pramāṃ janayatīti | śṛṇu yathānabhisaṃbaddhamapyanabhidhe ye'rthe'vidyānirākaraṇamukhena bodhayatītyāha |
units.translation: How can a word, unconnected with what it denotes, produce knowledge of something that cannot be denoted? Listen: though it is unconnected, it awakens knowledge by removing ignorance, as the following verse says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.105
units.deva:
शयानाः प्रायशो लोके बोध्यमानाः स्वनामभिः ।
सहसैव प्रबुध्यन्ते यथैवं प्रत्यगात्मनि ॥ १०५॥
units.iast:
śayānāḥ prāyaśo loke bodhyamānāḥ svanāmabhiḥ |
sahasaiva prabudhyante yathaivaṃ pratyagātmani || 105||
units.translation: People in ordinary life, when called by their own names while asleep, awaken at once; the same is true of the inward Self.

gloss.en: with regard to the inward Self

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.106
units.deva:
न हि नाम्नास्ति संबन्धो व्युत्थितस्य शरीरतः ।
तथापि बुध्यते तेन यथैवं तत्त्वमित्यतः ॥ १०६॥
units.iast:
na hi nāmnāsti saṃbandho vyutthitasya śarīrataḥ |
tathāpi budhyate tena yathaivaṃ tattvamityataḥ || 106||
units.translation: A name has no direct relation to the body of the person who has awakened, yet it awakens him. Likewise, the words “That thou art” awaken understanding.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 351
units.translation: And again:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.107
units.deva:
बोधाबोधौ नभोऽस्पृष्ट्वा कृष्णधीनीडगौ यथा ।
बाध्येतरात्मकौ स्यातां तथेहात्मनि गम्यताम् ॥ १०७॥
units.iast:
bodhābodhau nabho'spṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇadhīnīḍagau yathā |
bādhyetarātmakau syātāṃ tathehātmani gamyatām || 107||
units.translation: Knowledge and ignorance arise in a darkened mind without touching space; understand that, in the same way, one of these is sublated by the other in the Self, without affecting the Self.

gloss.en: dwelling in the nest of a darkened mind
having the nature of what is sublated and what sublates

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 354
units.deva: "असत्ये वर्त्मनि स्थित्वा" इत्युपश्रुत्यातिविस्मितो महता संभ्रमेण कश्चिच्चोदयति ।
units.iast: "asatye vartmani sthitvā" ityupaśrutyātivismito mahatā saṃbhrameṇa kaściccodayati |
units.translation: Hearing the words “one reaches the goal by taking an unreal path,” someone, greatly astonished, objects:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.108
units.deva:
नासन्नुपायो लोकेऽस्ति परमार्थविनिश्चये ।
नासल्लिङ्गाद्धि बाष्पदेः कश्चिदग्निं प्रपद्यते ॥ १०८॥
units.iast:
nāsannupāyo loke'sti paramārthaviniścaye |
nāsalliṅgāddhi bāṣpadeḥ kaścidagniṃ prapadyate || 108||
units.translation: In ordinary life, an unreal means cannot establish what is ultimately real; no one concludes that there is fire from a false sign such as mist.

gloss.en: for determining what is ultimately real

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.109
units.deva:
इत्येवं चोदयेद्योऽपि जोषयेत्तं घटादिना ।
सदसद्भ्यां विभक्तोऽसौ पर्यायश्च न चानयोः ॥ १०९॥
units.iast:
ityevaṃ codayedyo'pi joṣayettaṃ ghaṭādinā |
sadasadbhyāṃ vibhakto'sau paryāyaśca na cānayoḥ || 109||
units.translation: Answer anyone who objects this way with the example of a pot: it is distinct from both existence and nonexistence, and does not alternate between them.

gloss.en: with a pot and the like

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 359
units.translation: Having uprooted this mistaken objection, the author returns to the main point:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 360
units.deva: प्रकृतं चानभिधेये कथमभिधाश्रुतिरविद्याध्वंस्यात्मनि ज्ञानं जनयतीति । तत्रैव कारणान्तरमुच्यते ।
units.iast: prakṛtaṃ cānabhidheye kathamabhidhāśrutiravidyādhvaṃsyātmani jñānaṃ janayatīti | tatraiva kāraṇāntaramucyate |
units.translation: The question at hand is how a scriptural statement can produce knowledge of the Self, which cannot be denoted and which destroys ignorance. Another reason is now given.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.110
units.deva:
अतिदुस्स्थोऽप्रबोधोऽत्र ह्यात्मैवास्य प्रबुद्धता ।
निमित्तमात्राद्व्येत्येषा नासाग्रे बदरं यथा ॥ ११०॥
units.iast:
atidusstho'prabodho'tra hyātmaivāsya prabuddhatā |
nimittamātrādvyety eṣā nāsāgre badaraṃ yathā || 110||
units.translation: Ignorance is precariously established: the Self itself is its awakening. It departs at the slightest occasion, like a berry balanced on the tip of the nose.

gloss.en: at the tip of the nose

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 363
units.deva: अनुदितानस्तमितकूटस्थबोधमात्रस्वाभाव्यादात्मनो दुस्संभाव्योऽविद्यासद्भाव इति चेन्न । अविद्याप्रसिद्ध्यैव तत्सद्भावसिद्धेरुलूकनिशावदित्यत इदमुच्यते ।
units.iast: anuditānastamitakūṭasthabodhamātrasvābhāvyādātmano dussaṃbhāvyo'vidyāsadbhāva iti cenna | avidyāprasiddhyaiva tatsadbhāvasiddherulūkaniśāvadityata idamucyate |
units.translation: One might say that ignorance is hard to conceive when the Self is changeless, pure awareness, neither arising nor setting. This is no objection: ignorance is established by ordinary experience, just as an owl’s night is established. Hence the verse:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.111
units.deva:
अहो धार्ष्ट्यमविद्याया न कश्चिदतिवर्तते ।
प्रमाणं वस्त्वनादृत्य परमात्मेव तिष्ठति ॥ १११॥
units.iast:
aho dhārṣṭyamavidyāyā na kaścidativartate |
pramāṇaṃ vastvanādṛtya paramātmeva tiṣṭhati || 111||
units.translation: How brazen ignorance is—no one outdoes it! Disregarding reality and valid means of knowledge, it stands as though it were the Supreme Self.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 366
units.translation: Since ignorance is established only through ordinary experience, and cannot be supposed in keeping with the reality of the Self, the author says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.112
units.deva:
ज्ञानं यस्य निजं रूपं क्रियाकारकवर्जितम् ।
संभावनाप्यविद्यायास्तत्र स्यात्केन हेतुना ॥ ११२॥
units.iast:
jñānaṃ yasya nijaṃ rūpaṃ kriyākārakavarjitam |
saṃbhāvanāpyavidyāyāstatra syātkena hetunā || 112||
units.translation: For the one whose own nature is knowledge, free from action and its factors, by what reason could ignorance even be conceived?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 369
units.translation: Though the Self is awareness alone, without arising or setting, it is nevertheless seen otherwise, screened by ignorance accepted without examination. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.113
units.deva:
अनुमानादयं भावाव्द्यावृत्तोऽभावमाश्रितः ।
ततोऽप्यस्य निवृत्तिः स्याद्वाक्यादेव बुभुत्सतः ॥ ११३॥
units.iast:
anumānādayaṃ bhāvāvdyāvṛtto'bhāvamāśritaḥ |
tato'pyasya nivṛttiḥ syādvākyādeva bubhutsataḥ || 113||
units.translation: Inference sets this Self apart from what exists empirically and so places it in nonexistence; for the seeker, only the sentence removes this mistaken conclusion.

gloss.en: for one who seeks to know

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.114
units.iast: na vyāvṛttiryathā bhāvād bhāvenaivāviśeṣataḥ | abhāvādapyabhāvatvādvyāvṛttirna tatheṣyate || 114||
units.translation: Just as one existent thing is not distinguished from another by existence alone, so an exclusion is not accepted merely because something is non-existent.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 372
units.deva: भाववदभावादपि निवृत्तिरनुमानादेव किमिति न भवतीति चेच्छृणु ।
units.iast: bhāvavadabhāvādapi nivṛttiranumānādeva kimiti na bhavatīti cecchṛṇu |
units.translation: If asked why inference cannot remove nonexistence just as it removes what exists, listen:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 373
units.deva: यतो नानुमानेन व्याविद्धाशेषक्रियाकारकफलात्मनि स्वाराज्येऽभिषेक्तुं शक्यते तस्मात् ।
units.iast: yato nānumānena vyāviddhāśeṣakriyākārakaphalātmani svārājye'bhiṣektuṃ śakyate tasmāt |
units.translation: Inference cannot enthrone one in the sovereignty free from all actions, agents, instruments and results. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.115
units.deva:
अविद्यानिद्रया सोऽयं प्रसुप्तो दुर्विवेकया ।
भावाभावव्युदासिन्या श्रुत्यैव प्रतिबोध्यते ॥ ११५॥
units.iast:
avidyānidrayā so'yaṃ prasupto durvivekayā |
bhāvābhāvavyudāsinyā śrutyaiva pratibodhyate || 115||
units.translation: This person, asleep in the hard-to-discriminate sleep of ignorance, is awakened only by scripture, which sets aside both existence and nonexistence.

gloss.en: hard to discern; resistant to discrimination
which excludes both existence and nonexistence

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 376
units.translation: Someone objects: “Ignorance is hard to conceive because the Self is awareness alone, without arising or setting.” This is not so. Why? The verse says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.116
units.deva:
कुतो अविद्येति चोद्यं स्यान्नैव प्राग्घेत्वसंभवात् ।
कालत्रयापरिच्छित्तेर्न चोर्ध्वं चोद्यसंभवः ॥ ११६॥
units.iast:
kuto avidyeti codyaṃ syānnaiva prāgghetvasaṃbhavāt |
kālatrayāparicchitterna cordhvaṃ codyasaṃbhavaḥ || 116||
units.translation: The question “Where did ignorance come from?” is out of place both before and after realization: before, its cause cannot be established; afterward, ignorance is no longer present in any of the three times.

gloss.en: because it is not delimited by the three times

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 379
units.translation: Because a sentence such as “you are that” alone removes every trace of ignorance about the Self:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.117
units.deva:
अद्धातममनादृत्य प्रमाणं सदसीति ये ।
बुभुत्सन्तेऽन्यतः कुर्युस्तेऽक्ष्णापि रसवेदनम् ॥ ११७॥
units.iast:
addhātamamanādṛtya pramāṇaṃ sadasīti ye |
bubhutsante'nyataḥ kuryuste'kṣṇāpi rasavedanam || 117||
units.translation: Those who disregard the truest means of knowledge, the teaching “You are Being,” and seek to know by other means might as well try to taste flavor with their eyes.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 382
units.deva: एवमप्रतिहतामहं ब्रह्मेति प्रमां तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यं कुर्वदपि न प्रतिपादयतीति चेदभिमतं न कुतश्चनापि प्रतिपत्तिः स्यादत आह ।
units.iast: evamapratihatāmahaṃ brahmeti pramāṃ tattvamasyādivākyaṃ kurvadapi na pratipādayatīti cedabhimataṃ na kutaścanāpi pratipattiḥ syādata āha |
units.translation: If one says that even though the sentence “I am Brahman” produces unobstructed valid knowledge, it does not actually teach it, then nothing could ever be understood. Therefore:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.118
units.deva:
इदं चेदनृतं ब्रूयात्सत्यामवगतावपि ।
न चान्यत्रापि विश्वासो ह्यवगत्यविशेषतः ॥ ११८॥
units.iast:
idaṃ cedanṛtaṃ brūyātsatyāmavagatāvapi |
na cānyatrāpi viśvāso hyavagatyaviśeṣataḥ || 118||
units.translation: If this statement were false even when knowledge had arisen, there would be no reason to trust another source either, since each is alike in producing knowledge.

gloss.en: because there is no difference in the arising of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 385
units.translation: It is not reasonable to invent a different meaning for the sentence than the one intended. For:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.119
units.deva:
न चेदनुभवोऽतः स्यात्पदार्थावगतावपि ।
कल्प्यं विध्यन्तरं तत्र न ह्यन्योऽर्थोऽवगम्यते ॥ ११९॥
units.iast:
na cedanubhavo'taḥ syātpadārthāvagatāvapi |
kalpyaṃ vidhyantaraṃ tatra na hyanyo'rtho'vagamyate || 119||
units.translation: If no experience arose even after the word-meanings were understood, one would have to invent a separate injunction; no other meaning is actually understood here.

gloss.en: when the meanings of the words are understood

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 388
units.deva: न च यथाभिमतोऽर्थो यथोक्तेन न्यायेन नावसीयते ।
units.iast: na ca yathābhimato'rtho yathoktena nyāyena nāvasīyate |
units.translation: Nor is the intended meaning impossible to determine by the reasoning already explained.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 389
units.translation: The author states that reasoning:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.120
units.deva:
नामादिभ्यो निराकृत्य त्वमर्थं निष्परिग्रहः ।
निस्स्पृहो युष्मदर्थेभ्यः शमादिविधिचोदितः ॥ १२०॥
units.iast:
nāmādibhyo nirākṛtya tvamarthaṃ niṣparigrahaḥ |
nisspṛho yuṣmadarthebhyaḥ śamādividhicoditaḥ || 120||
units.translation: Having set aside names and the rest from the meaning of “thou,” one is free of possessiveness and desire for objects, guided by disciplines such as calm.

gloss.en: guided by disciplines such as calm

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 392
units.translation: “Breaking through the five sheaths, beginning with the food-made body, as barriers that are not-Self,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.121
units.deva: अहं ब्रह्मेति वाक्यार्थं वेत्ति चेन्नार्थ ईहया ॥ १२१॥
units.iast: ahaṃ brahmeti vākyārthaṃ vetti cennārtha īhayā || 121||
units.translation: one understands the sentence meaning ‘I am Brahman’ without further striving.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 394
units.deva: न चेदेवमुपगम्यते वाक्यस्य प्रमाणस्य सतोऽप्रामाण्यं प्राप्नोति । तदाह ।
units.iast: na cedevamupagamyate vākyasya pramāṇasya sato'prāmāṇyaṃ prāpnoti | tadāha |
units.translation: If this is not accepted, a sentence that is in fact a valid means of knowledge would be declared invalid. The author says:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 395
units.deva: यदर्थं च प्रवृत्तं यद्वाक्यं तत्र न चेच्छ्रुतम् ।
units.iast: yadarthaṃ ca pravṛttaṃ yadvākyaṃ tatra na cecchrutam |
units.translation: “If the sentence is heard but does not produce valid knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.122
units.translation: of the very matter for which it was spoken, on what grounds is it a valid means of knowledge?”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 397
units.translation: Suppose you think:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.123
units.deva: जानीयाच्चेत्प्रसंख्यानाच्छब्दस्सत्यवचाः कथम् । पारोक्ष्यं शब्दो नः प्राह प्रसंख्यानात्त्वसंशयम् ॥ १२३॥
units.iast: jānīyāccetprasaṃkhyānācchabdassatyavacāḥ katham | pārokṣyaṃ śabdo naḥ prāha prasaṃkhyānāttvasaṃśayam || 123||
units.translation: If repeated contemplation gives knowledge, how are the words themselves truthful? The words tell us [the Self is] indirect; through contemplation, [it becomes known] without doubt.

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 401
units.translation: We cannot suppose that correct understanding will arise from contemplation consisting of repeatedly turning over the reasoning and the words. For:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 402
units.translation: “If the words and reasoning did not produce valid knowledge before,

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.124
units.translation: what new result will come from simply repeating them inwardly?”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 404
units.deva: अथैवमपि प्रसंख्यानमन्तरेण प्राणान्धारयितुं न शक्नोषीति चेच्छ्रवणादावेव संपादयिष्यामः । कथम् ।
units.iast: athaivamapi prasaṃkhyānamantareṇa prāṇāndhārayituṃ na śaknoṣīti cecchravaṇādāveva saṃpādayiṣyāmaḥ | katham |
units.translation: If you say that without such contemplation you cannot even sustain life, we will provide for it during listening itself. How?

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 405
units.translation: “The same principle of repetition used in contemplation can be applied to hearing:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.125
units.translation: what was heard only faintly or in part is understood when heard properly.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 407
units.deva: ननु प्रसंख्यानविधिमनभ्युपगच्छतः पारमहंसी चर्या बौद्धादिचर्यावदशास्त्रपूर्विका प्राप्नोति ततश्चारूढपतितत्वं न स्यादशेषकर्मणां च निवृत्तिर्न प्राप्नोतीति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: nanu prasaṃkhyānavidhimanabhyupagacchataḥ pāramahaṃsī caryā bauddhādicaryāvadaśāstrapūrvikā prāpnoti tataścārūḍhapatitatvaṃ na syādaśeṣakarmaṇāṃ ca nivṛttirna prāpnotīti | ucyate |
units.translation: An objection: “If you reject an injunction to repeated contemplation, the highest renunciant’s way of life will be unscriptural, like the practices of Buddhists and others. Then there can be no ‘fallen’ person who has attained the path, and the cessation of all action cannot follow.” The answer is:

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Text 408
units.translation: “An injunction has also been accepted for understanding the meaning of ‘thou’;

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Verse 3.126
units.translation: without it, those faults would not arise either, since they have no basis.”

units.sectionTitle: Adhyāya 3 — The nature of the Self
units.label: Chapter colophon
units.translation: [End of the third chapter.]

units.label: Chapter heading
units.translation: Now begins the fourth chapter.

units.label: Text 2
units.translation: “What was explained clearly and at length in the earlier chapters,

units.label: Verse 4.1
units.translation: I will now state in brief, for the understanding of those who seek ease.”

units.label: Text 4
units.translation: “When a subject is taught briefly and at length, people of lesser and greater understanding

units.label: Verse 4.2
units.translation: take it into the mind; for that reason it is taught in both ways.”

units.label: Text 6
units.translation: “In this world, the Self and not-Self are established through perception and other means of knowledge;

units.label: Verse 4.3
units.translation: yet everywhere the not-Self depends on the Self as its ground.”

units.label: Text 8
units.translation: “The not-Selfhood of what is distinct from the body is self-evident;

units.label: Verse 4.4
units.translation: the knower too is taken to be the Self, but doubt arises between them.”

units.label: Text 10
units.translation: “Having learned their distinctive properties, the wise person reasons from them, as from smoke to fire,

units.label: Verse 4.5
units.translation: and thus recognizes the body, intellect and the rest as not-Self.”

units.label: Text 12
units.translation: “For external objects there is the thought ‘this’; for the knower, the thought ‘I.’

units.label: Verse 4.6
units.deva: द्वयं दृष्टं यतो देहे तेनायं मुह्यते जनः ॥ ६॥
units.iast: dvayaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ yato dehe tenāyaṃ muhyate janaḥ || 6||
units.translation: Since both are seen in the body, people are confused.”

units.label: Text 14
units.deva: केन पुनर्न्यायेनात्मानात्मनोरश्वमहिषयोरिव विभागः क्रियत इति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: kena punarnyāyenātmānātmanoraśvamahiṣayoriva vibhāgaḥ kriyata iti | ucyate |
units.translation: By what reasoning can the Self be distinguished from the not-Self, as a horse from a buffalo? The answer:

units.label: Text 15
units.translation: “We have already explained the reasoning that distinguishes Self from not-Self.

units.label: Verse 4.7
units.translation: Using it, one should set aside the meaning of ‘this’; whatever remains as ‘I’

units.label: Text 17
units.translation: one should know from ‘you are that’ as the ever-present witness of being and nonbeing,

units.label: Verse 4.8
units.translation: immediately inward and not an external object, O sage.”

units.label: Text 19
units.deva: उच्यतां तर्हि कया तु परिपाय्या वाक्यार्थं वेत्तीति ।
units.iast: ucyatāṃ tarhi kayā tu paripāyyā vākyārthaṃ vettīti |
units.translation: Then by what method does one understand the sentence meaning?

units.label: Text 20
units.translation: The answer: through agreement and difference.

units.label: Text 21
units.translation: “Having given up the entire meaning of ‘this,’ one thinks, ‘I too have been given up’,

units.label: Verse 4.9
units.translation: because I do not know my own Self as distinct from the not-Self.”

units.label: Text 23
units.deva: अथ शरीरादिबुद्धिपर्यन्तः स सर्वोऽनात्मैवेति प्रमाणाद्विनिश्चित्य किमिति बुभुत्सातो नोपरमते । शृणु ।
units.iast: atha śarīrādibuddhiparyantaḥ sa sarvo'nātmaiveti pramāṇādviniścitya kimiti bubhutsāto noparamate | śṛṇu |
units.translation: If, on the evidence, one has determined that everything from the body through the intellect is not-Self, why does the desire to know not cease? Listen:

units.label: Text 24
units.translation: “The desire to know remains unended because the cause of inwardness is not yet understood;

units.label: Verse 4.10
units.translation: the person’s mind wavers and is deluded, like one made of the elements.”

units.label: Text 26
units.deva: अविलुप्तविज्ञानात्मन आत्मत्वादेव नित्यसान्निध्याद्बुभुत्सुः किमिति न प्रतिपद्यत इति। यस्मात् ।
units.iast: aviluptavijñānātmana ātmatvādeva nityasānnidhyādbubhutsuḥ kimiti na pratipadyata iti| yasmāt |
units.translation: Why does the seeker not recognize the Self, though awareness remains undiminished and is always present? Because:

units.label: Text 27
units.translation: “By the very means through which one formerly saw the Self, one now regards it as not-Self;

units.label: Verse 4.11
units.translation: one seeks to know, through familiar means of knowledge, the very Seer of seeing.”

units.label: Text 29
units.translation: Why does one not see the Self as one sees not-Self through outward-directed thoughts that savor sound and the rest? The answer:

units.label: Text 30
units.translation: “The eye does not see sound, because sound is not of its nature;

units.label: Verse 4.12
units.translation: in the same way, sight formed of the physical elements cannot fully see the Self.”

units.label: Text 32
units.translation: The reason it is not seen has so far been explained from the nature of perception and the other means of knowledge.

units.label: Text 33
units.translation: Now the denial is explained from the nature of the object of knowledge:

units.label: Text 34
units.translation: “The Self is the constant witness of thousands of changes in the intellect, which are taken up and set aside;

units.label: Verse 4.13
units.translation: because it is inward, the ‘I’-thought does not see it.”

units.label: Text 36
units.translation: Where does this discriminating understanding occur—in the Self or in the not-Self? And what follows from either answer?

units.label: Text 37
units.translation: If it occurs in the Self, seeing not-Self contradicts the Self’s changelessness;

units.label: Text 38
units.translation: if in the not-Self, that too is unconscious, so how could discrimination belong to it? The reply is:

units.label: Text 39
units.translation: As already resolved by the statement “burner and burned can be in one place,”

units.label: Text 40
units.translation: “this discrimination occurs in the intellect: it distinguishes the Self from what is not-Self.”

units.label: Verse 4.14
units.translation: “It acts on the intellect alone, as fruit is said to act on a banana plant.”

units.label: Text 42
units.translation: This is the one who sees truth in what is not true.

units.label: Text 43
units.translation: “Using the lamp of inference, he sets aside all that is not-Self;

units.label: Verse 4.15
units.translation: yet with a mind relying solely on worldly bondage, he seeks the absence of that bondage.”

units.label: Text 45
units.deva: योऽयमन्वयव्यतिरेकजो विवेक आत्मानात्मविभागलक्षणोऽनात्मस्थः स्थाणौ संशयावबोधवत् प्रतिपत्तव्योऽन्यथावस्तुस्वाभाव्यान्मृगतृष्णिकोदकप्रबोधववदित्यत आह ।
units.iast: yo'yamanvayavyatirekajo viveka ātmānātmavibhāgalakṣaṇo'nātmasthaḥ sthāṇau saṃśayāvabodhavat pratipattavyo'nyathāvastusvābhāvyānmṛgatṛṣṇikodakaprabodhavavadityata āha |
units.translation: The discrimination born from agreement and difference, which distinguishes Self from not-Self, occurs in the not-Self, like mistaking a post for a person. It must be understood otherwise, in keeping with the nature of the thing, as one recognizes water in a mirage. Therefore:

units.label: Text 46
units.translation: “Established in the very seed of bondage, this person seeks liberation through a thought born of it;

units.label: Verse 4.16
units.translation: like a hare, he hopes to escape death by closing his eyes.”

units.label: Text 48
units.translation: A scriptural example is offered to strengthen this point:

units.label: Text 49
units.translation: “With this meaning in view, scripture states it clearly,

units.label: Verse 4.17
units.translation: plainly saying ‘that which is before the eye’ and ‘not seen.’”

units.label: Text 51
units.translation: “Having set aside everything down to the intellect, one asks, ‘Who am I?’

units.label: Verse 4.18
units.translation: Scripture replies, ‘You are that,’ which goes beyond every means of knowledge.”

units.label: Text 53
units.translation: This is a brief statement of the meaning of the first three chapters.

units.label: Text 54
units.translation: Although this Vedānta teaching is reasonable and can be gained through the grace of scripture and teacher, some faithful people do not understand it, because its nature is self-established and depends on nothing else.

units.label: Text 55
units.translation: To gather their understanding, an example accepted as authoritative is offered:

units.label: Text 56
units.translation: “The revered teacher, who sought the welfare of all beings, also taught just this;

units.label: Verse 4.19
units.translation: in this way he made the point we have stated perfectly clear.”

units.label: Text 58
units.deva: किं परमात्मन उपदेश उतापरमात्मन इति । किं चातः ।
units.iast: kiṃ paramātmana upadeśa utāparamātmana iti | kiṃ cātaḥ |
units.translation: Is the teaching addressed to the Supreme Self or to the individual self? What follows?

units.label: Text 59
units.deva: यदि परमात्मनस्तस्योपदेशमन्तरेणैव मुक्तत्वान्निरर्थक उपदेशः । अथापरमात्मनस्तस्यापि स्वत एव संसारस्वभावत्वान्निष्फल उपदेशः । एवमुभयत्रापि दोषवत्त्वादत आह ।
units.iast: yadi paramātmanastasyopadeśamantareṇaiva muktatvānnirarthaka upadeśaḥ | athāparamātmanastasyāpi svata eva saṃsārasvabhāvatvānniṣphala upadeśaḥ | evamubhayatrāpi doṣavattvādata āha |
units.translation: If to the Supreme Self, the teaching is pointless because that Self is already free; if to the individual, the teaching is fruitless because that self is by nature bound. Since either view has a fault, the author says:

units.label: Text 60
units.translation: “If scripture spoke of the two without distinguishing them, it would be caught in that same confusion”

units.label: Verse 4.20
units.translation: —this position is taken up and refuted below.

units.label: Text 62
units.translation: In fact, “you are that” is taught to one who, through confusion, fails to distinguish the Self that is already distinct by nature.

units.label: Text 63
units.translation: “This statement is meaningful for one who knows the difference between ‘you’ and ‘I’;

units.label: Verse 4.21
units.translation: to one who does not know it, the words are like singing to the deaf.”

units.label: Text 65
units.deva: तस्य च युष्मदस्मद्विभागविज्ञानस्य का युक्तिरुपायभावं प्रतिपद्यते । शृणु ।
units.iast: tasya ca yuṣmadasmadvibhāgavijñānasya kā yuktirupāyabhāvaṃ pratipadyate | śṛṇu |
units.translation: What reasoning or method establishes knowledge of the distinction between ‘you’ and ‘I’? Listen:

units.label: Text 66
units.translation: “Agreement and difference are the reasoning for the meaning of a thing and of a word;

units.label: Verse 4.22
units.translation: here they alone establish what is meant by ‘I.’”

units.label: Text 68
units.translation: How are these two forms of reasoning applied? The author says:

units.label: Text 69
units.translation: “In deep sleep I did not see even the slightest thing other than this;

units.label: Verse 4.23
units.deva: न वारयति दृष्टिं स्वां प्रत्ययं तु निषेधति " ॥ २३॥
units.iast: na vārayati dṛṣṭiṃ svāṃ pratyayaṃ tu niṣedhati " || 23||
units.translation: this does not deny my own awareness, only the mental cognition.”

units.label: Text 71
units.translation: “When the word’s ordinary meaning has been understood from scripture and common usage,

units.label: Verse 4.24
units.translation: scripture says ‘you are that’ to remove the listener’s delusion.”

units.label: Text 73
units.deva: तत्र त्वमिति पदं यत्र लक्षणया वर्तते सोऽर्थ उच्यते ।
units.iast: tatra tvamiti padaṃ yatra lakṣaṇayā vartate so'rtha ucyate |
units.translation: Here the meaning expressed figuratively by the word “thou” is now stated:

units.label: Text 74
units.translation: “The essential meaning of the word ‘I’ is the light within, the innermost Self;

units.label: Verse 4.25
units.translation: that alone is stated as ‘you are real’; its fruit is liberation.”

units.label: Text 76
units.translation: Here is another example of reasoning by agreement and difference:

units.label: Text 77
units.translation: “A hand, once cut off and discarded, no longer serves to distinguish the person;

units.label: Verse 4.26
units.translation: in the same way, whatever remains after each [attribute] is set aside may be used to distinguish the Self.”

units.label: Text 79
units.translation: “All these attributes are like fine ornaments;

units.label: Verse 4.27
units.translation: once known as superimposed by ignorance, they are seen to be absent in the Self.”

units.label: Text 81
units.translation: “Every attribute is therefore like the discarded hand;

units.label: Verse 4.28
units.translation: knowing this, the wise are free of every attribute, since all are not-Self.”

units.label: Text 83
units.translation: “The knower alone is always to be recognized as the Self; the known is to be set aside.

units.label: Verse 4.29
units.translation: Whatever can be grasped as ‘I’ is like a limb that has been removed.”

units.label: Text 85
units.translation: “Because it is seen, the ‘I’-thought is not a property of the Self, like a pot;

units.label: Verse 4.30
units.translation: the other thoughts are likewise known, and their defects do not stain the Self, which is pure.”

units.label: Text 87
units.translation: This gathers together all the reasoning:

units.label: Text 88
units.translation: “Knowledge of being ever free arises from the sentence, not from anything else.

units.label: Verse 4.31
units.translation: Understanding the sentence meaning, too, is preceded by recalling the meanings of its words.

units.label: Text 90
units.translation: Through agreement and difference the meanings of the words are surely recalled;

units.label: Verse 4.32
units.translation: in this way one recognizes the sorrowless, actionless Self.”

units.label: Text 92
units.translation: “From sentences such as ‘Being alone was this,’ knowledge becomes especially clear,

units.label: Verse 4.33
units.translation: just as the sentence ‘You are the tenth’ does; so too regarding the inward Self.”

units.label: Text 94
units.translation: Here is an example of someone who has fallen into error:

units.label: Text 95
units.translation: “Having lost count by miscounting the nine, a person does not see himself as the tenth,

units.label: Verse 4.34
units.translation: and yet longs to know his own self, which completes the ten.”

units.label: Text 97
units.translation: “With sight blinded by ignorance and understanding stolen by desire,

units.label: Verse 4.35
units.translation: he does not see the distinct witnessing Self, just as the man fails to see that he is the tenth.”

units.label: Text 99
units.translation: How, then, is this person, whose vision is veiled by ignorance, awakened? The author says:

units.label: Text 100
units.translation: “Just as a dreamer is awakened by the cause of waking,

units.label: Verse 4.36
units.deva: करणं कर्म कर्तारं स्वाप्नं नैवेक्षते स्वतः ॥ ३६॥
units.iast: karaṇaṃ karma kartāraṃ svāpnaṃ naivekṣate svataḥ || 36||
units.translation: and then sees none of the dream’s instruments, actions or agents as real,”

units.label: Text 102
units.translation: “so the one who does not know the Self is rightly awakened by scripture;

units.label: Verse 4.37
units.deva: गुरुं शास्त्रं तथा मूढं स्वात्मनोऽन्यं न पश्यति ॥ ३७॥
units.iast: guruṃ śāstraṃ tathā mūḍhaṃ svātmano'nyaṃ na paśyati || 37||
units.translation: the deluded person then sees neither teacher nor scripture as other than his own Self.”

units.label: Text 104
units.deva: स किं सकलसंसारप्रविविक्तमात्मानं वाक्यात्प्रतिपद्यत उत नेतीति । अत्र ब्रूमः । कूटस्थावगतिशेषमात्रत्वात्प्रतिपत्तेरत आह ।
units.iast: sa kiṃ sakalasaṃsārapraviviktamātmānaṃ vākyātpratipadyata uta netīti | atra brūmaḥ | kūṭasthāvagatiśeṣamātratvātpratipatterata āha |
units.translation: Does the person, then, understand from the sentence a Self entirely separate from worldly existence, or not? We answer: recognition leaves only changeless awareness. Therefore:

units.label: Text 105
units.translation: “Just as a snake imagined on a staff resolves into the staff,

units.label: Verse 4.38
units.translation: so, without doubt, the whole world resolves into ever-present awareness through the sentence.”

units.label: Text 107
units.translation: Why is this so? Because:

units.label: Text 108
units.translation: “The scripture that speaks clearly of seeing, of what is inward, unborn and undecaying,

units.label: Verse 4.39
units.translation: indicates you as without beginning, without end and boundless.”

units.label: Text 110
units.translation: Only the knowledge arising from a sentence such as “you are that” sublates the error. For:

units.label: Text 111
units.translation: “It teaches that no form other than this Self exists;

units.label: Verse 4.40
units.translation: misapprehension is the seed of both dream and waking.”

units.label: Text 113
units.translation: An example is given to strengthen this point:

units.label: Text 114
units.translation: “The waking person and the dreamer are held to effects and causes;

units.label: Verse 4.41
units.deva: प्राज्ञः कारणबद्धस्तु द्वौ तौ तुर्ये न सिध्यतः " ॥ ४१॥
units.iast: prājñaḥ kāraṇabaddhastu dvau tau turye na sidhyataḥ " || 41||
units.translation: the sleeper is held to causes, but neither is established in the Fourth.”

units.label: Text 116
units.translation: “Dream arises from misapprehension; sleep from not knowing reality.

units.label: Verse 4.42
units.translation: When both errors are ended, one attains the state called the Fourth.”

units.label: Text 118
units.translation: Here is another example from the revered teacher:

units.label: Verse 4.43
units.deva: सुषुप्ताख्यं तमोऽज्ञानं बीजं स्वप्नप्रबोधयोः । आत्मबोधप्रदग्धं स्याद्बीजं दग्धं यथाभवम् ॥ ४३॥
units.iast: suṣuptākhyaṃ tamo'jñānaṃ bījaṃ svapnaprabodhayoḥ | ātmabodhapradagdhaṃ syādbījaṃ dagdhaṃ yathābhavam || 43||
units.translation: The ignorance called deep sleep is the seed of dream and waking; burned by knowledge of the Self, it becomes like a scorched seed.

gloss.en: burned by knowledge of the Self
as it becomes; in that state

units.label: Text 122
units.translation: “In this way our revered teachers of Gauḍa and Drāviḍa have explained the point:

units.label: Verse 4.44
units.translation: the Lord, the Seer of ‘I’ and the rest, is conditioned only by ignorance.”

units.label: Text 124
units.translation: Just as the mistaken appearance has ignorance as its seed, so the failure to recognize the Self that seeds it belongs to the not-Self. The verse says:

units.label: Text 125
units.translation: “The triad ‘this is knowledge, I am the knower, this is what is known’—

units.label: Verse 4.45
units.translation: the changeless one who knows it is beyond that darkness.”

units.label: Text 127
units.deva: यत एतदेवमतस्तस्यैव बीजात्मनस्तमसश्चित्तधर्मविशिष्टस्य स्वकार्यद्वितीयाभिसंबन्धो न त्वविकारिण आत्मन इत्याह दृष्टान्तेन ।
units.iast: yata etadevamatastasyaiva bījātmanastamasaścittadharmaviśiṣṭasya svakāryadvitīyābhisaṃbandho na tvavikāriṇa ātmana ityāha dṛṣṭāntena |
units.translation: The seed-like darkness, which belongs to the mind, is connected with its changing effects and with what is other than the Self, not with the changeless Self. An example is given:

units.label: Text 128
units.translation: “As form is joined to the changing light that reveals it,

units.label: Verse 4.46
units.translation: so happiness, sorrow and the rest are joined to the changing mind.”

units.label: Text 130
units.translation: The author now shows this through agreement and difference:

units.label: Text 131
units.translation: “In deep repose, when what changes has subsided, because the Self is changeless,

units.label: Verse 4.47
units.translation: not even the slightest second thing touches the Seer.”

units.label: Text 133
units.translation: This is the Self, whose very nature is changeless awareness.

units.label: Text 134
units.translation: “As in deep sleep, so too at the ends of dream and waking:

units.label: Verse 4.48
units.translation: though it seems to see, because it is changeless it sees no second thing.”

units.label: Text 136
