units.translation: “For one who knows, there is no foothold for the thoughts ‘mine’ and ‘I’,

units.label: Verse 4.49
units.translation: just as darkness cannot remain before someone holding a shining lamp.”

units.label: Text 138
units.translation: Here is an example:

units.label: Text 139
units.translation: “Before waking, the existence of any object other than the dream is established only within that dream;

units.label: Verse 4.50
units.translation: with awakening, the intellect and the rest are likewise not established apart from the Self within.”

units.label: Text 141
units.translation: The wise person, seeing within the Self the Self that is free of taking up and laying down,

units.label: Text 142
units.translation: “accepts everything and denies everything;

units.label: Verse 4.51
units.translation: acceptance is the appearance of a separate form, while denial is knowing that it is not the Self’s nature.”

units.label: Text 144
units.translation: Everything has now been explained; the author concludes:

units.label: Text 145
units.translation: “I have set out the knowledge established by all Vedānta, resting on the highest truth,

units.label: Verse 4.52
units.translation: which removes the darkness from the understanding.”

units.label: Text 147
units.translation: This much has been taught here:

units.label: Text 148
units.translation: “There is no knower of the Self other than me, and no one ignorant apart from me.

units.label: Verse 4.53
units.translation: Whoever knows this without distinction is the highest knower of Brahman.”

units.label: Text 150
units.deva: एवमात्मानं ज्ञात्वा किं प्रवर्तितव्यमुत निवर्तितव्यमाहोस्विन्मुक्तप्रग्रहतेति । उच्यते ।
units.iast: evamātmānaṃ jñātvā kiṃ pravartitavyamuta nivartitavyamāhosvinmuktapragrahateti | ucyate |
units.translation: After knowing the Self in this way, should one act, refrain from acting, or have complete freedom to act? The answer is:

units.label: Text 151
units.translation: “Because this is not different from what is to be known, and follows the nature of the knowable,

units.label: Verse 4.54
units.deva: न प्रवृत्तिं निवृत्तिं वा कटाक्षेणापि वीक्षते ॥ ५४॥
units.iast: na pravṛttiṃ nivṛttiṃ vā kaṭākṣeṇāpi vīkṣate || 54||
units.translation: it does not even glance toward action or the cessation of action.”

units.label: Text 153
units.translation: Why is it not different from what is to be known? Because:

units.label: Text 154
units.translation: “Before knowing the Self, awareness takes external things as secondary;

units.label: Verse 4.55
units.translation: when all worldly bondage is destroyed, scriptural knowledge rests on the Self alone.”

units.label: Text 156
units.translation: One who has understood ultimate reality has no relation of dependent means to an end, since the cause of that relation has been removed. The verse says:

units.label: Text 157
units.translation: “Because true knowledge ends worldly becoming as it actually is,

units.label: Verse 4.56
units.translation: it does not undergo cessation any more than it undergoes action.”

units.label: Text 159
units.translation: “The very arising of knowledge of the Self, by itself, puts an end to all worldly becoming;

units.label: Verse 4.57
units.translation: by removing darkness alone, it leaves no further mistaken notion.”

units.label: Text 161
units.translation: “Because the Self is unrelated to place, time and the rest, which are effects of delusion,

units.label: Verse 4.58
units.translation: ignorance cannot be some separate thing that must first arise and then be burned away.”

units.label: Text 163
units.translation: “When the fire of right knowledge has once burned up delusion and all its effects,

units.label: Verse 4.59
units.translation: what further task remains for what has been sublated?”

units.label: Text 165
units.deva: वास्तवेनैव वृत्तेनाविद्यायाः प्रध्वस्तत्वान्न किंचिदवशिष्यत इत्युक्तः परिहारः । अथापरस्सांप्रदायिकः परिहारः ।
units.iast: vāstavenaiva vṛttenāvidyāyāḥ pradhvastatvānna kiṃcidavaśiṣyata ityuktaḥ parihāraḥ | athāparassāṃpradāyikaḥ parihāraḥ |
units.translation: This was the first reply: ignorance is destroyed as a real fact. Now comes another traditional reply:

units.label: Text 166
units.translation: “Even after the snake has disappeared, a person may still tremble from the snake he saw;

units.label: Verse 4.60
units.translation: so the knower of the Self may retain an effect of delusion, though all delusion is destroyed.”

units.label: Text 168
units.translation: Since the seed of action has been cut off:

units.label: Text 169
units.translation: “A tree whose root is torn out perishes by drying up;

units.label: Verse 4.61
units.translation: in the same way, for one who knows the truth of the Self, the body ends through withdrawal.”

units.label: Text 171
units.translation: The author now rejects the view that realization permits any conduct:

units.label: Text 172
units.translation: “If one who knows that duality is real may act as he pleases,

units.label: Verse 4.62
units.translation: what difference is there between the wise and dogs when they eat what is impure?”

units.label: Text 174
units.translation: Why should this not be allowed? Because:

units.label: Text 175
units.translation: “From unrighteousness comes ignorance, and from it comes heedless conduct;

units.label: Verse 4.63
units.translation: how could that be the result of virtue, when even virtue is not accepted?”

units.label: Text 177
units.translation: Rejecting heedless conduct, the Lord says:

units.label: Verse 4.64
units.translation: “The one whose every undertaking…” and “the one who sees the light…”—the all-seeing Lord [teaches this discipline].”

units.label: Text 179
units.deva: तिष्ठतु तावत्सर्वप्रवृत्तिबीजघस्मरं ज्ञानं मुमुक्ष्ववस्थायामपि न संभवति यथेष्टाचरणम् ।
units.iast: tiṣṭhatu tāvatsarvapravṛttibījaghasmaraṃ jñānaṃ mumukṣvavasthāyāmapi na saṃbhavati yatheṣṭācaraṇam |
units.translation: Set aside for now the liberated knower, whose knowledge consumes the seed of every action: even while one is still seeking liberation, heedless conduct is impossible.

units.label: Text 180
units.translation: The text says:

units.label: Text 181
units.deva: " यो हि यत्र विरक्तः स्यान्नासौ तस्मै प्रवर्तते ।
units.iast: " yo hi yatra viraktaḥ syānnāsau tasmai pravartate |
units.translation: “One who is dispassionate toward a thing does not pursue it;

units.label: Verse 4.65
units.translation: being dispassionate toward all three worlds, what would a seeker of liberation strive for here?”

units.label: Text 183
units.translation: An example is given:

units.label: Text 184
units.translation: “Even when tormented by hunger, a person does not wish to eat poison;

units.label: Verse 4.66
units.translation: one who knows that sweet food ends thirst, and is not deluded, longs for that.”

units.label: Text 186
units.deva: यतोऽवगतपरमार्थतत्त्वस्य यथेष्टाचरणं न मनागपि घटते मुमुक्षुत्वेऽपि च तस्मात् ।
units.iast: yato'vagataparamārthatattvasya yatheṣṭācaraṇaṃ na manāgapi ghaṭate mumukṣutve'pi ca tasmāt |
units.translation: Because heedless conduct cannot occur even slightly for one who knows ultimate reality, or even for one seeking liberation:

units.label: Text 187
units.translation: “Attachment is a sign of ignorance in the fields where the mind ranges;

units.label: Verse 4.67
units.deva: कुतः शाड्वलता तस्य यस्याग्निः कोटरे तरोः ॥ ६७॥
units.iast: kutaḥ śāḍvalatā tasya yasyāgniḥ koṭare taroḥ || 67||
units.translation: how could grass grow on a tree whose hollow is filled with fire?”

units.label: Text 189
units.translation: How does this knowledge of the Self, which fulfills every human aim, arise? The answer:

units.label: Text 190
units.translation: “Knowledge arises in one established in humility and the other virtues, and equipped with means such as freedom from hatred;

units.label: Verse 4.68
units.translation: it does not arise in a mind turned outward.”

units.label: Text 192
units.deva: उत्पन्न आत्मविज्ञाने किमविद्याकार्यत्वात्प्रवृत्तिवन्निवृत्त्यात्मकामानित्वदयो निवर्तन्त उत नेति । नेति ब्रूमः । किं कारणम् । निवृत्तिशास्त्राविरुद्धस्वाभाव्यात्परमात्मनो न तु नियोगवशात् । कथं तर्हि । शृणु ।
units.iast: utpanna ātmavijñāne kimavidyākāryatvātpravṛttivannivṛttyātmakāmānitvadayo nivartanta uta neti | neti brūmaḥ | kiṃ kāraṇam | nivṛttiśāstrāviruddhasvābhāvyātparamātmano na tu niyogavaśāt | kathaṃ tarhi | śṛṇu |
units.translation: When knowledge of the Self has arisen, do humility and the other qualities, which take the form of withdrawal, cease as effects of ignorance, like activity? We say no. Why? The Supreme Self naturally accords with the teaching of renunciation; these qualities do not arise from an injunction. How, then? Listen:

units.label: Text 193
units.translation: “For one awakened to the Self, qualities such as freedom from hatred

units.label: Verse 4.69
units.translation: arise effortlessly; they are not practices to be cultivated as means.”

units.label: Text 195
units.translation: Because this is so:

units.label: Text 196
units.translation: “One who wishes to study this treatise should diligently cultivate humility and the other means;

units.label: Verse 4.70
units.translation: one should not behave badly, for this teaching accords with the nature of the inward Self.”

units.label: Text 198
units.translation: This treatise must not be given to:

units.label: Text 199
units.translation: “One who is not dispassionate toward worldly existence, or who has not cast aside desire,

units.label: Verse 4.71
units.translation: or to one unfit to enter into the meaning of Vedānta.”

units.label: Text 201
units.translation: “One who has properly known what was taught has nothing further left to know;

units.label: Verse 4.72
units.translation: one should therefore not imagine this knowledge while action still remains unremoved.”

units.label: Text 203
units.translation: “Renunciants who have laid aside all action, whose minds are turned inward,

units.label: Verse 4.73
units.translation: desireless and peaceful, know this teaching as it has been set out.”

units.label: Text 205
units.deva: श्रीमच्छङ्करपादपद्मयुगलं संसेव्य लब्ध्वोचिवान् ज्ञानं पारमहंस्यमेतदमलं स्वान्तान्धकारापनुत् ।
units.iast: śrīmacchaṅkarapādapadmayugalaṃ saṃsevya labdhvocivān jñānaṃ pāramahaṃsyametadamalaṃ svāntāndhakārāpanut |
units.translation: “Having served the twin lotus feet of the blessed Śaṅkara, I received this pure knowledge of the highest renunciation, which removes the darkness of the heart.

units.label: Verse 4.74
units.deva: मा भूदत्र विरोधिनी मतिरतः सद्भिः परीक्ष्यं बुधैः सर्वत्रैव विशुद्धये मतमिदं सन्तः परं कारणम् ॥७४॥
units.iast: mā bhūdatra virodhinī matirataḥ sadbhiḥ parīkṣyaṃ budhaiḥ sarvatraiva viśuddhaye matamidaṃ santaḥ paraṃ kāraṇam ||74||
units.translation: Let no contrary view arise here; let wise and good people examine this teaching for the sake of purity everywhere. The good are its highest cause.”

units.label: Text 207
units.translation: “The sound teaching of great souls shines pure, like the sun to those who see by night;

units.label: Verse 4.75
units.translation: for minds made clear, it shines like a great treasure to one whose thirst has been quenched.”

units.label: Text 209
units.deva: विष्णोः पादानुगां यां निखिलभवनुदं शंकरोऽवापयोगात् सर्वज्ञं ब्रह्मसंस्थं मुनिगणसहितं सम्यगभ्यर्च्यभक्तया ।
units.iast: viṣṇoḥ pādānugāṃ yāṃ nikhilabhavanudaṃ śaṃkaro'vāpayogāt sarvajñaṃ brahmasaṃsthaṃ munigaṇasahitaṃ samyagabhyarcyabhaktayā |
units.translation: “Śaṅkara attained through yoga the knowledge that follows Viṣṇu’s path and removes all worldly becoming. I worshipped with devotion the all-knowing sage, established in Brahman, together with the company of sages.

units.label: Verse 4.76
units.deva: विद्यां गङ्गामिवाहं प्रवरगुणनिधेः प्राप्य वेदान्तदीप्तां कारुण्यात्तामवोचं जनिमृतिनिवहध्वस्तये दुःखितेभ्यः ॥ ७६॥
units.iast: vidyāṃ gaṅgāmivāhaṃ pravaraguṇanidheḥ prāpya vedāntadīptāṃ kāruṇyāttāmavocaṃ janimṛtinivahadhvastaye duḥkhitebhyaḥ || 76||
units.translation: Receiving from that treasure of excellent qualities the knowledge that flows like the Gaṅgā and illumines Vedānta, I have spoken it out of compassion for the suffering, to end the multitude of births and deaths.”

units.label: Text 211
units.deva: वेदान्तोदरवर्ति भास्वदमलं ध्वान्तच्छिदस्मद्धियो दिव्यं ज्ञानमतीद्रियेऽपिविषये व्याहन्यते न क्वचित् ।
units.iast: vedāntodaravarti bhāsvadamalaṃ dhvāntacchidasmaddhiyo divyaṃ jñānamatīdriye'piviṣaye vyāhanyate na kvacit |
units.translation: “This pure, radiant knowledge, dwelling in the heart of Vedānta and removing the darkness of our understanding, concerns a supersensible truth, yet is never obstructed.

units.label: Verse 4.77
units.deva: यो नो न्यायशलाकयैव निखिलं संसारबीजं तमः प्रोत्सार्याविरकार्षीद्गुरुगुरुः पूज्याय तस्मै नमः ॥ ७७॥
units.iast: yo no nyāyaśalākayaiva nikhilaṃ saṃsārabījaṃ tamaḥ protsāryāvirakārṣīdguruguruḥ pūjyāya tasmai namaḥ || 77||
units.translation: We bow to that revered teacher of teachers, who, solely through the rod of reasoning, drove away the darkness that is the seed of all worldly bondage and revealed the truth.”

units.label: Text 213
units.translation: “This account of the connections between the verses is skillfully given for each verse;

units.label: Verse 4.78
units.translation: one who knows it will surely have explained the Naiṣkarmyasiddhi correctly.”

units.label: Chapter colophon
units.translation: [End of the fourth chapter.]
